title: Federal Law On the Development of Artificial Intelligence Technologies in the Russian Federation (draft; originally 'On the Foundations of State Regulation of Areas of Application of AI Technologies')
short_title: Russia AI Foundations Law
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: Authorized body in the field of artificial intelligence; Federal executive authorities
summary: Russia's draft comprehensive AI governance framework law, submitted by the Government. Establishes foundational principles for AI development and deployment including risk-based regulation, disclosure obligations, data localisation requirements for trusted AI models, a register of certified trusted AI models for use in state systems, and liability provisions. Emphasises technological sovereignty and Russian value alignment. A sovereign AI model development programme supports domestic large foundation models. Mandatory human-in-the-loop rights for autonomous decisions affecting citizens. Watermarking/labelling requirements for AI-generated content. Enters into force 1 September 2026.

title: Anpassningar till AI-förordningen — proposed complementary Swedish law and ordinance implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (SOU 2025:101)
short_title: Sweden AI Act Adaptation Bill (SOU 2025:101)
summary: Swedish government inquiry proposing a new supplementary law and ordinance to implement the EU AI Act. Report (betänkande) published 6 Oct 2025; in public consultation (remiss) from Nov 2025; not yet a proposition. Recommends 11 market surveillance authorities and 2 notifying authorities, with the Swedish Post and Telecom Authority (PTS) as principal market surveillance authority; adds provisions on sanctions, secrecy, reporting duties, and AI regulatory sandboxes. Proposed entry into force 2 Aug 2026.

title: Partial Amendment to the Framework Act on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and the Establishment of a Foundation of Trust (인공지능 발전과 신뢰 기반 조성 등에 관한 기본법 일부개정법률안)
short_title: South Korea AI Basic Act Amendment (Public-Sector AI Security)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI; National security & defence
summary: The bill would amend South Korea's AI Basic Act to make security-management measures mandatory when public institutions adopt or use AI systems, including prior security review, control of system access rights, and blocking and logging of external data transmission. Its stated aim is to prevent uncontrolled leakage of government-held public and private data to external AI systems while still enabling public-sector AI adoption.

title: New Jersey A 3497 — Rental Property Owners Competition Agreements
short_title: New Jersey A 3497 — Rental Property Owners Competition Agreements
summary: Prohibits certain coordination among residential rental property owners who restrict competition with respect to residential dwelling units.

title: Hawaii H 2137 — Artificial Intelligence
short_title: Hawaii H 2137 — Artificial Intelligence
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Consumer protection; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Prohibits certain harmful uses of and mandates disclosure for realistic digital imitations generated by artificial intelligence (AI), establishes certain exemptions, provides for civil actions and civil remedies for individuals injured by unauthorized AI-generated realistic digital imitations, requires the disclosure of the use of synthetic performers in advertising, establishes civil fines.

title: Hawaii S 3001 — Artificial Intelligence
short_title: Hawaii S 3001 — Artificial Intelligence
summary: Requires operators of conversational artificial intelligence services in the State to issue certain disclosures to account holders and users, requires operators to develop protocols to prevent the production of suicidal ideations in account holders and users. establishes protections for account holders and users of conversational artificial intelligence services. establishes protections for minor account holders and users of conversational artificial intelligence services.

title: Amendment to the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and Establishment of Trust Basis
short_title: South Korea AI Basic Act Enforcement Decree Amendment (July 2026)
summary: Amendment to the Enforcement Decree of South Korea's AI Basic Act, approved by the Cabinet on 14 July 2026 and effective 21 July 2026. It creates an 'AI Product and Service Verification System' requiring public institutions to prioritise verified AI products and services in the roughly KRW 243 trillion public procurement market, and broadens the definition of AI-vulnerable groups to include jobseekers and women re-entering the workforce. The measure complements the AI Basic Act's risk-based obligations by adding industry-promotion and inclusion provisions.

title: Missouri S 1019 — Hospital Investments and Service Areas
short_title: Missouri S 1019 — Hospital Investments and Service Areas
summary: Modifies provisions relating to hospital investments and service areas.

title: Missouri H 2372 — Health Care
short_title: Missouri H 2372 — Health Care
summary: Modifies provisions relating to health care.

title: Entwurf eines Gesetzes zur Durchführung der KI-Verordnung (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsförderungsgesetz, KI-MIG)
short_title: AI Act implementation act (KI-MIG, draft)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Government use of AI; Financial services
issuing_body: Federal Ministry for Digital and State Modernisation
summary: The draft implementation act designates the Bundesnetzagentur as the central market-surveillance authority and single point of contact under the EU AI Act, keeps sector regulators (financial supervision, data protection for law-enforcement uses) competent in their fields, sets the national penalty framework within the Regulation's ranges and creates a national AI regulatory sandbox and an AI service desk for companies.
scope: Applies to providers, deployers, importers and distributors of AI systems in Germany as far as the EU AI Act reaches them; it allocates supervision rather than adding new substantive duties.

title: Illinois S 2909 — Evaluation of Certified Employees Article
short_title: Illinois S 2909 — Evaluation of Certified Employees Article
summary: Amends the Evaluation of Certified Employees Article of the School Code, provides that a teacher is prohibited from using an artificial intelligence tool to generate evidence of professional practice that will be used by an evaluator to evaluate the teachers performance, provides that an artificial intelligence tool may be used by a teacher to support the teacher in administrative tasks, makes changes concerning the joint committee requirement.

title: Illinois S 3114 — Transparency in Downcoding Act
short_title: Illinois S 3114 — Transparency in Downcoding Act
summary: Creates the Transparency in Downcoding Act, provides that the Act applies to certain policies of health insurance amended, delivered, issued, or renewed on or after the effective date of the Act, except for employee or employer self-insured health benefit plans under the federal Employee Retirement Income Security Act and health care provided pursuant to the Workers' Compensation Act or the Workers' Occupational Diseases Act.

title: Projeto de Lei 4089/2024 — Proteção dos direitos dos consumidores no uso de produtos e serviços que utilizam Inteligência Artificial
short_title: Brazil AI Consumer Protection Bill (PL 4089/2024)
summary: Chamber of Deputies bill (PL 4089/2024, Dep. Marcos Tavares) on consumer protection for AI products/services: clear disclosure when interacting with AI, explanation of automated decisions, right to human review and to refuse solely-automated decisions. On 10 June 2026 the Science, Technology & Innovation Committee approved a substitute (rapporteur Dep. David Soares) consolidating PL 4089/2024 with PL 5441/2025 and PL 6586/2025. Proceeds conclusively; still to be analysed by the Consumer Protection Committee and the CCJC. Not yet enacted.

title: European Commission Proposal — Digital Omnibus Regulation Amending GDPR, NIS2, Data Act, DORA and Related Instruments
short_title: EU Digital Omnibus — Digital Law Amendments
topics: Data protection & privacy; National security & defence
issuing_body: National Data Protection Authorities; ENISA; National Competent Authorities
summary: European Commission proposal (19 November 2025) amending six EU digital regulations simultaneously: narrows GDPR personal data identifiability standard; extends breach notification from 72 to 96 hours; integrates cookie consent into GDPR framework; clarifies legitimate interest basis for AI training data; amends NIS2, Data Act, DORA, CER, and eIDAS 2.0. Part of the Digital Omnibus package alongside the AI Act amendment proposal. As of May 2026, file is in the European Parliament under joint ITRE/LIBE responsibility (rapporteurs Aura Salla and Marina Kaljurand); EDPB-EDPS Joint Opinion 2/2026 adopted 10 February 2026; no Council general approach or EP plenary position yet.

title: North Carolina S 474 — The DAVE Act
short_title: North Carolina S 474 — The DAVE Act
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
summary: Enacts the dave act by creating the division of accountability, value, and efficiency within the Department of State auditor, directing each state agency to report to the division on its use of public monies and the status of its vacant positions, and directing the division to assess the continued need of each state agency and the vacant positions within each state agency.

title: Hawaii H 1682 — Disclosure of Intimate Images
short_title: Hawaii H 1682 — Disclosure of Intimate Images
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Enacts the Uniform Civil Remedies for Unauthorized Disclosure of Intimate Images Act.

title: Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act (Public Act 104-0538 / Senate Bill 315, 104th General Assembly)
short_title: Illinois AI Safety Measures Act (SB 315)
summary: Signed by Governor JB Pritzker on 6 July 2026 as Public Act 104-0538, the Act imposes safety and transparency obligations on 'large frontier developers' of advanced AI models. Covered developers must adopt, publish, and annually update a frontier AI safety framework addressing catastrophic-risk assessment and mitigation, file transparency reports before deploying new or substantially modified models, report safety incidents to the state, and undergo first-in-the-nation annual independent third-party safety audits, with whistleblower protections for employees who raise safety concerns. It takes effect on 1 January 2027.

title: California S 300 — Companion Chatbots
short_title: California S 300 — Companion Chatbots
summary: Require a companion chatbot operator to take the above actions when it has constructive knowledge that a user is a minor. Requires an operator to prevent its companion chatbot from producing or facilitating the exchange of any sexually explicit material or proposing sexually explicit conduct.

title: California S 574 — Generative Artificial Intelligence
short_title: California S 574 — Generative Artificial Intelligence
summary: Obligates an attorney who uses generative artificial intelligence to practice law to ensure that confidential personal identifying, or other nonpublic information, is not entered into a public generative artificial intelligence system. Requires an attorney to ensure that reasonable steps are taken to verify the accuracy of generative artificial intelligence material and to correct any erroneous or hallucinated output in any material used by the attorney.

title: California S 607 — California Institutes for Science and Innovation
short_title: California S 607 — California Institutes for Science and Innovation
summary: Provides that existing law authorizes the Regents of the University of California to establish 4 California Institutes for Science and Innovation at separate campuses of the University of California for specified purposes. Provides that existing law authorizes the concentration of each institute to include, among other concentrations, medicine, bioengineering, or space. Authorizes the concentration of an institute to include artificial intelligence.

title: California S 813 — California AI Standards and Safety Commission
short_title: California S 813 — California AI Standards and Safety Commission
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI; Consumer protection
summary: Require the agency to establish the California AI Standards and Safety Commission and would provide for its membership. Requires the commission to take certain actions related to the safety of artificial intelligence, including maintaining formal liaison relationships with state agencies deploying or procuring artificial intelligence, providing artificial intelligence technical expertise and artificial intelligence risk assessment.

title: California S 903 — Mental Health Professionals: Artificial Intelligence
short_title: California S 903 — Mental Health Professionals: Artificial Intelligence
summary: Regulates the use of artificial intelligence by licensed professionals providing psychotherapy services. Prohibits an individual, corporation, or entity from using artificial intelligence to record or transcribe psychotherapeutic communications or sessions or to triage or screen a person for the need for psychotherapy services unless the patient or their authorized representative is informed that artificial intelligence will be used and provides consent.

title: California S 916 — Civil Actions: Housing Development Projects
short_title: California S 916 — Civil Actions: Housing Development Projects
summary: Provides that existing law provides that in a civil action brought by a plaintiff to challenge a housing development project that meets or exceeds the requirements for low or moderate income housing, a defendant may seek an order requiring the plaintiff to furnish an undertaking as security for costs and damages. Provides that existing law authorizes the court to limit the amount of the undertaking or to decline that requirement under certain conditions. Applies provisions to a student housing development.

title: California S 947 — Employment: Automated Decision Systems
short_title: California S 947 — Employment: Automated Decision Systems
summary: Requires an employer that primarily relied upon an ADS to make a disciplinary, termination, or deactivation decision to provide the affected worker with a written postuse notice, as specified.

title: California S 951 — Employment: Technological Displacement: Notice
short_title: California S 951 — Employment: Technological Displacement: Notice
summary: Requires an employer to provide a written technology hiring disruption notice to the Employment Development Department and the local workforce investment board when it executes a technological cessation in hiring directly and primarily due to the adoption of artificial intelligence or other automating technology. Imposes various reporting requirements on the Employment Development Department.

title: California S 1000 — California AI Transparency Act
short_title: California S 1000 — California AI Transparency Act
summary: Provides that the California AI Transparency Act requires a covered provider to make available an AI detection tool at no cost to the user. Provides that existing law requires a covered provider to include a certain latent disclosure in AI generated image, video, or audio content, or content that is any combination thereof, created by the covered providers GenAI system. Requires a covered provider to include in the latent disclosure whether the content is generated or modified by artificial intelligence.

title: California S 1119 — Companion Chatbots: Childrens Safety
short_title: California S 1119 — Companion Chatbots: Childrens Safety
summary: Requires an operator of a companion chatbot to do various things with respect to child safety and companion chatbots, including annually performing and documenting a comprehensive risk assessment to identify any child safety risk posed by the design, configuration, and operation of the companion chatbot that assesses, among other things, the likelihood of a covered harm occurring to users.

title: California S 1133 — Pupil Instruction: Preventative Health Instruction
short_title: California S 1133 — Pupil Instruction: Preventative Health Instruction
summary: Provides for the Ready to Learn, Ready for Health Act. Requires, when the Health Education Framework for California Public Schools is next revised on or after the specified date, the Instructional Quality Commission to consider including information on evidence based preventative health instruction, including information on nutrition, food literacy, sleep, movement, stress management, and digital balance in an integrated manner that discusses these key health factors and the interrelationship between them.

title: California S 1159 — Artificial Intelligence: Transparency and Governance
short_title: California S 1159 — Artificial Intelligence: Transparency and Governance
topics: Government use of AI; Consumer protection
summary: Specifies that, for purposes of the State Public Records Act, the Bagley Keene Open Meeting Act, the Ralph M. Brown Act, the Political Reform Act of 1974, the Administrative Procedure Act, and the California Environmental Quality Act, the terms person, interested person, participant, member of the public, and any other similar terms under each act referring to those who may engage with governmental agencies, do not include artificial intelligence.

title: California S 1181 — Central Valley School Safety Coordination Pilot Program
short_title: California S 1181 — Central Valley School Safety Coordination Pilot Program
summary: Requires the Office of Emergency Services, in consultation with the State Department of Education, to establish the Central Valley School Safety Coordination Pilot Program for the purpose of studying and evaluating improved communication pathways between local educational agencies and regional fusion centers regarding credible safety threats affecting school communities.

title: California S 1276 — Crimes: Sexual Exploitation of a Child
short_title: California S 1276 — Crimes: Sexual Exploitation of a Child
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Makes a person guilty of a misdemeanor or a felony if the person downloads, streams, or accesses through electronic or digital media material that depicts a person under 18 years of age engaged in an act of sexual conduct, except as specified.

title: California A 1883 — Workplace Surveillance Tools
short_title: California A 1883 — Workplace Surveillance Tools
topics: General AI governance; Employment & HR; Consumer protection
summary: Prohibits an employer from using a workplace surveillance tool on workers for various purposes. Includes preventing compliance with laws or regulations, inferring information about workers engaging in a protected activity, making inferences about an individual's emotional state or based on their gait, or collecting neural data. Prohibits an employer from using facial recognition technology, unless it is used strictly to open a locked device or grant access to locked or secure areas.

title: California A 1946 — Reporting Mechanism: Child Sexual Abuse Material
short_title: California A 1946 — Reporting Mechanism: Child Sexual Abuse Material
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Makes a social media company liable to a depicted individual, as defined, for actual and statutory damages, as provided. Imposes a civil penalty on a noncomplying company to be collected in a civil action by certain public attorneys, including the Attorney General. Establishes the Survivor Support Fund within the state treasury and makes moneys in the fund available, upon appropriation by the Legislature, for grants by the State Victim Compensation Board to community-based organizations.

title: California A 1979 — Health Care Services: Artificial Intelligence
short_title: California A 1979 — Health Care Services: Artificial Intelligence
summary: Requires a health facility, clinic, physician's office, or office or a group practice to ensure that no clinical decision, is based solely on the output of a clinical decision support system, as defined, and that a licensed health care professional exercises independent professional judgment when reviewing and approving a clinical decision that is based on the output of a clinical decision support system.

title: California A 2071 — Pupil Instruction: Digital Wellness
short_title: California A 2071 — Pupil Instruction: Digital Wellness
summary: Requires the State Department of Education, on or before a specified date, to develop a plan to expand mental health instruction in State public schools. Requires the department, on or before a specified date, to develop a plan to expand digital wellness instruction in the state public schools, as provided.

title: California A 2403 — Income Tax: Credits: Commercial Production
short_title: California A 2403 — Income Tax: Credits: Commercial Production
summary: Excludes any commercial that is created entirely by generative artificial intelligence, as specified, or that utilizes generative artificial intelligence, automated technologies, or autonomous vehicles in a manner that replaces or diminishes the job functions customarily performed by a human worker in the production. Requires any bill authorizing a new tax expenditure to contain, among other things, specific goals, purposes, and objectives that the tax expenditure will achieve.

title: California S 420 — Automated Decision Systems
short_title: California S 420 — Automated Decision Systems
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI; Consumer protection
summary: Requires a developer or a deployer of a high-risk automated decision system to perform an impact assessment before making it publicly available or deploying it. Authorizes the Attorney General or the Civil Rights Department to allow a developer or deployer to cure certain violations. Prohibits an agency from awarding a contract for a high-risk automated decision system unless the person to whom the contract is awarded has certified that the system does not violate, among other civil rights laws, this bill.

title: California S 813 — Multistakeholder Regulatory Organizations
short_title: California S 813 — Multistakeholder Regulatory Organizations
topics: Government use of AI; Consumer protection
summary: Provides that existing law requires the Department of Technology to conduct a comprehensive inventory of all high risk automated decision systems that have been proposed for use, development or procurement by, or are being used, developed, or procured by, a State agency. Establishes a process by which the Attorney General designates a private entity as a multistakeholder regulatory organization. Authorizes the Attorney General to establish a fee structure for charging fees to applicants and designated MROs.

title: California S 867 — Toys: Companion Chatbots
short_title: California S 867 — Toys: Companion Chatbots
summary: Prohibits, until 1/1/2031, the manufacture, sale, exchange, possession with intent to sell or exchange, and exposition or offer for sale or exchange to a retailer a toy, as defined, that includes a companion chatbot, and would make violations of the bill subject to the same civil liability as violations of the provisions applicable to operators of companion chatbots in the above-described paragraph.

title: California S 1050 — False Advertising: Synthetic Digital Performers
short_title: California S 1050 — False Advertising: Synthetic Digital Performers
summary: Makes it an unlawful advertising practice for a person to create and cause to be published in an advertising medium an advertisement that includes a synthetic performer without a clear and conspicuous disclosure that the performer is synthetic. Prohibits an advertising medium from transmitting, distributing, displaying, airing, or otherwise making available an advertisement containing a synthetic performer if a court of competent jurisdiction has issued an order.

title: California S 1111 — Digital Replicas
short_title: California S 1111 — Digital Replicas
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Provides that existing law creates a civil cause of action against any person who knowingly uses the name, voice, signature, photograph, or likeness of another person, without their consent, for specified purposes. Clarifies that a voice or likeness includes a digital replica. Clarifies that false impersonation includes the use of a digital replica with the intent to impersonate another.

title: California A 1609 — Customer Service Chatbots
short_title: California A 1609 — Customer Service Chatbots
summary: Prohibits a large private business from representing that a customer service chatbot is a human. Requires the large private business to provide certain disclosures if a reasonable person interacting with the chatbot would be misled to believe they are interacting with a human. Requires a large private business to provide customers with human customer service support and communications within a specified number of minutes of requesting human customer service.

title: California A 1705 — Pornographic Internet Websites
short_title: California A 1705 — Pornographic Internet Websites
summary: Requires an operator of a pornographic internet website, among other things, to exercise ordinary care and reasonable diligence to ensure that each instance of sexually explicit content displayed on the operator's pornographic internet website does not include a depicted individual. Defines terms, including depicted person, for its purposes.

title: California A 2212 — Postsecondary Education: Sexual Harassment
short_title: California A 2212 — Postsecondary Education: Sexual Harassment
summary: Requires, in order to receive State funds for student financial assistance, the governing board of a community college district, the Trustees of the State University, the Regents of the University of California, and the governing boards of independent postsecondary educational institutions to update their sexual harassment policies to include, among other things, a list of organizations to assist students and employees with the removal of digitized sexually explicit material from digital platforms.

title: California A 2656 — Public Employees: Notice: Artificial Intelligence
short_title: California A 2656 — Public Employees: Notice: Artificial Intelligence
topics: Government use of AI; Consumer protection
summary: Relates to the deployment of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools by the State. Requires certain State and local public employers to provide written notice to a recognized employee organization at least a specified number of days before taking an action to develop, purchase, implement, or utilize GenAI to perform a service that is within the scope of work of the job classification represented by the recognized employee organization.

title: California S 238 — Workplace Surveillance Tools
short_title: California S 238 — Workplace Surveillance Tools
summary: Requires an employer to annually provide a notice to the Department of Industrial Relations, in the Labor and Workforce Development Agency, of all the workplace surveillance tools the employer is using in the workplace. Requires the notice to include, among other information, the personal information that will be collected from workers and consumers and whether they will have the option of opting out of the collection of personal information.

title: Delaware H 233 — Large Energy Use Facilities
short_title: Delaware H 233 — Large Energy Use Facilities
summary: Requires regulated utilities to establish a separate rate for large energy-use facilities that mitigates the risk of costs associated with expanding infrastructure and maintaining reliability in the face of growing demand from being shifted to residential, small business, and other electric customers.

title: Delaware H 233 — Large Energy Use Facilities
short_title: Delaware H 233 — Large Energy Use Facilities
summary: Requires regulated utilities to establish a separate rate for large energy-use facilities that mitigates the risk of costs associated with expanding infrastructure and maintaining reliability in the face of growing demand from being shifted to residential, small business, and other electric customers.

title: Pennsylvania H 2006 — Artificial Intelligence In Companionship Applications
short_title: Pennsylvania H 2006 — Artificial Intelligence In Companionship Applications
summary: Provides for safety regarding artificial intelligence in companionship applications, imposes a penalty.

title: California A 412 — Generative Artificial Intelligence: Training Data
short_title: California A 412 — Generative Artificial Intelligence: Training Data
summary: Relates to copyrighted materials. Requires a developer of a generative artificial intelligence model to document any covered materials that the developer knows were used by the developer to train the model. Requires the developer to make available a mechanism on the developer's website allowing a rights owner to submit a request for information. Authorizes a rights owner who complies with specified requirements for submitting a request that is not provided with information to bring a civil action.

title: California S 719 — Department of Technology: Inventory
short_title: California S 719 — Department of Technology: Inventory
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
summary: Provides that existing law, until January 1, 2029, requires the Department of Technology to annually submit to certain legislative committees a report regarding a specified required comprehensive inventory of all high-risk automated decision systems that have been, or are being, used, developed, or procured by a state agency. Extends that reporting requirement until January 1, 2032.

title: California A 2148 — Elementary and secondary education
short_title: California A 2148 — Elementary and secondary education
summary: Establishes a system of public elementary and secondary education in this state. Requires school districts, county offices of education, and charter schools employ personnel to provide instruction to and services for pupils in kindergarten and grades 1 to 12, inclusive, at school sites throughout the state. Defines, for purposes of the Education Code, both a public school employee and a contractor providing services in a public school to mean a natural person.

title: California A 2392 — Public Postsecondary Education: Artificial Intelligence
short_title: California A 2392 — Public Postsecondary Education: Artificial Intelligence
summary: Requires the California Community Colleges and the California State University, and requests the University of California, before providing a generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) system to students, faculty, or staff, to as specified, convene a joint working group to present recommendations for procurement standards and training, which the bill would require to be submitted on or before a specified date.

title: California A 2504 — Community Colleges: Artificial Intelligence: Pilot
short_title: California A 2504 — Community Colleges: Artificial Intelligence: Pilot
summary: Relates to the Chancellor of the California Community Colleges. Requires the chancellors office to implement the Future of Creative Industries Pilot Program and to select up to a specified number of community college districts to participate in the pilot program. Requires the chancellors office to submit a report to the Legislature evaluating the effectiveness of the pilot program.

title: California A 2545 — Report: Labor Force Impact: Artificial Intelligence
short_title: California A 2545 — Report: Labor Force Impact: Artificial Intelligence
summary: Establishes the State Artificial Intelligence Worker Impact Data Assessment Project and establishes the State Artificial Intelligence Worker Impact Data Assessment Project Advisory Panel in the Employment Development Department. Requires the EDD, in consultation with the advisory panel, to perform an assessment of data sources and collection methods regarding the use and impact of advanced artificial intelligence systems on the labor force. Requires the advisory panel to submit a report to the Legislature.

title: California A 412 — Generative Artificial Intelligence: Training Data
short_title: California A 412 — Generative Artificial Intelligence: Training Data
summary: Relates to copyrighted materials. Requires a developer of a generative artificial intelligence model to document any covered materials that the developer knows were used by the developer to train the model. Requires the developer to make available a mechanism on the developer's website allowing a rights owner to submit a request for information. Authorizes a rights owner who complies with specified requirements for submitting a request that is not provided with information to bring a civil action.

title: New Jersey S 451 — Algorithmic Systems to Influence Price
short_title: New Jersey S 451 — Algorithmic Systems to Influence Price
summary: Provides that it shall be unlawful and a violation of the State Antitrust Act for a rental property owner to subscribe to, contract with, or otherwise exchange any form of consideration in return for the use of services of a coordinator, defined as any person who operates a software or data analytics service that performs a coordinating function for any rental property owner, provides that a coordinator shall not include a government entity that sets or limits rents or sale prices of residential property.

title: New Jersey S 3612 — Fair Price Protection Act
short_title: New Jersey S 3612 — Fair Price Protection Act
summary: Provides that it shall be considered an unlawful practice for a person to use personalized algorithmic pricing, surveillance pricing, or any pricing strategy that determines or varies the sale price of groceries and other foodstuff based, in whole or in part, on personal data.

title: Anteproyecto de Ley para el buen uso y la gobernanza de la inteligencia artificial
short_title: Draft law on good use and governance of AI
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Government use of AI; Financial services
issuing_body: Ministry for Digital Transformation and the Civil Service
summary: The draft implements the EU AI Act in Spain: it allocates supervision among AESIA, the data-protection authority, the electoral board, the financial and audiovisual regulators, sets the national penalty scale (up to EUR 35 million or 7% of turnover for prohibited practices), treats failure to label AI-generated content as a serious infringement and provides for the national sandbox to continue.
scope: Providers, deployers, importers and distributors of AI systems in Spain within the scope of the EU AI Act.

title: California A 2575 — Health Care Services: Artificial Intelligence
short_title: California A 2575 — Health Care Services: Artificial Intelligence
summary: Requires a health facility, clinic, physician's office, or office of a group practice that uses or deploys a clinical decision support system, as defined, for patient care to provide written notice of required information to any licensed health care professional or other person using a clinical decision support system or viewing outputs from a clinical decision support system.

title: California A 502 — Elections: Deceptive Media In Advertisements
short_title: California A 502 — Elections: Deceptive Media In Advertisements
summary: Sets forth additional requirements relating to the color and font size of the disclosure's text. Exempts an election communication from the prohibition if the content includes a disclosure stating that the communication has been generated or substantially altered using artificial intelligence. Exempts an advertisement or other election communication from these prohibitions if a reasonable person would understand that the content was satire or parody.

title: Illinois S 3020 — Domestic Violence and Harassment
short_title: Illinois S 3020 — Domestic Violence and Harassment
summary: Amends the Protective Orders Article of the Code of Criminal Procedure of 1963, changes the definition of harassment, provides that the court may order the respondent to cease harassment, establishes procedures for motions to extend plenary protective orders, provides that the court may order the respondent to stop creating, using, and disseminating.

title: California A 1988 — Companion Chatbots: Crisis Interruption Pauses
short_title: California A 1988 — Companion Chatbots: Crisis Interruption Pauses
summary: Provides for the Preventing AI User Self Endangerment (PAUSE) Act. Requires an operator of companion chatbots to adopt and make publicly available a policy governing its protocol for identifying and responding to credible crisis expressions and, for each companion chatbot an operator makes available to users in the State, implement a system for monitoring and detecting credible crisis expressions in user conversations with companion chatbots.

title: California A 2412 — State Agencies or Departments: Public Communications
short_title: California A 2412 — State Agencies or Departments: Public Communications
topics: Government use of AI; Consumer protection
summary: Provides that existing law requires a State agency or department that utilizes generative artificial intelligence to directly communicate with a person regarding government services and benefits to ensure that those communications include a disclaimer that indicates to the person that the communication was generated by GenAI. Requires that disclaimer when a State agency or department communicates with the public.

title: Illinois H 5284 — Menopause Equity and Care Act
short_title: Illinois H 5284 — Menopause Equity and Care Act
topics: General AI governance; Employment & HR; Health
summary: Improves awareness, understanding, and quality of care for individuals experiencing menopause, requires the Department of Public Health to develop and make publicly available educational materials about menopause, including symptoms, evidence-based treatment options, and patient rights, amends the Illinois Insurance Code, requires that any individual or group plan of accident or health insurance amended, delivered, issued, or renewed on or after a specified date.

title: California S 1015 — Crimes: Minors
short_title: California S 1015 — Crimes: Minors
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Makes any adult person who recruits, induces, coerces, or persuades a minor to commit an illegal act against another minor, or to solicit physical harm, sexual conduct, or images of an intimate body part, from another minor, or who utilizes a minor as a conduit of communication to facilitate any such acts guilty of a crime punishable either as a misdemeanor or a felony. summary: Uzbekistan's first AI-specific law amends the Law on Informatization and the Code on Administrative Liability. Adopted by the Legislative Chamber on 12 August 2025 and approved by the Senate on 1 November 2025.
