The Online Safety Commission can issue stop-communication and account-restriction directions against platforms hosting AI-generated harmful content.

title: Act LXXV of 2025 on the Domestic Implementation of the EU AI Act (Hungary)
short_title: Hungary AI Act Implementation 2025
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Government use of AI; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: Hungarian Artificial Intelligence Council; sector-specific competent authorities
summary: Hungary becomes first Central-Eastern European state to enact a standalone domestic AI Act implementation law. Establishes the Hungarian AI Council, designates sector-specific national competent authorities, and creates domestic procedures for market surveillance, conformity assessment, and regulatory sandboxes. Aligns enforcement and sanctions with EU AI Act timelines and penalty structures.

title: Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Amending the Cybersecurity Law of the People's Republic of China
short_title: China Cybersecurity Law Amendments 2025
issuing_body: CAC; MIIT; MPS
summary: First major amendment to China's Cybersecurity Law since its 2017 enactment. Adds explicit AI safety provisions: AI systems deployed in critical infrastructure and key sectors must meet cybersecurity standards, AI providers must conduct security assessments, and entities using AI must implement AI ethics standards and monitoring. Increases maximum fines tenfold (from RMB 1M to RMB 10M) and adds personal liability for responsible persons.

title: Puerto Rico H.B. 824 — Amendment to Act 40-2024 (Cybersecurity Act) to Include Artificial Intelligence in Cybersecurity Education
short_title: Puerto Rico H.B. 824 — Cybersecurity Act AI Amendment
topics: General AI governance; Education; Government use of AI; National security & defence
issuing_body: PRITS
summary: Amends Act 40-2024 (Cybersecurity Act of the Government of Puerto Rico) to expressly incorporate artificial intelligence as a topic in the virtual cybersecurity education program and continuing education course administered by PRITS. Passed House; received positive committee report from the Senate Committee on Science, Technology, and Artificial Intelligence in 2026.

title: Massachusetts H 1946 — Facial Recognition Technology
short_title: Massachusetts H 1946 — Facial Recognition Technology
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
summary: Implements the recommendations of the special commission on facial recognition technology.

title: Ohio H 525 — Artificial Intelligence in Therapy Services
short_title: Ohio H 525 — Artificial Intelligence in Therapy Services
summary: Regards the use of artificial intelligence in therapy services.

title: Guidance for AI Adoption (Australian Government, DISR/NAIC)
short_title: Guidance for AI Adoption
issuing_body: Department of Industry, Science and Resources; National AI Centre
summary: Official successor to the 2024 Voluntary AI Safety Standard, published by the Department of Industry, Science and Resources and the National AI Centre. Streamlines ten guardrails from the prior standard into six essential practices for responsible AI governance in Australian organizations. Non-binding voluntary guidance applicable across all sectors.

title: Massachusetts S 1053 — Facial Recognition Technology
short_title: Massachusetts S 1053 — Facial Recognition Technology
summary: Implements the recommendations of the special commission on facial recognition technology.

title: Massachusetts H 1136 — Health Insurance Prior Authorization Process
short_title: Massachusetts H 1136 — Health Insurance Prior Authorization Process
summary: Relates to the health insurance prior authorization process.

title: Massachusetts S 35 — Electronic Monitoring Tools
short_title: Massachusetts S 35 — Electronic Monitoring Tools
topics: General AI governance; Employment & HR; Consumer protection
summary: Promotes employee physical and mental health and wellbeing by limiting the use of electronic monitoring tools.

title: Massachusetts S 37 — Artificial Intelligence Models and Safety
short_title: Massachusetts S 37 — Artificial Intelligence Models and Safety
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI; Consumer protection
summary: Promotes economic development with emerging artificial intelligence models and safety.

title: Massachusetts S 44 — Election Communications
short_title: Massachusetts S 44 — Election Communications
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Law enforcement & justice; Elections
summary: Relates to deceptive and fraudulent deepfakes in election communications.

title: Massachusetts S 46 — Healthcare Decision Making
short_title: Massachusetts S 46 — Healthcare Decision Making
topics: Health; Government use of AI; Consumer protection
summary: Relates to the use of artificial intelligence and other software tools in healthcare decision-making.

title: Massachusetts S 48 — AI Generated Child Sexual Abuse Material
short_title: Massachusetts S 48 — AI Generated Child Sexual Abuse Material
summary: Relates to AI-generated child sexual abuse material.

title: Massachusetts S 51 — Social Media Algorithm Accountability and Transparency
short_title: Massachusetts S 51 — Social Media Algorithm Accountability and Transparency
summary: Relates to social media, algorithm accountability, and transparency.

title: Massachusetts S 2630 — Artificial Intelligence Models
short_title: Massachusetts S 2630 — Artificial Intelligence Models
summary: Promotes economic development with emerging artificial intelligence models and safety.

title: Massachusetts S 2631 — Election Misinformation
short_title: Massachusetts S 2631 — Election Misinformation
summary: Relates to protect against election misinformation.

title: Massachusetts S 2633 — AI Generated Child Sexual Abuse Material
short_title: Massachusetts S 2633 — AI Generated Child Sexual Abuse Material
summary: Relates to AI-generated child sexual abuse material.

title: New York A 1417 — Landlords
short_title: New York A 1417 — Landlords
summary: Amends the general business law, in relation to prohibiting the use of algorithmic pricing by a landlord for the purpose of determining the amount of rent to charge a residential tenant.

title: New York S 7882 — Residential Rental Dwelling Units
short_title: New York S 7882 — Residential Rental Dwelling Units
summary: Prohibits a person or entity from knowingly or with reckless disregard facilitate an agreement between or among two or more residential rental property owners or managers to not compete with respect to residential rental dwelling units, including by operating or licensing a software, data analytics service, or algorithmic device that performs a coordinating function on behalf of or between and among such residential rental property owners or managers.

title: Guam B 171 — Deepfakes
short_title: Guam B 171 — Deepfakes
summary: Prohibits the creation, possession, disclosure, or threatened disclosure of nonconsensual intimate depictions, whether authentic or technologically manipulated (""deepfakes""), provides criminal penalties, civil remedies, forfeiture, victim-privacy safeguards, and expanded jurisdiction.

title: Companion Chatbot Safety and Disclosure Act
short_title: California SB 243 (Companion Chatbot)
issuing_body: California Attorney General
summary: First US law regulating AI companion chatbots. Requires disclosure that the companion is an AI, mandates safety protocols for minors including suicide/self-harm prevention, and prohibits romantic or sexual interactions with minors. Includes private right of action and AG enforcement.

title: California Assembly Bill 853 — AI Transparency Act Technical Corrections
short_title: California AB 853 (AI Transparency Act Technical Corrections)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: California Attorney General
summary: Amends the California AI Transparency Act (SB 942) to delay the compliance deadline for AI content provenance and origin disclosure requirements from January 1, 2026 to August 2, 2026, while making technical corrections to disclosure obligations. The core requirement that large AI providers offer a free, publicly accessible AI detection tool is maintained without substantive change.

title: California Assembly Bill 316 — Artificial Intelligence Autonomous Harm Defense Limitation
short_title: California AB 316 (AI Autonomous Harm Defense Limitation)
issuing_body: California courts (civil litigation)
summary: In civil litigation alleging harm caused by an AI system, defendants (developers, modifiers, or deployers) may not assert as a complete defense that the AI caused harm autonomously or without human involvement. All other civil defenses — including causation, foreseeability, assumption of risk, and comparative negligence — are preserved.

title: California A 82 — Health Care: Legally Protected Health Care Activity
short_title: California A 82 — Health Care: Legally Protected Health Care Activity
summary: Expands the Address Confidentiality Program to a gender-affirming health care provider, employee or volunteer who faces threats of violence or harassment because of affiliation with a gender-affirming health services facility. Prohibits a person, business or association from soliciting, selling or trading on the internet or social media personal information or images of providers, employees, volunteers or patients with certain intent. Prohibits certain reports of testosterone or mifepristone prescriptions.

title: California A 621 — Deepfake Pornography
short_title: California A 621 — Deepfake Pornography
summary: Provides that existing law grants to a depicted individual a cause of action against a person who creates and intentionally discloses sexually explicit material. Grants to a depicted individual a cause of action against a person who knows, or reasonably should know, that the depicted individual was a minor when the digitized sexually explicit material was created. Grants a cause of action to that depicted individual against a person who knowingly facilitates or recklessly aids or abets prohibited conduct.

title: California Assembly Bill 489 — Healthcare AI Deception Prevention Act
short_title: California AB 489 (Healthcare AI Deception Prevention)
issuing_body: California Attorney General
summary: Prohibits AI systems from using licensed healthcare professional titles (e.g., doctor, nurse, therapist) in ways that imply users are receiving care from a licensed human practitioner. Healthcare facilities using generative AI in patient communications must include clear disclaimers that communications are AI-generated and not a substitute for professional medical advice.

title: California S 57 — Electrical Corporations: Data Centers: Report
short_title: California S 57 — Electrical Corporations: Data Centers: Report
summary: Provides that existing law authorizes the commission to fix the rates and charges for every public utility and requires that those rates and charges be just and reasonable. Authorizes the Public Utilities Commission to assess the extent to which electrical corporation costs associated with new loads from data centers result in cost shifts to other electrical corporation customers.

title: California S 524 — Law Enforcement Agencies: Artificial Intelligence
short_title: California S 524 — Law Enforcement Agencies: Artificial Intelligence
summary: Requires each law enforcement agency to maintain a policy to require an official report prepared by a law enforcement officer or any member of a law enforcement agency that is generated using artificial intelligence either fully or partially to include specified information, including a disclosure statement and the signature of the law enforcement officer or member of a law enforcement agency who prepared the official report. Requires an agency utilizing artificial intelligence to generate a first draft.

title: California S 683 — Privacy: Use of a Person's Name
short_title: California S 683 — Privacy: Use of a Person's Name
summary: Provides that a party seeking relief may also seek an injunction or temporary restraining order according to specified procedures. Requires the respondent to comply with the order within 2 business days from the day the order is served, unless otherwise required by the order, if the court grants the applicant a temporary restraining order without notice to the opposing party that requires the respondent to remove, recall, or otherwise cease the publication.

title: California A 723 — Real Estate: Digitally Altered Images: Disclosure
short_title: California A 723 — Real Estate: Digitally Altered Images: Disclosure
summary: Requires a real estate broker or salesperson, or person acting on their behalf, who includes a digitally altered image in an advertisement or other promotional material for the sale of real property to include a specified disclosure. Requires, if the advertisement or promotional material is posted on an internet website, the same image without digital alteration to be included.

jurisdiction: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
title: Monitoring Adoption of Artificial Intelligence and Related Vulnerabilities in the Financial Sector (FSB Report)
short_title: FSB — Monitoring AI Adoption and Vulnerabilities (2025)
summary: FSB report published October 10, 2025 as a G20 deliverable under the South Africa G20 presidency. A follow-up to the November 2024 FSB AI stability report, it identifies direct and proxy indicators for financial supervisory authorities to monitor AI adoption and related vulnerabilities in the financial sector. The report provides a practical monitoring toolkit for national regulators implementing AI oversight in financial services.

title: Malta Artificial Intelligence Regulations 2025 (Legal Notice 226 of 2025)
short_title: Malta AI Market Surveillance Regulations
issuing_body: Malta Digital Innovation Authority (MDIA)
summary: Malta Legal Notice 226 of 2025 designates the Malta Digital Innovation Authority (MDIA) as the primary market surveillance authority and notifying authority under the EU AI Act. It establishes the national AI regulatory sandbox and enforcement framework required by the EU AI Act. The regulation implements Malta's obligations as an EU member state to operationalise national AI oversight structures.

title: Artificial Intelligence (Designation of the IDPC) Regulations 2025 (Legal Notice 227 of 2025)
short_title: Malta IDPC AI Designation Regulations
topics: General AI governance; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: Information and Data Protection Commissioner (IDPC)
summary: Malta Legal Notice 227 of 2025 designates the Information and Data Protection Commissioner (IDPC) as market surveillance authority specifically for high-risk AI systems in sensitive domains listed under EU AI Act Annex III. The IDPC's remit covers AI systems involving biometrics, law enforcement, migration and border control, and the administration of justice. This creates a dual-authority model alongside the MDIA established under Legal Notice 226.

title: Massachusetts S 32 — Advanced Technology and the Internet
short_title: Massachusetts S 32 — Advanced Technology and the Internet
summary: Relates to the potential impacts and legal implications of advanced technology and the internet on protecting individuals from exploitation.

title: Puerto Rico S 731 — Artificial Intelligence
short_title: Puerto Rico S 731 — Artificial Intelligence
summary: Relates to Public Auctions with Artificial Intelligence and Government Transparency Act.

title: Defending Californians' Data Act
short_title: California SB 361 (Data Broker + GenAI)
issuing_body: California Privacy Protection Agency
summary: Expands California's data broker registration law to require disclosure when consumer data is shared with generative AI developers for training purposes. Data brokers must update privacy disclosures and provide opt-out mechanisms for GenAI training use.

title: Algorithmic Price-Fixing Prohibition Act (Cartwright Act Amendment)
short_title: California AB 325 (Algorithmic Pricing)
issuing_body: California Attorney General
summary: Amends the Cartwright Act to prohibit anticompetitive use of common pricing algorithms. Makes it unlawful to coerce competitors into adopting algorithm-recommended prices and lowers pleading standards for California antitrust claims involving algorithmic coordination.

title: California S 253 — State Bar of California
short_title: California S 253 — State Bar of California
topics: Employment & HR; Education; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Requires the California Lawyers Association or the affiliated 501(c)(3) organization to submit an annual report to the Legislature detailing their use of funds and a statement of compliance with the prohibition on creating, operating, or soliciting members for affinity or royalty programs involving similar products or services.

title: California A 979 — California Cybersecurity Integration Center: AI
short_title: California A 979 — California Cybersecurity Integration Center: AI
topics: Government use of AI; National security & defence
summary: Requires the State Cybersecurity Integration Center to develop, in consultation with the Office of Information Security and the Government Operations Agency, a State AI Cybersecurity Collaboration Playbook to facilitate information sharing across the cyber and artificial intelligence communities and to strengthen collective cyber defenses against emerging threats. Requires the center to review federal requirements, standards, and industry best practices, and to use those resources to inform the playbook.

title: Wisconsin 2025 Act 34 — Sexually Explicit Deepfake Prohibition
short_title: Wisconsin 2025 Act 34 (Sexually Explicit Deepfakes)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: courts
summary: Wisconsin Act 34/2025 makes it a misdemeanor to create AI-generated sexually explicit imagery of a person without consent; makes it a felony to use such content to coerce, harass, or intimidate. Covers 'synthetic intimate representations' realistic enough to be believed real.

title: Illinois S 124 — Insurance and Motor Vehicle Rates
short_title: Illinois S 124 — Insurance and Motor Vehicle Rates
summary: Amends the Insurance Code, provides that the Amendatory Act may be referred to as the Motor Vehicle Insurance Fairness Act, provides that no insurer shall refuse to issue or renew a policy of automobile insurance based in whole or in part on specified prohibited underwriting or rating factors, sets forth factors that are prohibited with respect to underwriting and rating a policy of automobile insurance, sets forth provisions concerning the use of Territorial factors, provides that every insurer.

title: Wisconsin S 33 — Representations Depicting Nudity
short_title: Wisconsin S 33 — Representations Depicting Nudity
summary: Relates to representations depicting nudity, provides a penalty.

title: California S 47 — February 2025 Bar Exam: Audit
short_title: California S 47 — February 2025 Bar Exam: Audit
summary: Relates to the State Bar Act. Requires the State Auditor to conduct an audit of the specified bar exam and to submit the audit as soon as possible to the Board of Trustees of the State Bar, the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, and to the Assembly and Senate Committees on Judiciary. Requires the State Bar to provide the California State Auditor with the funding necessary to cover the costs of the audit.

title: California S 241 — Community Colleges: Personnel: Qualifications
short_title: California S 241 — Community Colleges: Personnel: Qualifications
summary: Relates to the California Community Colleges. Requires a community college instructor, librarian, counselor, student personnel worker, supervisor, administrator, chief administrative officer, extended opportunity programs and services worker, disabled students programs and services worker, apprenticeship instructor, or supervisor of health to be a person who meets specified minimum qualifications to serve in that position or the alternative qualifications to serve in that position.

title: Ohio H 469 — Declare Artificial Intelligence Systems Nonsentient
short_title: Ohio H 469 — Declare Artificial Intelligence Systems Nonsentient
summary: Declares artificial intelligence systems nonsentient and prohibits them from obtaining legal personhood.

title: Puerto Rico Senate Bill 820 — Media and Information Literacy Act of Puerto Rico: requiring public school curriculum to include critical media literacy, AI literacy, and disinformation resistance competencies
short_title: Puerto Rico S 820 — Media and Information Literacy Act
issuing_body: Department of Education
summary: Creates the Media and Information Literacy Act of Puerto Rico, requiring the Department of Education to integrate media and digital literacy competencies into all K-12 subjects, with emphasis on identifying AI-generated content and deepfakes, understanding algorithmic bias, critical source evaluation, and responsible digital citizenship. Teachers must be trained; annual report to Legislature required.

title: Norway — KI-loven (Artificial Intelligence Act — EEA Implementation)
short_title: Norway KI-loven (AI Act EEA)
issuing_body: Norwegian Communications Authority (Nkom)
summary: Norwegian implementing legislation to incorporate the EU AI Act into Norwegian law via the EEA Agreement. Consultation package published 30 June 2025; consultation closed 30 September 2025; formal Storting introduction expected 2026. Designates Nkom as coordinating national AI supervisory authority. Provides national enforcement procedures, language localization requirements, and NOK-denominated penalty thresholds. Requires parallel EEA Joint Committee decision to incorporate EU AI Act into EEA Agreement Annex XX.

title: California SB 53: Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act
short_title: California SB 53
topics: General AI governance; Frontier / general-purpose AI
issuing_body: California State Legislature
summary: SB 53 requires "large frontier developers" (developers of the most compute-intensive models above statutory thresholds) to publish a frontier AI framework describing how they assess and mitigate catastrophic risks, publish transparency reports when deploying new frontier models, report critical safety incidents to the California Office of Emergency Services, and protect employees who report safety concerns. It also directs creation of a public computing cluster ("CalCompute").
scope: Applies to developers of frontier models meeting compute-based thresholds, with heightened duties for large frontier developers above a revenue threshold. Most obligations are transparency and reporting duties rather than prescriptive technical requirements.

title: Massachusetts S 1403 — Reducing Administrative Burden
short_title: Massachusetts S 1403 — Reducing Administrative Burden
summary: Relates to reducing administrative burden.

title: Guam B 64 — Artificial Intelligence Regulatory Task Force
short_title: Guam B 64 — Artificial Intelligence Regulatory Task Force
summary: Establishes the Guam Artificial Intelligence (AI) Regulatory Task Force to develop a comprehensive framework for the regulation of artificial intelligence (AI) in the Government of Guam and private sector while protecting Constitutional and Organic Act Rights.

title: Massachusetts S 2516 — Data Privacy Act
short_title: Massachusetts S 2516 — Data Privacy Act
summary: Establishes the Massachusetts data privacy act.

title: Michigan H 4938 — Public Morals
short_title: Michigan H 4938 — Public Morals
summary: Prohibits distribution of certain material.

title: AI Safety Governance Framework Version 2.0 (TC260/CAC)
short_title: AI Safety Framework v2.0
issuing_body: Cyberspace Administration of China; TC260 (National Information Security Standardization Technical Committee)
summary: Upgraded operational version of the 1.0 framework jointly published by TC260 and the Cyberspace Administration of China. Introduces structured risk grading by application scenario and intelligence level, open-source AI governance provisions, and catastrophic risk guidance. Non-binding as a technical document but directly influences regulatory enforcement practice.

title: California S 295 — California Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025
short_title: California S 295 — California Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025
summary: Enacts the California Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025. Prohibits person from distributing or making recommendations based on the use of a pricing algorithm to a specified number or more competitors if the person knows or should know that the pricing algorithm processes competitor data. Establishes an affirmative defense to liability under this prohibition for a person who demonstrates by a preponderance of evidence that they exercised reasonable due diligence.

title: California A 1018 — Automated Decision Systems
short_title: California A 1018 — Automated Decision Systems
topics: General AI governance; Employment & HR; Health; Education; Consumer protection
summary: Requires a deployer of a covered automated decision system to take certain actions, including conduct impact assessments of the covered ADS and provide deployers to whom the developer transfers the covered ADS with certain information, including a high-level summary of the results of those impact assessments.

title: California A 1331 — Workplace Surveillance
short_title: California A 1331 — Workplace Surveillance
summary: Limits the use of workplace surveillance tools by employers, including by prohibiting an employer from monitoring or surveilling workers in employee-only, employer-designated areas. Provides workers with the right to leave behind workplace surveillance tools that are on their person or in their possession during off-duty hours. Prohibits a worker from removing or physically tampering with any component of a workplace surveillance tool that is part of or embedded in employer equipment or vehicles.

title: California S 259 — Fair Online Pricing Act
short_title: California S 259 — Fair Online Pricing Act
summary: Provides that the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018 grants to a consumer various rights with respect to personal information that is collected by a business. Provides for the Fair Online Pricing Act. Prohibits, subject to specified exceptions, a price offered to a consumer through the consumer's online device from being generated, in whole or in part, based on certain input data, including the presence or absence of any software on the online device.

title: OSFI Guideline E-23 — Model Risk Management (Final, September 2025)
short_title: OSFI Guideline E-23 (Model Risk Management)
issuing_body: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI)
summary: OSFI Guideline E-23 is binding guidance for all federally regulated financial institutions (FRFIs) in Canada, explicitly covering AI/ML models. It requires enterprise-wide model risk management frameworks including model identification and inventory, risk ratings, lifecycle governance, validation, and periodic reviews. The guideline also extends coverage to AI/ML models sourced from external vendors. It was finalised September 2025 and takes effect May 2027.

title: California S 503 — Health Care Services: Artificial Intelligence
short_title: California S 503 — Health Care Services: Artificial Intelligence
topics: General AI governance; Health; Consumer protection
summary: Specifies that the Department of Public Health is not required to independently inspect, test, or evaluate the functionality of an artificial intelligence system. Requires, beginning January 1, 2027, developers to provide a report identifying compliance efforts with the specified provisions to the department before making an artificial intelligence system commercially or publicly available to a deployer.

title: Pennsylvania H 1857 — Artificial Intelligence
short_title: Pennsylvania H 1857 — Artificial Intelligence
summary: Requires business entities to disclose the use of artificial intelligence in certain consumer interactions, establishes the right of consumers to human review in high-impact decisions, provides for enforcement by Attorney General.

title: NDRC/NEA Implementation Opinions on "Artificial Intelligence+" Energy Integration
short_title: AI+ Energy Integration
issuing_body: National Development and Reform Commission; National Energy Administration
summary: Quasi-binding sector directive from the National Development and Reform Commission and National Energy Administration implementing the State Council AI+ Initiative in the energy sector. Targets five sector large language models and 100 or more AI-energy application scenarios by 2027. Mandates domestic data storage for AI in energy and integrates AI into grid management, renewable energy forecasting, and energy consumption monitoring.

title: California S 52 — Housing Rental Terms: Algorithmic Devices
short_title: California S 52 — Housing Rental Terms: Algorithmic Devices
summary: Makes it unlawful for any person to sell, license, or provide to a certain number or more persons a rental pricing algorithm with the intent or reasonable expectation that it be used by a specified number or more persons to set rental terms for residential premises. Makes it unlawful for a person to set or adopt rental terms based on the recommendation of a rental pricing algorithm if the person knows or should know that the rental pricing algorithm processes nonpublic competitor data for certain purposes.

title: California S 69 — Artificial Intelligence Program: Attorney General
short_title: California S 69 — Artificial Intelligence Program: Attorney General
topics: Government use of AI; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Requires the Attorney General to establish and maintain a specified program to build internal expertise in artificial intelligence, including its applications, risks, regulatory implications, and civil rights impacts. Requires, on or before the specified date, and annually thereafter, the Attorney General to submit a public report to the Legislature describing the program, key developments in artificial intelligence law and policy, and recommendations for additional State oversight or safeguards.

title: California A 222 — Data Centers: Power Usage Effectiveness: Cost Shifts
short_title: California A 222 — Data Centers: Power Usage Effectiveness: Cost Shifts
summary: Requires the State Energy Resources Conservation and Development Commission to establish a process for the owner of a data center to submit the power usage effectiveness ratio for the data center to the Energy Commission on a biannual basis. Requires the Energy Commission, as part of the 2027 edition of the Integrated Energy Policy Report, to include an assessment of electrical load trends for data centers.

title: California A 279 — School Libraries: Model Library Standards
short_title: California A 279 — School Libraries: Model Library Standards
summary: Provides that existing law requires the State Board of Education to adopt standards, rules, and regulations for school library services. Requires the Superintendent of Public Instruction to consider recommending revisions to the standards for school library services to the State Board. Requires the Superintendent to convene a group of experts to assist the Superintendent in developing revisions. Requires the Superintendent, in consultation with the Instructional Quality Commission, to hold public hearings.

title: California S 384 — Preventing Algorithmic Price Fixing Act: Prohibition
short_title: California S 384 — Preventing Algorithmic Price Fixing Act: Prohibition
summary: Provides for the Preventing Algorithmic Price Fixing Act. Prohibits a person from selling, licensing, providing, or price-setting algorithm with the intent or reasonable expectation that it be used by a specified number or more competitors in the same market if the person knows or should know that the algorithm processes nonpublic data to set either a price or supply level of a good or service or a rent or occupancy level of rental property. Provides a user of such algorithm an affirmative defense.

title: California A 392 — Pornographic Internet Websites: Consent
short_title: California A 392 — Pornographic Internet Websites: Consent
summary: Requires a person who operates a website to exercise ordinary care and reasonable diligence to ensure that any sexually explicit content uploaded to the operator's pornographic internet website does not include a depicted individual. Requires an operator of a pornographic website to verify a user's email address before permitting the user to upload sexually explicit content to the operator's website. Authorizes a depicted individual and a public prosecutor to bring a civil action to enforce such provisions.

title: California A 410 — Bots: Disclosure
short_title: California A 410 — Bots: Disclosure
summary: Requires a person who uses a bot to autonomously communicate with another to ensure that the bot discloses to any person with whom the bot communicates when the bot first communicates with the person that the bot is a bot and not a human being. Authorizes the Attorney General, a district attorney, a county counsel, a city attorney, or a city prosecutor to bring a civil action to punish noncompliance.

title: California S 833 — Critical Infrastructure: Automated Decision Systems
short_title: California S 833 — Critical Infrastructure: Automated Decision Systems
summary: Provides that existing law requires the Technology Recovery Plan element of the State Administrative Manual to ensure the inclusion of cybersecurity strategy incident response standards. Requires an operator responsible for operating, managing, overseeing, or controlling access to critical infrastructure, that deploys a covered artificial intelligence (AI) system to establish a human oversight mechanism that ensures a human monitors the system's operations in real time.

title: California A 887 — Pupil Instruction: High Schools: Computer Science
short_title: California A 887 — Pupil Instruction: High Schools: Computer Science
summary: Establishes the California Computer Science Demonstration Grant Program for specified purposes, including increasing the number of public high schools offering a computer science course to increase pupil access to computer science education and increasing the computer science course access of pupils eligible for free or reduced-priced meals and pupils that are underrepresented in the field of computer science.

title: California A 1242 — Language Access
short_title: California A 1242 — Language Access
summary: Relates to the Dymally-Alatorre Bilingual Services Act. Revises the definition of substantial number of non-English-speaking people to include the higher of either the people served by or eligible to be served by a State agency. Requires the State Health and Human Services Agency to designate a Language Access Director to ensure individuals with limited English proficiency and individuals who are deaf or hard of hearing have meaningful access to government programs and services.

title: California A 1405 — Artificial Intelligence: Auditors: Enrollment
short_title: California A 1405 — Artificial Intelligence: Auditors: Enrollment
summary: Requires the Government Operations Agency to establish a mechanism on the agency's website allowing artificial intelligence auditors to enroll with the agency and allowing natural persons to report misconduct by an enrolled AI auditor. Requires the agency to publish information provided by an enrolled AI auditor on the agency's website, retain specified reports, and share reports submitted by persons reporting misconduct with other State agencies. Requires an AI auditor to enroll with the agency.

title: Colorado Senate Bill 25B-004 — Consumer AI Protections Act Effective Date Amendment
short_title: Colorado SB 25B-004 (AI Act Delay)
issuing_body: Colorado Attorney General
summary: Enacted during a special legislative session, this bill delays the compliance date of Colorado's comprehensive AI law (SB 24-205, Consumer AI Protections Act) from February 1, 2026 to June 30, 2026. The bill makes no substantive changes to SB 24-205's requirements; as of early 2026 that underlying law faces a federal court preliminary injunction on First Amendment grounds.

title: Colorado S 4 — Increase Transparency for Algorithmic Systems
short_title: Colorado S 4 — Increase Transparency for Algorithmic Systems
topics: General AI governance; Health; Consumer protection
summary: Concerns measures effective no later than June 30, 2026, to increase transparency for algorithmic systems.

jurisdiction: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
title: UN General Assembly Resolution A/RES/79/325 — Terms of Reference and Modalities for the Independent International Scientific Panel on AI and the Global Dialogue on AI Governance
short_title: UN Independent International Scientific Panel on AI & Global Dialogue
summary: UN General Assembly resolution adopted by consensus on 26 August 2025 establishing two standing global AI governance mechanisms called for by the Global Digital Compact: a 40-member Independent International Scientific Panel on AI (producing evidence-based scientific assessments of AI risks and opportunities) and a Global Dialogue on AI Governance (an inclusive intergovernmental platform). Panel members were appointed for a 2026-2029 term; the Global Dialogue first convenes in Geneva in 2026.

title: Michigan H 4047 — Civil Actions
short_title: Michigan H 4047 — Civil Actions
summary: Imposes civil liability and prescribe criminal penalties for the nonconsensual creation or dissemination of deep fake sexual images.

title: Michigan H 4048 — Deep Fakes
short_title: Michigan H 4048 — Deep Fakes
summary: Enacts guidelines for dissemination of deep fake sexual images.

title: Illinois S 2398 — Wagering Act
short_title: Illinois S 2398 — Wagering Act
summary: Amends the Sports Wagering Act, prohibits a sports wagering licensee from using artificial intelligence to: track the sports wagers of an individual, creates an offer or promotion targeting a specific individual, or create a gambling product.

title: State Council Opinions on Deepening the "Artificial Intelligence+" Initiative
short_title: AI+ Initiative
issuing_body: State Council
summary: State Council policy document deepening AI integration across six key domains: science and technology, industry, consumption, livelihoods, governance, and global cooperation, with targets through 2035. Sets mandatory integration targets for ministries and subordinate agencies. Quasi-binding in nature as State Council Opinions carry directive force on subordinate government bodies.

title: Illinois S 1507 — State Vehicle Code
short_title: Illinois S 1507 — State Vehicle Code
summary: Provides that the University of Illinois Chicago Urban Transportation Center shall conduct a study that includes, among other things, a comprehensive review of the City of Chicagos website multi year crash data on North and South DuSable Lake Shore Drive, an assessment of the effectiveness of psychological deterrence in reducing habitual speeding, and an assessment of how fatalities can be reduced using cameras powered by artificial intelligence and other technical options in place of cameras powered by AI.

title: Illinois H 1859 — Public Community College Act
short_title: Illinois H 1859 — Public Community College Act
summary: Amends the Public Community College Act, provides that each board of trustees of a community college district shall require the faculty member who teaches a course to be an individual who meets the qualifications in the State Administrative Code and any other applicable rules adopted by the State Community College Board, provides that a course may not, in lieu of a faculty member, use artificial intelligence as the sole source of instruction for students.

title: Illinois S 1920 — School Code and Artificial Intelligence
short_title: Illinois S 1920 — School Code and Artificial Intelligence
summary: Provides that the State Board of Education shall develop statewide guidance for school districts and educators on the use of artificial intelligence in elementary and secondary education, provides that the Superintendent of Education may convene stakeholders for a statewide council to consult on the further development of guidance on the use of AI in schools, provides that the State Board of Education shall encourage school districts to collect teaching resources to support American Sign Language programs.

title: Illinois H 3178 — Digital Voice and Likeness Protection Act
short_title: Illinois H 3178 — Digital Voice and Likeness Protection Act
summary: Provides that a provision in an agreement between an individual and any other person for the performance of personal or professional services is unenforceable only as it relates to a new performance, fixed on or after January 1, 2026, by a digital replica of an individual if specified conditions are satisfied, provides that the failure to include a reasonably specific description of the intended uses of a digital replica shall not render a provision in an agreement unenforceable.

title: Illinois H 3851 — Cyber Bullying
short_title: Illinois H 3851 — Cyber Bullying
summary: Effective July 1, 2026 (applying from the 2026-2027 school year), HB 3851 amends the Illinois School Code so that cyber-bullying includes posting or distributing an unauthorized AI digital replica, including AI-generated sexually explicit images of students. It defines artificial intelligence, generative AI, and digital replica, and establishes the State Bullying and Cyberbullying Prevention Fund.

title: National Artificial Intelligence Policy, 2082 (2025) — Nepal
short_title: Nepal National AI Policy
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of Nepal, Ministry of Communication and Information Technology
summary: Nepal's National AI Policy sets the government's direction for developing and using artificial intelligence. Based on the published summaries, it aims to build AI infrastructure and skills, promote ethical and responsible AI, strengthen data governance, establish institutional arrangements for AI oversight, and prepare legal and regulatory measures. It is a policy framework, not a law, and does not itself create enforceable obligations on private organisations.
scope: Government ministries and agencies implementing the policy; indirectly the private sector, academia and development partners engaged in AI in Nepal. Specific measures, timelines and institutions must be confirmed from the official text.

title: Illinois H 5003 — Wellness and Oversight for Psychological Resources Act
short_title: Illinois H 5003 — Wellness and Oversight for Psychological Resources Act
summary: Amends the Wellness and Oversight for Psychological Resources Act, defines qualified research program, provides that the prohibitions on unauthorized therapy services under the Act shall not apply to artificial intelligence-assisted therapy or psychotherapy services provided exclusively within a qualified research program, sets forth requirements for qualified research programs, requires a licensed professional participating in a qualified research program to perform certain actions.

title: Pennsylvania H 1779 — Algorithmic Pricing Transparency and Fairness
short_title: Pennsylvania H 1779 — Algorithmic Pricing Transparency and Fairness
summary: Amends Title 12 Commerce and Trade of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, in preliminary provisions, provides for algorithmic pricing transparency and fairness, imposes duties on the Office of Attorney General and Bureau of Consumer Protection.

title: Law 2502 of 2025 — AI-Facilitated Identity Fraud Criminal Aggravator
short_title: Colombia AI Criminal Aggravator (Law 2502)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: Fiscalia General de la Nacion (Prosecutor General)
summary: Amends Colombia's Criminal Code to classify the use of AI in identity fraud (deepfakes, digital voice/image impersonation) as a specific criminal aggravating circumstance, increasing applicable prison sentences by up to one-third. Covers AI-enabled identity theft, fraudulent impersonation using synthetic media, and unauthorized use of a person's digital likeness.

title: Illinois H 1806 — Wellness and Oversight for Psychological Resources Act
short_title: Illinois H 1806 — Wellness and Oversight for Psychological Resources Act
summary: Creates the Wellness and Oversight for Psychological Resources Act, adds provisions concerning the permitted use of artificial intelligence under the Act, provides that a licensed professional may not allow an artificial intelligence system to detect emotions or mental states, provides that all records kept by a licensed professional and all communications between an individual seeking therapy or psychotherapy services and a licensed professional shall be confidential.

title: New Hampshire AI Chatbot Child Harm Prevention Act
short_title: New Hampshire HB 143 (Chatbot Child Safety)
issuing_body: New Hampshire Attorney General
summary: Prohibits AI chatbot operators from facilitating or encouraging harmful conduct toward children, including sexual exploitation, illegal drug use, self-harm, and violence. Provides private right of action for minors and parents with $1,000 statutory damages. AG enforcement available after 90-day cure notice.

title: European Union (Artificial Intelligence) (Designation) Regulations 2025 (S.I. No. 366 of 2025)
short_title: Ireland AI Designation Regulations 2025
issuing_body: Data Protection Commission (DPC); Central Bank of Ireland; 15 national competent authorities
summary: Ireland's S.I. 366/2025 implements Article 70 of the EU AI Act by designating 15 national competent authorities across sectors. The Data Protection Commission (DPC) is designated as market surveillance authority for fundamental rights AI obligations. The Minister for Enterprise is Ireland's single point of contact with the EU AI Office.

title: North Carolina H 805 — Prevent Sexual Exploitation of Women and Minors
short_title: North Carolina H 805 — Prevent Sexual Exploitation of Women and Minors
summary: Recognizes two sexes in North Carolina, to prevent the sexual exploitation of women and minors, to limit the use of state funding, to modify the law related to birth certificates, to modify the law related to civil remedies for gender transition procedures on non-minors, to allow students with religious objections to be excused from certain classroom discussions or activities, and to allow parent access to library books and to provide for restrictions on school sleeping quarters.

title: Artificial Intelligence Ethics Principles (Information & eGovernment Authority, Kingdom of Bahrain)
short_title: Bahrain AI Ethics Principles
issuing_body: Information & eGovernment Authority (iGA)
summary: Soft guidance document setting out AI ethics principles published by the Bahrain Information & eGovernment Authority (iGA). Publication date unknown. Full text unavailable at time of record creation.

title: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
short_title: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
issuing_body: The White House (Office of Science and Technology Policy)
summary: America's AI Action Plan is the federal AI strategy mandated by Executive Order 14179. It lists more than 90 policy actions grouped under three pillars: accelerating innovation (including removing regulatory barriers), building AI infrastructure such as data centres and chip fabrication with streamlined permitting, and leading internationally through AI exports and security measures. It was released with accompanying executive orders on federal procurement, data-centre permitting and AI exports.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by The White House (Office of Science and Technology Policy). Oversight: OSTP coordinates; implementation assigned to federal departments and agencies. Stated purpose: Secure US leadership in AI through deregulation, infrastructure build-out and export of American AI.

title: European Commission Guidelines on the Scope of Obligations for Providers of General-Purpose AI Models (Article 53 EU AI Act)
short_title: EU GPAI Guidelines (Art. 53)
issuing_body: EU AI Office; National Competent Authorities
summary: Binding interpretive guidelines published by the European Commission on 18 July 2025 under Article 96 of the EU AI Act, clarifying which AI models qualify as General-Purpose AI Models and the specific compliance obligations for GPAI model providers under Article 53. Establishes the 10²³ FLOPs compute threshold for GPAI model classification and the 10²⁵ FLOPs threshold for systemic risk designation. Covers technical documentation, training data summaries, copyright compliance policies, and incident reporting requirements. Legally distinct from the non-binding GPAI Code of Practice.

title: New Hampshire S 300 — Child Intimate Visual Representations
short_title: New Hampshire S 300 — Child Intimate Visual Representations
summary: Makes it a class B felony and a tier II registrable offense for a person to knowingly create, produce, manufacture or direct an intimate visual representation of a child for prurient purposes, provides that no person shall knowingly create, produce, manufacture, or direct an intimate visual representation of a child for prurient purposes when that child is identifiable from the representation or information displayed in connection with the representation, provides for the registration of criminal offenders.

title: Massachusetts S 323 — Use To Personal Electronic Devices in Schools
short_title: Massachusetts S 323 — Use To Personal Electronic Devices in Schools
summary: Prohibits the use to personal electronic devices in schools.

title: Bank of Russia Code of Ethics for Working with Artificial Intelligence for Financial Organizations (Central Bank of the Russian Federation)
short_title: CBR AI Code of Ethics for Finance
issuing_body: Bank of Russia (Central Bank of the Russian Federation)
summary: The Bank of Russia published a voluntary Code of Ethics for Working with Artificial Intelligence on July 9, 2025, targeting financial organizations operating in the Russian financial sector. The code provides sector-specific guidance on AI governance, transparency, fairness, and accountability, and forms part of the Central Bank's broader AI consultation process. While non-binding, it sets expectations for responsible AI use in finance and aligns with international ethical AI principles adapted to the Russian regulatory context.

title: DIFC Laws Amendment Law, DIFC Law No. 1 of 2025
short_title: DIFC Laws Amendment Law No. 1 of 2025 (Data Protection Amendments)
topics: General AI governance; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: DIFC Commissioner of Data Protection
summary: Omnibus amendment law amending four DIFC laws. Part 2 amends the Data Protection Law 2020: clarifies territorial scope, strengthens data sharing safeguards (validity, proportionality, minimisation), restructures liability provisions, and adds an explicit private right of action for data subjects (new Article 64A). Also adjusts DPIA fine from $50 to $20,000 and data sharing fine from $50 to $10,000. Parts 3–5 amend the Law of Security 2024, Insolvency Law 2019, and Employment Law 2019.

title: Pennsylvania Act 35 of 2025 — Digital Forgery Law (SB 649)
short_title: Pennsylvania Act 35 of 2025 (Digital Forgery Law)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: courts
summary: Pennsylvania's Digital Forgery Law creates the crime of 'digital forgery' — using AI to generate fake voices, images, or videos to injure, exploit, or scam. Misdemeanor for digital impersonation; Felony for fraud. Satire and parody are protected.

title: Pennsylvania S 649 — Digital Forgery
short_title: Pennsylvania S 649 — Digital Forgery
summary: Provides that a person is guilty of digital forgery if, with intent to defraud or injure anyone, the person generates or creates and distributes a forged digital likeness as genuine and knows or reasonably should know the visual representation or audio recording is a forged digital likeness, provides that a violation is a misdemeanor of the first degree, provides exceptions for, among others, constitutionally protected activity and an officer engaged in official duties, provides for affirmative defenses.

jurisdiction: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
title: BRICS Leaders' Statement on the Global Governance of Artificial Intelligence (Rio de Janeiro, July 2025)
short_title: BRICS Leaders' Statement on Global Governance of AI (2025)
summary: First stand-alone consensus declaration on global AI governance adopted at leadership level by BRICS, agreed at the 17th BRICS Summit in Rio de Janeiro on 6 July 2025 by the expanded eleven-member bloc (Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, UAE, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran). It affirms a UN-centred, sovereignty-respecting approach to AI governance, prioritises developing-country participation and data sovereignty, warns against AGI concentration among few actors, and supports inclusive international collaboration. Non-binding.

title: Rhode Island H5872 / S0816 — Prohibition on Deceptive AI Campaign Communications
short_title: Rhode Island H5872 (Election Deepfakes Disclosure)
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: courts
summary: Rhode Island prohibits candidates, parties, and PACs from distributing AI-manipulated media within 90 days of an election without clear disclosure. Allows targeted candidates to seek injunctions and civil damages. Parody and satire exempt.

title: Rhode Island Senate Bill 816 — Deceptive and Fraudulent Synthetic Media in Elections
short_title: Rhode Island S 816 — AI Deepfake Election Fraud
summary: Prohibits creation and distribution of deceptive AI-generated synthetic media designed to influence Rhode Island elections. Creates private right of action and criminal penalties for election-related deepfake fraud.

title: Rhode Island S 136 — Criminal Offenses Regarding Electronic Imaging Devices
short_title: Rhode Island S 136 — Criminal Offenses Regarding Electronic Imaging Devices
summary: Criminalizes the unauthorized dissemination of sexually explicit images of another person that are created by digital devices or created without the consent of the person depicted.

title: Rhode Island H 5046 — Electronic Imaging Devices Criminal Offenses
short_title: Rhode Island H 5046 — Electronic Imaging Devices Criminal Offenses
summary: Criminalizes the unauthorized dissemination of sexually explicit images of another person that are created by digital devices or created without the consent of the person depicted.

title: Maine S 139 — Deed Fraud
short_title: Maine S 139 — Deed Fraud
summary: Establishes the Commission to Recommend Methods for Preventing Deed Fraud in the State to study options for both preventing deed fraud and recompensing the victims of deed fraud, provides for membership, provides that the commission shall, among other things, gather information on the practice and prevalence of deed fraud in the State and examine the sufficiency of State laws and practices related to, among other things, criminal penalties and civil remedies available to victims of deed fraud.

title: Puerto Rico House Joint Resolution 68 — R. C. de la C. 68
short_title: Puerto Rico HJR 68 — AI Study for Anti-Corruption (PRITS)
summary: Orders PRITS to conduct a comprehensive study on the feasibility and benefits of using AI to optimize government auditing, fraud detection, risk mitigation, and expenditure oversight; requires 180-day report to the Governor, Legislature, and oversight agencies.

title: Ohio House Bill 96 (FY2026-27 State Budget) — AI Policy Requirements for Public Schools
short_title: Ohio HB 96 Budget — AI in Schools
issuing_body: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce
summary: Embedded in Ohio's biennial state budget bill; requires every Ohio public school district to adopt a formal AI use policy for students and staff by July 1, 2026. Directs the Ohio Department of Education and Workforce to publish a model AI policy. Creates an AI Integration in Community Colleges Pilot Grant Program. No penalties on students or AI companies — compliance obligation falls on school districts.

title: Connecticut Data Privacy Act Amendment — LLM Training Data Disclosure
short_title: Connecticut PA 25-113 (LLM Training Disclosure)
issuing_body: Connecticut Attorney General
summary: Amends Connecticut Data Privacy Act to require controllers to disclose in privacy notices whether they collect, use, or sell personal data to train large language models. First US state law making LLM training data use a mandatory privacy disclosure element.

title: Michigan H 4667 — Artificial Intelligence
short_title: Michigan H 4667 — Artificial Intelligence
summary: Prohibits use of artificial intelligence to commit certain crimes.

title: Oregon House Bill 2748 — Nurse Title Use Restricted to Humans
short_title: Oregon HB 2748 — AI Cannot Use Protected Professional Titles
summary: Prohibits AI systems from using protected professional titles (such as 'Nurse') in communications with patients or the public. AI health tools must clearly identify themselves as AI and cannot represent themselves as licensed professionals.

title: Oregon House Bill 3936 — Security of State Assets — Artificial Intelligence Systems
short_title: Oregon HB 3936 — AI Security of State Assets
topics: Government use of AI; National security & defence
summary: Establishes security requirements for AI systems used to manage or protect Oregon state assets, data, and infrastructure. Mandates security assessments, access controls, and incident response for AI systems with access to sensitive state information.

title: Pennsylvania H 811 — Fraudulent Misrepresentation of a Candidate Prevention
short_title: Pennsylvania H 811 — Fraudulent Misrepresentation of a Candidate Prevention
summary: Provides for civil liability for fraudulent misrepresentation of candidates, imposes penalties, provides that a covered person shall be liable for the fraudulent misrepresentation of a candidate if, within a specified number of days before an election, the covered person knowingly and intentionally disseminates or causes to be disseminated a campaign advertisement that contains a deepfake, requires disclosures to carry embedded tamper evident digital content provenance for the deepfake content.

title: Puerto Rico S 622 — Artificial Intelligence
short_title: Puerto Rico S 622 — Artificial Intelligence
topics: Government use of AI; Consumer protection
summary: Relates to Transparency and Right to Human Interaction in Public Services Assisted by Artificial Intelligence Act.

title: Rhode Island Senate Bill 1039 — Artificial Intelligence and Employment — Study Commission
short_title: Rhode Island S 1039 — AI and Employment Study
topics: Employment & HR; Government use of AI
summary: Establishes a commission to study the effects of artificial intelligence on employment and workers in Rhode Island. Commission examines workforce impacts, displacement risks, and recommends policies to support workers affected by AI.

title: Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (HB 149, 89th Legislature)
short_title: Texas Responsible AI Governance Act (TRAIGA)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Health; Government use of AI; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: Texas Legislature
summary: Signed on 22 June 2025 and effective 1 January 2026, TRAIGA bans developing or deploying AI systems intended to manipulate people into self-harm or crime, government social scoring, biometric identification by government from public data without consent, intentional unlawful discrimination against protected classes, and production of child sexual abuse material or unlawful sexual deepfakes. State agencies and health-care providers must disclose AI interactions. It creates a 36-month regulatory sandbox administered by the Department of Information Resources, a Texas Artificial Intelligence Council, and gives the Attorney General exclusive enforcement with civil penalties after a 60-day cure period; disparate impact alone does not prove intent to discriminate.
scope: Persons doing business in Texas, producing products used by Texans, or developing or deploying AI systems in Texas, plus state agencies; no private right of action.

title: Maine House Paper 1303a — Threatened Unauthorized Dissemination of Private Intimate Images
short_title: Maine HP 1303a — Non-Consensual AI Intimate Images
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Criminalizes threatened or actual non-consensual dissemination of intimate images, including AI-generated deepfake images. Creates criminal penalties and civil remedies for victims of non-consensual intimate imagery.

title: Pennsylvania H 1625 — Keystone Artificial Intelligence Authority
short_title: Pennsylvania H 1625 — Keystone Artificial Intelligence Authority
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI; Consumer protection
summary: Establishes the Keystone Artificial Intelligence Authority within the Department of Community and Economic Development, provides for the duties of authority and its governing board, provides for duties of other entities, establishes the Artificial Intelligence Permitting System Pilot Program within the Department of Environmental Protection, establishes the Keystone Artificial Intelligence Development Fund, provides for sovereign immunity.

title: Texas Senate Bill 1188 — Healthcare AI Disclosure Act
short_title: Texas SB 1188 (Healthcare AI Disclosure)
issuing_body: Texas Medical Board
summary: Requires Texas healthcare practitioners who use AI for diagnostic purposes to disclose that use to patients verbally or in writing before or at the time of the clinical encounter, covering AI-assisted diagnosis, AI-generated treatment recommendations, and AI interpretation of medical imaging. Also prohibits offshoring of electronic medical records outside the United States.

title: Texas Senate Bill 441 — Unlawful Production or Distribution of Intimate Deepfake Images
short_title: Texas SB 441 (Intimate Deepfake Criminalization)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: Texas state prosecutors
summary: Criminalizes the production or distribution of AI-generated or AI-manipulated intimate images without the depicted person's consent (Class A misdemeanor), elevated to a state jail felony when the depicted person is a minor. Also separately criminalizes threatening to produce or distribute such imagery as a form of sexual coercion.

title: Texas House Bill 581 — Creation of Artificial Sexual Material Harmful to Minors
short_title: Texas HB 581 — AI-Generated Sexual Material Harmful to Minors
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Criminalizes the creation, promotion, or distribution of AI-generated sexual material harmful to minors in Texas. Establishes criminal penalties and extends existing harmful-to-minors statutes to synthetic content.

title: Texas House Bill 2818 — Relating to the Artificial Intelligence Division within the Department of Information Resources
short_title: Texas HB 2818 (AI Division within Dept. of Information Resources)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
summary: Establishes an Artificial Intelligence Division within the Texas Department of Information Resources (DIR) to help state agencies adopt generative AI and modernize legacy state-government computer systems. DIR may develop, procure, or contract for AI technologies (with the majority of contracted work performed by the vendor's AI), and the division must prepare a cost-analysis report for each completed project. Focused on internal state-government modernization rather than private-sector regulation. Signed June 20, 2025; effective September 1, 2025.

title: Texas House Bill 3512 — Artificial Intelligence Training Programs for Government
short_title: Texas HB 3512 — AI Training Programs
summary: Mandates AI literacy and training programs for Texas state government employees. Ensures that government workers using AI tools are trained in responsible use, limitations, and bias awareness.

title: Texas Senate Bill 20 — Obscene Visual Material Appearing to Depict a Child — AI-Generated
short_title: Texas SB 20 — AI-Generated Obscene Material Depicting Children
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Extends Texas obscenity laws to cover AI-generated and synthetic visual material that appears to depict minors in obscene situations. Creates criminal offenses with significant penalties.

title: Texas Senate Bill 815 — Artificial Intelligence in Health Benefit Plan Utilization Review
short_title: Texas SB 815 — AI in Health Benefit Plan Review
summary: Regulates the use of AI in health benefit plan utilization review processes in Texas. Requires health plans to disclose AI use, mandates human clinical oversight for AI-generated adverse determinations, and establishes patient appeal rights.

title: Texas Senate Bill 1621 — Prosecution and Punishment of Crimes Against Children — AI-Generated Content
short_title: Texas SB 1621 — AI-Generated CSAM Prosecution
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Enhances prosecution and penalties for crimes involving AI-generated child sexual abuse material in Texas. Clarifies that AI-generated CSAM is subject to the same criminal laws as traditional CSAM and establishes enhanced penalties.

title: Texas Senate Bill 1964 — Regulation and Use of Artificial Intelligence Systems
short_title: Texas SB 1964 — AI Systems Regulation and Use
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI; Consumer protection
summary: Comprehensive AI regulation establishing a framework for the development, deployment, and use of AI systems in Texas. Addresses consumer protections, risk classifications, transparency requirements, impact assessments, and government AI oversight. Creates accountability mechanisms for high-risk AI applications.

title: Texas Senate Bill 2373 — Financial Exploitation or Abuse of Persons — Artificial Intelligence
short_title: Texas SB 2373 — AI Financial Exploitation of Persons
summary: Addresses the use of AI to facilitate financial exploitation and elder abuse in Texas. Criminalizes and creates civil liability for using AI tools to deceive, manipulate, or defraud vulnerable individuals for financial gain.

title: Texas H 3133 — Deep Fake Material on Social Media Reports
short_title: Texas H 3133 — Deep Fake Material on Social Media Reports
summary: Relates to user reports of explicit deep fake material on social media platforms.

title: Data (Use and Access) Act 2025
short_title: UK Data Use and Access Act 2025
issuing_body: Information Commissioner's Office (ICO)
summary: The UK's Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 fundamentally restructures the UK approach to AI automated decision-making under UK GDPR. It replaces the near-prohibition on sole automated decisions with a broader permission framework tied to legitimate interests, while mandating transparency, right to contest, and human review options. This represents a deliberate post-Brexit divergence from EU GDPR Article 22.

title: Ohio H 362 — Regulate Fraudulent Synthetic Media
short_title: Ohio H 362 — Regulate Fraudulent Synthetic Media
topics: Consumer protection; Law enforcement & justice; Elections
summary: Regulates the dissemination of deceptive and fraudulent synthetic media for the purpose of influencing the results of an election.

title: New York S 2698 — Certification of Filings Produced Using Generative AI
short_title: New York S 2698 — Certification of Filings Produced Using Generative AI
summary: Amends the Civil Practice Law & Rules Law, requires certification of filings produced using generative artificial intelligence, requires the brief of an appellant to contain a disclosure of the use of generative artificial intelligence in the drafting of the brief and certification that the content therein was reviewed and verified by a human.

title: Act to Ensure Transparency in Consumer Transactions Involving Artificial Intelligence
short_title: Maine HP 1154 (Chatbot Transparency)
issuing_body: Maine Attorney General; Maine Department of Consumer Protection
summary: Prohibits AI chatbots from misleading consumers into believing they are interacting with a human without clear conspicuous notice. Violations treated as Unfair Trade Practices Act violations. Separate from LD 2082, which covers mental health specifically.

title: New Hampshire S 263 — Responsive Generative Communication
short_title: New Hampshire S 263 — Responsive Generative Communication
summary: Criminalizes and creates a private right of action for the facilitation, encouragement, offer, solicitation, or recommendation of certain acts or actions through a responsive generative communication to a child.

title: Louisiana House Bill 178 — Civil Procedure — Artificial Intelligence Use
short_title: Louisiana HB 178 — AI in Civil Procedure
topics: Government use of AI; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Addresses the use of AI in Louisiana civil legal proceedings, including authentication requirements for AI-generated evidence and disclosure obligations when AI tools are used in legal practice.

title: Rhode Island S 13 — Use of Artificial Intelligence by Health Insurers
short_title: Rhode Island S 13 — Use of Artificial Intelligence by Health Insurers
summary: Promotes transparency and accountability in the use of artificial intelligence by health insurers to manage coverage and claims.

title: Florida H 1103 — Agency for Persons with Disabilities
short_title: Florida H 1103 — Agency for Persons with Disabilities
summary: Requires the Agency for Person with Disabilities to provide a list of all qualified organizations located within the region in which the client resides and to post its quarterly reconciliation reports on its website within specified timeframes, requires the agency to participate in transition planning activities and to post the total number of individuals in each priority category on its website, establishes the Statewide Family Care Council.

title: Nevada Senate Bill 263 — Pornography Involving Minors — AI-Generated Content
short_title: Nevada SB 263 — AI-Generated CSAM
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Extends Nevada's child pornography laws to include AI-generated and synthetic depictions of minors. Criminalizes creation, distribution, and possession of AI-generated CSAM.

title: Nevada Assembly Bill 406 — Prohibition on AI in Mental/Behavioral Healthcare
short_title: Nevada AB 406 (Healthcare AI Prohibition)
issuing_body: Nevada State Board of Examiners for Marriage and Family Therapists and Clinical Professional Counselors; Nevada Board of Psychological Examiners
summary: Nevada enacts the first broad US prohibition on AI systems providing professional mental or behavioral healthcare services. Bars AI platforms from acting as or substituting for licensed therapists, counselors, and psychiatrists. Restricts licensed professionals from using AI in ways that replace clinical judgment in therapeutic settings.

title: Nevada S 213 — Unlawful Dissemination of an Intimate Image
short_title: Nevada S 213 — Unlawful Dissemination of an Intimate Image
summary: Relates to the unlawful dissemination of an intimate image, includes the distribution of certain photorealistic images, digital images, computer images and computer generated images, provides that a person commits unlawful dissemination of an intimate image when, with the intent to harass, harm or terrorize, the person distributes an intimate image if the image is created in a way that would lead a reasonable person to believe it is an actual depiction of the person depicted and the person did not consent.

title: Nebraska Legislative Bill 77 — Ensuring Transparency in Prior Authorization Act
short_title: Nebraska LB 77 — AI Prior Authorization Transparency
summary: Requires health insurers in Nebraska to disclose when AI is used in prior authorization decisions and mandates human clinical review for AI-generated coverage denials. Establishes notification and appeal rights for patients.

title: Nebraska L 77 — Ensuring Transparency in Prior Authorization Act
short_title: Nebraska L 77 — Ensuring Transparency in Prior Authorization Act
topics: Health; Government use of AI; Consumer protection
summary: Relates to insurance, adopts the Ensuring Transparency in Prior Authorization Act, provides for insurance and Medicaid coverage of biomarker testing as prescribed, provides operative dates, provides severability.

title: Hawaii Senate Bill 742 — Data Sharing and Governance Working Group
short_title: Hawaii SB 742 — Data Sharing and AI Governance Working Group
summary: Establishes a working group to study and recommend policies for data sharing and AI governance in Hawaii state government. Focuses on interoperability, privacy protections, and AI accountability.

title: Nevada Assembly Bill 73 — Elections — Prohibition on AI Deepfake Election Content
short_title: Nevada AB 73 — AI Deepfakes in Elections
summary: Prohibits the creation and distribution of AI-generated deepfakes designed to influence Nevada elections without clear disclosure. Establishes penalties for deceptive AI election content and requires labeling of AI-generated political media.

title: Colorado Senate Bill 288 — Intimate Digital Depictions — Criminal and Civil Actions
short_title: Colorado SB 288 — AI Intimate Digital Depictions
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Establishes criminal and civil liability for creating or distributing non-consensual AI-generated intimate images of identifiable individuals. Creates private right of action for victims.

title: Illinois H 35 — Artificial Intelligence Systems and Health Insurance
short_title: Illinois H 35 — Artificial Intelligence Systems and Health Insurance
summary: Creates the Artificial Intelligence Systems Use in Health Insurance Act, provides that the Department of Insurances regulatory oversight of health insurance coverage includes oversight of the use of AI systems or predictive models to make or support adverse consumer outcomes, provides that the departments authority in an investigation or market conduct action includes review regarding the development, implementation, and use of AI systems or predictive models and the outcomes from the use of such systems.

title: Illinois H 3646 — Innovation and Technology Act
short_title: Illinois H 3646 — Innovation and Technology Act
summary: Amends the Department of Innovation and Technology Act, provides that the Generative AI and Natural Language Processing Task Force may hold public meetings in a hybrid format, with both virtual and in-person options to attend, as frequently as necessary to carry out its duties and shall convene and meet at the call of the co-chairpersons, provides that the Task Force shall file periodic reports with the Governor and the General Assembly covering the Task Force's investigation into generative artificial.

title: Florida House Bill 757 — Criminal Prohibition on Nonconsensual AI-Generated Sexually Explicit Imagery
short_title: Florida HB 757 (AI Deepfake Criminal Prohibition)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: Florida state prosecutors; Florida courts (civil)
summary: Makes it a third-degree felony (up to 5 years) to willfully create, solicit, or possess with intent to promote nonconsensual AI-generated sexually explicit imagery of an identifiable person, covering both wholly synthetic and AI-manipulated imagery. Also creates a civil cause of action for victims to seek actual damages, injunctive relief, and attorney's fees.

title: Florida House Bill 1161 (Brooke's Law) — Platform Obligations for Deepfake Intimate Image Removal
short_title: Florida HB 1161 (Brooke's Law)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: Florida courts (civil)
summary: Named after Brooke Shields, this law requires online platforms to establish accessible victim-reporting mechanisms for nonconsensual deepfake intimate images and to remove confirmed content within 48 hours of a valid report. Platform failure to maintain the reporting mechanism or to timely remove confirmed content creates civil liability.

jurisdiction: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
title: ISO/IEC 42005:2025 — Information Technology — Artificial Intelligence — AI System Impact Assessment
short_title: ISO/IEC 42005:2025 — AI System Impact Assessment
summary: ISO/IEC 42005:2025 is a voluntary international standard providing a methodology for organizations to assess potential societal and individual impacts (both benefits and harms) of AI systems across their lifecycle.
