title: Arkansas House Bill 1877 — Criminal Offenses — AI-Generated Child Sexual Abuse Material
short_title: Arkansas HB 1877 — AI-Generated CSAM Criminal Offenses
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Establishes criminal offenses for creating, distributing, or possessing AI-generated child sexual abuse material. Applies existing CSAM laws to synthetic and AI-generated depictions.

title: Maryland Senate Bill 360 — Nonconsensual Deepfake Intimate Imagery Act
short_title: Maryland SB 360 (Deepfake Intimate Imagery)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: Maryland state prosecutors; Maryland courts (civil)
summary: Expands Maryland's existing nonconsensual intimate image law to expressly cover AI-generated and digitally manipulated deepfake intimate images; adds a civil cause of action allowing victims to sue for damages, attorney's fees, and injunctive relief. Passed unanimously (47-0 Senate, 140-0 House).

title: Maryland House Bill 956 — Workgroup on Artificial Intelligence Implementation
short_title: Maryland HB 956 — Workgroup on AI Implementation
summary: Establishes a workgroup to study the implementation of AI in private sector industries in Maryland. Examines economic impacts, workforce displacement risks, and best practices for responsible AI deployment.

title: North Dakota S 2186 — Removal or Withholding of a Child
short_title: North Dakota S 2186 — Removal or Withholding of a Child
summary: Relates to interference with court-ordered parenting time, creates a child custody review task force, provides for a legislative management report, provides a penalty.

title: Rhode Island H 5923 — Criminal Offenses Regarding Children Exploitation
short_title: Rhode Island H 5923 — Criminal Offenses Regarding Children Exploitation
summary: Prohibits the distribution, transfer, or possession of any material that depicts a minor engaging in sexually explicit conduct, is obscene and lacks serious literary, artistic, political, or scientific value with violators subject to imprisonment and fines ranging from two (2) to fifteen (15) years and fines from one thousand dollars ($1,000) to five thousand dollars ($5,000).

title: Arkansas House Bill 1876 — Model Training and Content Generated by Generative AI
short_title: Arkansas HB 1876 — Generative AI Training Data and Content Disclosure
summary: Requires disclosure when content is generated by AI models and establishes transparency requirements for AI training data. Mandates labeling of AI-generated content for commercial use.

title: Arkansas Senate Bill 612 — Private Right of Action Against Social Media Platforms for AI Harms
short_title: Arkansas SB 612 — Social Media AI Private Right of Action
summary: Establishes a private right of action for individuals harmed by AI systems deployed on social media platforms. Allows affected persons to sue platforms for AI-related harms including algorithmic manipulation and non-consensual AI-generated content.

title: North Dakota House Bill 1386 — Computer Generated Images — Child Sexual Exploitation
short_title: North Dakota HB 1386 — AI-Generated CSAM
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Expands North Dakota's sexual exploitation laws to include AI-generated and computer-generated images of minors. Criminalizes creation, distribution, and possession of AI-generated CSAM.

title: North Dakota House Bill 1429 — Harassment and Stalking with a Robot or AI System
short_title: North Dakota HB 1429 — AI Robot Harassment and Stalking
topics: General AI governance; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Creates criminal offenses for using robots, AI systems, or automated tools to harass or stalk individuals. Extends existing harassment and stalking laws to AI-enabled conduct.

title: Arizona House Bill 2342 — Blockchain Technology and AI Oversight
short_title: Arizona HB 2342 — AI/Blockchain Governance
summary: Establishes governance framework for government and private sector use of blockchain technology and AI systems in Arizona. Addresses oversight, interoperability, and accountability.

title: Colorado S 143 — Extend Prohibition on School Facial Recognition
short_title: Colorado S 143 — Extend Prohibition on School Facial Recognition
summary: Concerns the limited use of facial recognition services by schools, provides that for a product, device, or software application that allows for analysis of facial features for educational purposes in conjunction with curricula, allows for the analysis of facial features to identify a person who has made a significant threat against a school or the occupants of a school, or to identify a missing student.

title: Arkansas House Bill 1958 — Public Entities Required to Create AI Use Policy
short_title: Arkansas HB 1958 — Government AI Policy Requirement
summary: Requires Arkansas state agencies and public entities to establish written policies governing the use of artificial intelligence. Policies must address accountability, transparency, and appropriate use limitations.

title: Arkansas H 1529 — Deepfake Visual Material of a Sexual Nature
short_title: Arkansas H 1529 — Deepfake Visual Material of a Sexual Nature
summary: Concerns deepfake visual material of a sexual nature, creates the criminal offense of unlawful creation and distribution of deepfake visual material, establishes a cause of action for unlawful creation of deepfake visual material, provides that engaging in sexual contact, sexual intercourse, deviate sexual activity, or sexually explicit conduct such that an ordinary person viewing the deepfake visual material would conclude that the depiction is of the identifiable person engaging in sexual contact.

title: Montana Right to Compute Act
short_title: Montana SB 212 (Right to Compute Act)
topics: General AI governance; National security & defence
issuing_body: Montana courts
summary: Establishes a fundamental right to privately own and use computational resources in Montana. Any government restriction on computing resources must be narrowly tailored and demonstrably necessary. Requires AI-controlled critical infrastructure operators to develop NIST-based risk management policies and annual safety reviews.

title: New York S 185 — Automated Employment Decision Tools
short_title: New York S 185 — Automated Employment Decision Tools
topics: General AI governance; Employment & HR; Consumer protection
summary: Amends the labor law, in relation to restricting the use of electronic monitoring and automated employment decision tools and to amend the civil rights law, in relation to making a conforming change.

title: Hawaii H 716 — Health Infrastructure Grant Program
short_title: Hawaii H 716 — Health Infrastructure Grant Program
summary: Establishes the Health Information Technology Infrastructure Grant Program within the Department of Health, to be administered by the State Health Planning and Development Agency, to support health information technology infrastructure and the implementation of interoperable health information technologies in federally qualified health centers, rural health clinics, Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program centers, and Native Hawaiian health centers.

title: North Dakota H 1410 — Legislative Management Study
short_title: North Dakota H 1410 — Legislative Management Study
summary: Provides that, during the specified interim, the Legislative Management shall consider studying State laws relating to criminal conduct against children, child sexual abuse, child physical abuse, child neglect, and human trafficking of children, provides that the study must include a review of, among other things, the use of the term child sexually abusive material instead of the term sexual performance to describe child pornography or sexual conduct of a minor.

title: Washington Forged Digital Likeness Act
short_title: Washington HB 1205 (Forged Digital Likeness)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media
issuing_body: Washington law enforcement; Washington courts (civil and criminal)
summary: Broadly criminalizes forged digital likenesses — AI-manipulated audio or video indistinguishable from genuine and likely to deceive. Applies to creation and distribution. Provides both criminal (gross misdemeanor) and civil ($3,000/violation) remedies. Carve-outs for satire, public interest, and fair use.

title: Illinois H 1918 — Managed Care Reform and Patient Rights Act
short_title: Illinois H 1918 — Managed Care Reform and Patient Rights Act
summary: Amends the Managed Care Reform and Patient Rights Act, provides that any intergovernmental joint self-insurance pool providing health benefits under a specified provision of the Intergovernmental Cooperation Act shall not be included under the definition of health care plan.

title: North Carolina H 970 — Preventing Algorithmic Rent Fixing
short_title: North Carolina H 970 — Preventing Algorithmic Rent Fixing
summary: Prevents algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market.

title: North Carolina H 1002 — Rate Payer Protection Act
short_title: North Carolina H 1002 — Rate Payer Protection Act
summary: Prohibits passing any grid or energy costs incurred solely for serving data centers to rate payers, creates a special commission for data center planning.

title: North Carolina H 1004 — Technology Hubs
short_title: North Carolina H 1004 — Technology Hubs
summary: Appropriates funds to establish artificial intelligence hubs at select constituent institutions of the University of North Carolina, appropriates funds to establish technology hubs at each constituent institution of the University of North Carolina and for the state Collaboratory to establish a grant program for research projects on artificial intelligence.

title: Guide on Artificial Intelligence Governance and Ethics for Brunei Darussalam
short_title: Brunei AI Governance & Ethics Guide 2025
summary: Voluntary national AI governance guide issued by AITI (public consultation July 2024). Seven guiding principles: transparency and explainability, security and safety, fairness and equity, data protection and governance, robustness and reliability, human centricity, and accountability and integrity. Aligned with the ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics. Brunei's principal national AI governance instrument.

title: Illinois Artificial Intelligence Video Interview Act (820 ILCS 42)
short_title: Illinois AI Video Interview Act
issuing_body: Illinois General Assembly
summary: In force since 1 January 2020, the Act requires employers that use AI to analyse video interviews of applicants for Illinois-based positions to notify applicants, explain how the AI works and what characteristics it evaluates, obtain consent, limit sharing of videos, and delete videos on request within 30 days; a 2022 amendment requires employers relying solely on AI to decide who gets an in-person interview to report demographic data annually.
scope: Employers using AI analysis of video interviews for positions based in Illinois.

title: Illinois S 150 — Election Code and AI Advert Disclosure
short_title: Illinois S 150 — Election Code and AI Advert Disclosure
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Consumer protection; Elections
summary: Amends the Election Code, provides that, if a person, committee, or other entity, creates, originally publishes, or originally distributes a qualified political advertisement, the qualified political advertisement, includes in a clear and conspicuous manner, a statement that the qualified political advertisement, generates in whole or substantially by artificial intelligence, satisfies specified requirements, provides for civil penalties and exceptions to the provision.

title: Illinois S 1425 — Artificial Intelligence Systems and Health Insurance
short_title: Illinois S 1425 — Artificial Intelligence Systems and Health Insurance
topics: General AI governance; Health; Consumer protection
summary: Creates the Artificial Intelligence Systems Use in Health Insurance Act, provides that the Department of Insurance's regulatory oversight of insurers includes oversight of an insurer's use of AI systems to make or support adverse determinations that affect consumers, provides that any insurer authorized to operate in the State is subject to review by the Department in an investigation or market conduct action regarding the development, implementation, and use of AI systems or predictive models.

title: Illinois S 1554 — Artificial Intelligence
short_title: Illinois S 1554 — Artificial Intelligence
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Amends the Criminal Code of 2012, provides that certain forms of false impersonation may be accomplished by artificial intelligence, defines artificial intelligence.

title: Illinois S 1556 — Artificial Intelligence and School Code
short_title: Illinois S 1556 — Artificial Intelligence and School Code
summary: Amends the School Code, requires the State Board of Education to establish the State Instructional Technology Advisory Board, which shall collaborate with the State Board of Education to provide guidance, integration, oversight, and evaluation of education technologies, including, but not limited to, artificial intelligence technologies, sets forth the membership of the Advisory Board and terms.

title: Illinois S 1677 — Evaluation of Certified Employees Article
short_title: Illinois S 1677 — Evaluation of Certified Employees Article
summary: Amends the Evaluation of Certified Employees Article of the School Code, provides that a teacher evaluation plan, prohibits an evaluator from using artificial intelligence tools, performs teacher evaluation tasks.

title: Illinois S 1792 — Consumer Fraud and Deceptive Business Practices Act
short_title: Illinois S 1792 — Consumer Fraud and Deceptive Business Practices Act
summary: Amends the Consumer Fraud and Deceptive Business Practices Act, provides that the owner, licensee, or operator of a generative artificial intelligence system shall conspicuously display a warning on the system's user interface that is reasonably calculated to consistently apprise the user that the outputs of the generative artificial intelligence system may be inaccurate or inappropriate, provides that a violation of the provision constitutes an unlawful practice within the meaning of the Act.

title: Illinois S 1929 — Provenance Data Requirements Act
short_title: Illinois S 1929 — Provenance Data Requirements Act
summary: Creates the Provenance Data Requirements Act, provides that a generative artificial intelligence tool provider shall apply provenance data, either directly or through the use of third-party technology, to wholly-generated synthetic content generated by the provider's generative artificial intelligence tool, sets forth additional requirements on generative artificial intelligence tool providers, large online platforms, and manufacturers of capture devices, defines terms.

title: Illinois S 2203 — Preventing Algorithmic Discrimination Act
short_title: Illinois S 2203 — Preventing Algorithmic Discrimination Act
summary: Creates the Preventing Algorithmic Discrimination Act, provides that, on or before January 1, 2027, and annually thereafter, a deployer of an automated decision tool shall perform an impact assessment for any automated decision tool the deployer uses or designs, codes, or produces that includes specified information, provides that a deployer shall, at or before the time an automated decision tool is used to make a consequential decision, notify any natural person.

title: Illinois S 2259 — Medical Practice Act
short_title: Illinois S 2259 — Medical Practice Act
summary: Amends the Medical Practice Act, defines terms, provides that a health facility, clinic, physician's office, or office of a group practice that uses generative artificial intelligence to generate written or verbal patient communications pertaining to patient clinical information shall ensure that the communications meet certain criteria, provides that a communication that is generated by generative artificial intelligence and read and reviewed by a human licensed or certified health care provider.

title: Illinois H 3689 — Preventing Sexual Violence in Higher Education Act
short_title: Illinois H 3689 — Preventing Sexual Violence in Higher Education Act
summary: Amends the Preventing Sexual Violence in Higher Education Act, makes changes concerning definitions, requires a higher education institution's comprehensive policy to include digital sexual harassment and doxing, makes changes concerning the components of the comprehensive policy and the notification of a survivor's rights and options, including providing a summary of the higher education institution's process for protecting survivors from retaliation.

title: North Dakota House Bill 1167 — Artificial Intelligence in Political Communications Disclosure Act
short_title: North Dakota HB 1167 (AI Political Disclosure)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: County State's Attorney; North Dakota AG
summary: Requires political communications or advertisements created wholly or in part by AI to carry a prominent 'This content generated by artificial intelligence' disclaimer. Applies to paid political ads and mass communications. Misdemeanor criminal penalty for violations. Exempts spell-check/autocorrect tools and clearly labeled satire/parody.

title: North Dakota House Bill 1351 — Nonconsensual Distribution of Intimate Deepfakes Prohibition
short_title: North Dakota HB 1351 (Deepfake NCII)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children

summary: Creates criminal offense and civil cause of action for creating or distributing nonconsensual AI-generated or digitally altered sexually explicit images of identifiable persons. Criminal penalty escalates from Class A misdemeanor (first offense) to Class C felony (subsequent violations). Victims may seek civil damages and injunctive relief.

title: Pennsylvania S 631 — Virtual Mental Health Services
short_title: Pennsylvania S 631 — Virtual Mental Health Services
summary: Provides for parental consent for virtual mental health services provided by a school entity.

title: Tennessee H 825 — Curriculum Education
short_title: Tennessee H 825 — Curriculum Education
summary: Enacts the Teen Social Media and Internet Safety Act, which requires the Department of Education to develop guidance for LEAs and public charter schools to instruct students in grades six through twelve who are enrolled in the LEA or public charter school on social media and internet safety, prohibit students from accessing a social media platform using the internet access provided by the LEA or public charter school, except when expressly authorized by a teacher for educational purposes only.

title: Arkansas House Bill 1071 — Publicity Rights Protection Act Extension to AI
short_title: Arkansas HB 1071 (Digital Identity Protection)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Copyright & IP
issuing_body: Private civil action; Arkansas Attorney General
summary: Arkansas extends its Publicity Rights Protection Act to explicitly cover AI-generated images, voice replicas, and digital likenesses. Prohibits commercial use of a person's AI-generated likeness without consent. Part of Arkansas's 2025 legislative expansion addressing AI-generated identity exploitation.

title: North Dakota H 1204 — False Information in Political Advertisements
short_title: North Dakota H 1204 — False Information in Political Advertisements
summary: Provides that a person is guilty of a class A misdemeanor if the person knowingly publishes a political advertisement or news release containing an assertion, representation, or statement of fact which is untrue, deceptive, or misleading, on behalf of or in opposition to any candidate for public office, measure, constitutional amendment, or issue on an election ballot, which is published by, among other things, radio, television, newspaper, text message, telephone call, social media, or other public means.

title: Pennsylvania H 1188 — Electronic Devices
short_title: Pennsylvania H 1188 — Electronic Devices
summary: Amends Title 71 (State Government) of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, provides for protection of state-owned electronic devices and networks from applications controlled by foreign adversaries.

title: Rhode Island H 5434 — Protect Patients and Traditional Medicare
short_title: Rhode Island H 5434 — Protect Patients and Traditional Medicare
summary: (Resolution) Urges the United States Congress to protect patients and traditional Medicare from Medicare advantage.

title: South Carolina H 3045 — Obscene Visual Representations of Child Sexual Abuse
short_title: South Carolina H 3045 — Obscene Visual Representations of Child Sexual Abuse
summary: Creates the offense of obscene visual representations of child sexual abuse, define necessary terms, and establish penalties, relates to the sex offender registry, adds the offense of obscene visual representations of child sexual abuse to the sex offender registry, relates to termination of registration requirements, clarifies possible termination requirements and include tier I and tier II designations for out-of-state or federal convictions.

title: South Carolina H 3046 — Offenses Against Minors
short_title: South Carolina H 3046 — Offenses Against Minors
summary: Relates to definitions applicable to certain offenses against minors, revises definitions and add the terms identifiable minor and morphed image, relates to first degree sexual exploitation of a minor, includes morphed images of identifiable minors as an offense, relates to second degree sexual exploitation of a minor, includes morphed images of identifiable minors as an offense, relates to third degree sexual exploitation of a minor, includes morphed images.

title: New Mexico House Bill 20 — Technology and Innovation Division — AI Governance
short_title: New Mexico HB 20 — Technology and Innovation AI Division
summary: Creates or expands the Technology and Innovation Division to include oversight of AI systems used by state agencies. Division coordinates AI policy, standards, and implementation across New Mexico government.

title: Kansas Senate Substitute for HB 2313 (Chapter 84, 2025) — Foreign Adversary AI Platform Prohibition
short_title: Kansas HB 2313 (Foreign AI Platform Prohibition)
topics: General AI governance; National security & defence
issuing_body: Kansas Office of Information Technology Services
summary: Kansas prohibits state agencies from using AI platforms owned by foreign adversaries (China, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia, Venezuela) on state networks or devices. Specifically names DeepSeek. Also bars state-funded medical/research facilities from using genetic sequencers from foreign adversaries.

title: Kansas H 2313 — Technology Produced by Certain Foreign Countries
short_title: Kansas H 2313 — Technology Produced by Certain Foreign Countries
summary: Relates to artificial intelligence platforms, prohibits the use of artificial intelligence platforms of concern on State issued devices and networks, prohibits medical and research facilities from using genetic sequencers or operational software used for genetic analysis that is produced in or by a foreign adversary, provides that any State agency that utilizes an AI platform of concern or has an account with such platform shall deactivate and delete such account and shall no longer use the platform.

title: Rhode Island S 56 — Protect Patients and Traditional Medicare
short_title: Rhode Island S 56 — Protect Patients and Traditional Medicare
summary: (Resolution) Urges the United States Congress to protect patients and traditional Medicare from Medicare advantage.

title: Montana House Bill 82 — Crimes Against Children — AI-Generated Sexual Exploitation Material
short_title: Montana HB 82 — AI-Generated CSAM
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Extends Montana's child sexual exploitation laws to cover AI-generated and synthetic images of minors. Criminalizes creation, distribution, and possession of AI-generated child sexual abuse material with penalties equivalent to traditional CSAM.

title: Pennsylvania H 1167 — Solar Radiation Modification
short_title: Pennsylvania H 1167 — Solar Radiation Modification
topics: Government use of AI; Consumer protection; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Prohibits solar radiation modification or sunlight reflection methods, cloud seeding and polluting atmospheric interventions within this Commonwealth, imposes duties on the state Police and sheriffs, imposes penalties.

title: North Carolina H 723 — Technology Coalitions Strategic Support Fund
short_title: North Carolina H 723 — Technology Coalitions Strategic Support Fund
topics: Education; Government use of AI; Consumer protection
summary: Establishes the State Technology Coalitions Strategic Support Fund.

title: Pennsylvania H 1125 — Automated License Plate Reader Systems
short_title: Pennsylvania H 1125 — Automated License Plate Reader Systems
summary: Amends Title 75 of the State Consolidated Statutes, in operation of vehicles, provides for automated license plate reader systems.

title: OMB Memorandum M-25-21: Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust
short_title: OMB M-25-21
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Office of Management and Budget, Executive Office of the President
summary: M-25-21 directs US federal agencies on how to govern and use AI. It requires agencies to designate Chief AI Officers, maintain AI governance boards, publish AI use-case inventories, and apply minimum risk-management practices to "high-impact" AI, including pre-deployment testing, AI impact assessments, ongoing monitoring, human oversight and training, and remedies for affected individuals. It replaced the 2024 memoranda with a greater emphasis on adoption and innovation while retaining core risk practices.
scope: Applies to federal executive agencies' development, acquisition and use of AI, with exceptions for national security systems and certain research. It does not bind private organisations but sets the expectations vendors must meet to sell AI to federal agencies.

title: New Jersey P.L. 2025, c.40 — Deepfake Civil and Criminal Penalties
short_title: New Jersey A3540 (Deepfakes Civil and Criminal Penalties)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: courts
summary: New Jersey's deepfake law establishes criminal penalties (3rd degree crime, up to $30,000 fine) for making or distributing deceptive AI deepfakes to further additional criminal activity. Creates civil cause of action for victims. Passed unanimously in both chambers.

title: New Jersey S 2544 — Deceptive Audio or Visual Media
short_title: New Jersey S 2544 — Deceptive Audio or Visual Media
summary: Establishes criminal penalties for production or dissemination of deceptive audio or visual media, commonly known as deepfakes, clarifies certain free speech exceptions applicable to interactive computer service providers, cloud services providers, commercial developers or providers of artificial intelligence technology, advertisers, the news media, and other media companies.

title: New Jersey A 3838 — Deceptive Audio or Visual Media
short_title: New Jersey A 3838 — Deceptive Audio or Visual Media

short_title: Ohio S 164 — Artificial Intelligence Use By Health Insurers
summary: Regulates the use of artificial intelligence by health insurers.

title: Virginia House Bill 1642 — Criminal Justice Risk Assessments — Artificial Intelligence
short_title: Virginia HB 1642 — AI in Criminal Justice Risk Assessments
topics: Government use of AI; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Establishes standards for the use of AI-driven risk assessment tools in Virginia criminal justice proceedings. Addresses pretrial detention decisions, sentencing, and parole. Requires transparency, bias auditing, and limits on how AI risk scores are used.

title: Virginia H 2692 — Custodial Interrogations
short_title: Virginia H 2692 — Custodial Interrogations
topics: Government use of AI; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Relates to custodial interrogations, relates to false statements to a child prohibited, relates to inauthentic replica documents, prohibits law-enforcement officers from intentionally making false statements or materially misrepresenting any fact, including by use of inauthentic replica documents, prior to or during a custodial interrogation of a child to secure the cooperation, confession, or conviction of such child, defines inauthentic replica documents as any documents, including computer.

title: Cybersecurity Technology — Generative AI Training Data Security Standards (Three-Part)
short_title: China GenAI Training Data Standards
issuing_body: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR); Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC)
summary: Three national standards establish security requirements for GenAI training data: annotation security procedures, pre-training and fine-tuning data requirements, and basic service security standards. Mandate minimal use of 'unsafe' data, require regular model testing, and specify data provenance documentation.

title: North Carolina S 514 — Social Media Control
short_title: North Carolina S 514 — Social Media Control
summary: Combats social media addiction by requiring that social media platforms respect the privacy of North Carolina users' data and not use a North Carolina minor's data for advertising or algorithmic recommendations, appropriates funds for that purpose, makes willful violations of data user privacy an unfair practice under specified statutes.

title: Oman General Policy for the Safe and Ethical Use of Artificial Intelligence Systems (MTCIT)
short_title: Oman General Policy for Safe and Ethical AI 2025
issuing_body: Oman Ministry of Transport, Communications and Information Technology (MTCIT)
summary: A quasi-binding ministerial circular from Oman's MTCIT applying to public entities and relevant private-sector actors. Covers security, ethics, transparency, data privacy, and bias mitigation requirements for AI system deployment. Represents Oman's most operationally detailed AI governance instrument to date.

title: Qatar MCIT Principles and Guidelines for Ethical Use and Development of Artificial Intelligence (2025)
short_title: Qatar MCIT Ethical AI Guidelines 2025
issuing_body: Qatar Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT)
summary: Two complementary non-binding documents from Qatar's Ministry of Communications and Information Technology on ethical AI use and ethical AI development and deployment. Organized around eight pillars: do no harm, robustness and security, fairness, transparency, privacy, sustainability, human oversight, and accountability. Intended as a voluntary framework for public and private sector AI actors.

title: Rhode Island H 5172 — Transparency and Accountability of Health Insurers
short_title: Rhode Island H 5172 — Transparency and Accountability of Health Insurers
summary: Promotes transparency and accountability in the use of artificial intelligence by health insurers to manage coverage and claims.

title: Tennessee H 433 — Criminal Offenses
short_title: Tennessee H 433 — Criminal Offenses
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Expands the offense of unlawful exposure to include the distribution, with the intent to cause emotional distress, of an image of the intimate parts of another identifiable person or an image of an identifiable person engaged in sexually explicit conduct and the image was created or modified by means of a computer software program, artificial intelligence application, or other digital editing tools.

title: South Dakota Senate Bill 164 — Prohibition on Unlabeled AI-Generated Deepfakes to Influence Elections
short_title: South Dakota SB 164 (Election Deepfakes)

title: Utah Senate Bill 271 — Unauthorized Artificial Intelligence Impersonation
short_title: Utah SB 271 — AI Unauthorized Impersonation

short_title: North Carolina S 530 — Agricultural Manufacturing
summary: Provides for economic development incentives targeted for agricultural manufacturing.

short_title: North Carolina S 619 — Artificial Intelligence Academic Support Grant Program
summary: Establishes the artificial intelligence academic support grant program, appropriates funds for that purpose.

short_title: North Carolina S 624 — Artificial Intelligence Chatbots

summary: Regulates artificial intelligence chatbot licensing, safety, and privacy in the State.

short_title: North Carolina S 640 — Artificial Intelligence In Schools
summary: Requires instruction on artificial intelligence in schools.

title: North Carolina S 735 — Artificial Intelligence Innovation Trust Fund
short_title: North Carolina S 735 — Artificial Intelligence Innovation Trust Fund
summary: Enacts the artificial intelligence innovation trust fund.

title: North Carolina S 738 — Digital Content Provenance
short_title: North Carolina S 738 — Digital Content Provenance
summary: Creates the digital content provenance initiative, appropriates funds for that purpose.

title: North Carolina S 746 — Study Automation and the Workforce
short_title: North Carolina S 746 — Study Automation and the Workforce
summary: Establishes the study committee on automation and the workforce.

short_title: Utah HB 452 (Mental Health Chatbot Disclosure)

summary: Promulgated jointly by the CAC, MIIT, Ministry of Public Security, and SART on March 7, 2025 and effective September 1, 2025, these Measures operationalize content labeling obligations for AI-generated synthetic content (text, images, audio, video, virtual scenes) across the Chinese internet ecosystem. summary: Provides that a person commits the offense of unlawful creation or distribution of a sexually explicit deepfake if the person knowingly and without the consent of the depicted individual creates, distributes to, exhibits to, or exchanges with others or offers to distribute to, exhibit to, or exchange with others a deepfake that depicts an individual nude or personally engaging in sexual conduct, provides that unlawful creation or distribution of a sexually explicit deepfake is a misdemeanor.

jurisdiction: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
title: Hiroshima AI Process (HAIP) Reporting Framework for Organisations Developing Advanced AI Systems
short_title: G7 Hiroshima AI Process (HAIP) Reporting Framework
summary: Voluntary transparency reporting framework launched by the OECD on 7 February 2025 to operationalize and monitor application of the G7 Hiroshima Process International Code of Conduct for advanced AI developers. Organisations across the AI value chain submit standardized reports (inaugural deadline 15 April 2025, annual updates thereafter) published on the OECD.AI Policy Observatory. Initial signatories include Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, OpenAI, Amazon, Salesforce, Fujitsu, NEC, NTT, SoftBank and others.

title: Georgia S 104 — State Government
short_title: Georgia S 104 — State Government
summary: Relates to information technology relative to state government, prohibits the use or installation of any artificial intelligence system on state equipment when the company that developed or deployed such artificial intelligence system is associated with the Peoples Republic of China, provides definitions, provides for related matters, repeals conflicting laws.

title: Rhode Island H 5217 — Clean Air Preservation Act
short_title: Rhode Island H 5217 — Clean Air Preservation Act
topics: Government use of AI; Consumer protection; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Establishes the State Clean Air Preservation Act that establishes a regulatory process to prohibit polluting atmospheric experimentation such as solar radiation modification, sunlight reflection methods, solar radiation management, geoengineering, weather modification, cloud seeding, or other atmospheric interventions involving the release of pollutants including Perfluoroalkyl and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances, known also as forever chemicals, within the State.

title: Hawaii H 639 — Consumer Interactions with Artificial Intelligence
short_title: Hawaii H 639 — Consumer Interactions with Artificial Intelligence
summary: Requires corporations, organizations, or individuals engaging in commercial transactions to inform consumers when the consumers are communicating or interacting with a chatbot or other technology that mimics human interaction, requires developers that sell, offer for sale, advertise, or make available chatbots to disclose that their chatbots use artificial intelligence and are capable of mimicking human behavior and textual or spoken conversation, authorizes private rights of action and statutory penalties.

title: Hawaii S 1136 — Insurance Ratemaking Regulations
short_title: Hawaii S 1136 — Insurance Ratemaking Regulations
summary: Establishes ratemaking regulations for insurers who base their rates on a policyholder or applicant's wildfire risk, amends the definition of prospective loss costs to incorporate catastrophe modeling instead of historical aggregate losses, prohibits insurers from basing certain insurance rates on past loss experience within or outside the state, requires insurers to provide a list of items that may be covered under a homeowners insurance policy issued or renewed.

title: Pennsylvania H 518 — Unfair Trade Practices
short_title: Pennsylvania H 518 — Unfair Trade Practices
summary: Amends the act known as the Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law, provides for definitions and for unlawful acts or practices and exclusions.

title: Tennessee H 449 — Criminal Procedure
short_title: Tennessee H 449 — Criminal Procedure
summary: Restores the right of suffrage for persons convicted of an infamous crime after expiration of the sentence imposed for the infamous crime, removes requirement that the person pay restitution and court costs and be current in all child support obligations before having the person's right of suffrage restored, permits a person to have the right of suffrage restored without having the person's full rights of citizenship restored.

title: EU AI Office Guidelines on Prohibited AI Practices (Article 5 EU AI Act)
short_title: EU AI Office Guidelines on Prohibited Practices
topics: General AI governance; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: EU AI Office; National market surveillance authorities
summary: Published by the EU AI Office on 4 February 2025, these guidelines provide authoritative interpretation of the eight categories of prohibited AI practices under Article 5 of the EU AI Act. They cover: subliminal manipulation, exploitation of vulnerabilities, social scoring by public authorities, real-time biometric surveillance in public, emotion recognition in workplace/education, biometric categorisation from scraping, and AI-enabled manipulation of criminal risk.

title: Illinois H 1937 — State Auditing Act
short_title: Illinois H 1937 — State Auditing Act
summary: Amends the State Auditing Act, requires the Auditor General to conduct a survey of the Administrative Code to determine how many mandates and restrictions are imposed by the Administrative Code on persons, firms, and other entities within the private sector and units of local government and taxing bodies other than the state, allows the Auditor General to contract with a private entity to fulfill some or all of these requirements, allows the use of artificial intelligence for these requirements.

title: Pennsylvania H 486 — Advertising
short_title: Pennsylvania H 486 — Advertising
summary: Amends the act known as the Pennsylvania Election Code, in primary and election expenses, provides for advertising.

title: Pre-market Guidance for Machine Learning-Enabled Medical Devices (Health Canada, February 2025)
short_title: Health Canada ML Medical Devices Guidance
issuing_body: Health Canada
summary: Health Canada's pre-market guidance provides a quasi-binding framework under the Food and Drugs Act and Medical Devices Regulations for AI/ML-enabled medical devices seeking Canadian market authorisation. It covers predetermined change control plans (algorithm change protocols), transparency obligations, cybersecurity requirements, equity analysis to address algorithmic bias, and risk-based evidence requirements. Manufacturers must demonstrate ongoing performance monitoring and post-market surveillance aligned with device risk class.

title: Namibia National Artificial Intelligence Strategy (NCRST/Ministry)
short_title: Namibia National AI Strategy 2025
issuing_body: Namibia National Commission on Research, Science and Technology (NCRST); National AI Council
summary: Namibia's National AI Strategy launched by the National Commission on Research, Science and Technology (NCRST) in February 2025. Establishes a decentralized governance structure with a National AI Council and sector-specific Technical Working Groups. Prioritizes AI applications in healthcare, agriculture, and education as key development sectors.

title: Pennsylvania H 431 — Artificially Generated Impersonations
short_title: Pennsylvania H 431 — Artificially Generated Impersonations
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Consumer protection; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Amends Title 18 Crimes and Offenses of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, in forgery and fraudulent practices, provides for the offense of unauthorized dissemination of artificially generated impersonation of individual.

title: Georgia S 37 — AI Accountability Act
short_title: Georgia S 37 — AI Accountability Act
summary: Requires that all governmental entities develop and maintain artificial intelligence system usage plans, relates to commissions and other agencies, so as to create the State Board for Artificial Intelligence, provides guidance to governmental entities in their development of artificial intelligence system usage plans, provides for the purpose, membership, and duties of such board.

title: Illinois H 1594 — Human Rights Act
short_title: Illinois H 1594 — Human Rights Act
summary: Amends the Human Rights Act, provides that it is a civil rights violation for an employer, employment agency, or labor organization to take certain employment-related actions on the basis of an individual's weight and size, provides that it is a civil rights violation for the owner, lessee, proprietor, manager, superintendent, agent, or employee of a place of public accommodation, because of the weight and size of any person, directly or indirectly, to refuse, withhold from, or deny to any individual.

title: Ohio H 11 — Post Policy Documents
short_title: Ohio H 11 — Post Policy Documents
summary: Amends specified sections and to enact specified sections of the Revised Code to require legislative approval of administrative rules and other regulatory actions under specified conditions, to allow a Joint Committee on Agency Rule Review (JCARR) chairperson to request a third-party fiscal analysis of a rule, and to require state agencies to publicly post policy documents.

title: Pennsylvania H 399 — Administration of Assistance Programs
short_title: Pennsylvania H 399 — Administration of Assistance Programs
summary: Amends the act known as the Human Services Code, in public assistance, provides for administration of assistance programs.

title: South Carolina H 3796 — Granting or Recognizing Legal Personhood
short_title: South Carolina H 3796 — Granting or Recognizing Legal Personhood
summary: Prohibits a governmental entity from granting or recognizing legal personhood in certain items.

title: Hawaii S 1176 — Official State Computer Language
short_title: Hawaii S 1176 — Official State Computer Language
summary: Adopts, establishes, and designates Python as the official computer language of the state.

title: Hawaii S 1288 — Transitional Homes
short_title: Hawaii S 1288 — Transitional Homes
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI; Consumer protection
summary: Establishes the Hawaii Efficient Transitional Homes Commission to, among other things, oversee the strategic development, operation, and funding of transitional homes and enhance the efficient management of transitional homes through technology and data driven approaches.

title: Hawaii S 1618 — Journalistic Ethics Commission
short_title: Hawaii S 1618 — Journalistic Ethics Commission
summary: Establishes a Journalistic Ethics Commission within the Department of Commerce and Consumer Affairs, establishes a Journalistic Code of Ethics, requires news media outlets to provide training in the ethics of journalism to journalists and editors in their employ, establishes a Journalistic Ethics Review Board to be administratively attached to the Department of Commerce and Consumer Affairs, requires the Journalistic Ethics Review Board to handle complaints and appeals regarding violations.

title: Pennsylvania H 317 — Artificial Intelligence
short_title: Pennsylvania H 317 — Artificial Intelligence
summary: Amends Title 18 Crimes and Offenses of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, in computer offenses, provides for artificial intelligence, imposes a penalty.

title: Hawaii S 785 — Food Sales Dynamic Pricing
short_title: Hawaii S 785 — Food Sales Dynamic Pricing
summary: Prohibits retailers from using dynamic pricing in the sale of food that is sold, or qualifies to be sold, as part of the federal Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program or Special Supplemental Foods Program for Women, Infants, and Children, establishes fines.

title: Hawaii H 824 — Government Efficiency
short_title: Hawaii H 824 — Government Efficiency
summary: Appropriate funds to the Legislative Reference Bureau to procure artificial intelligence software and analytic services to streamline state law and regulations, requires a report to the Legislature.

title: Hawaii H 831 — Rental Market Algorithmic Price Setting
short_title: Hawaii H 831 — Rental Market Algorithmic Price Setting
topics: Government use of AI; Consumer protection
summary: Prohibits the use of algorithmic price setting in the state's rental market, requires the Department of the Attorney General to develop and undertake a public education program regarding the prohibition.

title: Executive Order 14179: Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence
issuing_body: President of the United States
summary: Executive Order 14179, signed 23 January 2025, sets US federal policy to sustain and enhance American AI dominance, directs the development of an AI Action Plan within 180 days, and orders agencies to review and revise or rescind actions taken under the revoked Executive Order 14110 that are inconsistent with the new policy. It also called for revision of the OMB memoranda governing federal agency use and procurement of AI, which OMB replaced in April 2025 with M-25-21 and M-25-22.
scope: Binds executive departments and agencies of the US federal government. It does not itself impose obligations on private companies, but it shapes federal procurement, agency guidance and enforcement priorities.

title: Alaska S 2 — Deepfake Disclosure
short_title: Alaska S 2 — Deepfake Disclosure
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Government use of AI; Consumer protection; Law enforcement & justice; Elections
summary: Relates to the disclosure of election related deepfakes, relates to use of artificial intelligence by State agencies, relates to the transfer of data about individuals between State agencies.

title: Alaska S 33 — Synthetic Media Liability
short_title: Alaska S 33 — Synthetic Media Liability
summary: Relates to defamation claims based on the use of synthetic media, relates to the use of synthetic media in electioneering communications.

title: Cabinet of Ministers Resolution Establishing the National Council for Artificial Intelligence Development (Kyrgyz Republic)
short_title: National Council for AI Development (Kyrgyzstan)
issuing_body: Cabinet of Ministers of the Kyrgyz Republic; National Council for Artificial Intelligence Development
summary: The National Council for AI Development was established by Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of the Kyrgyz Republic No. 29 of 2025-01-22 (a Cabinet resolution, NOT a presidential decree), under the 2024-2028 Digital Transformation Concept. Advisory body coordinating AI policy. Subsequently amended by Resolution No. 844 of 2025-12-29.

title: New York S 2697 — Use of an Algorithmic Device by a Landlord
short_title: New York S 2697 — Use of an Algorithmic Device by a Landlord
summary: Prohibits the use of an algorithmic device by a landlord for the purpose of determining the amount of rent to charge a residential tenant, declares that such use is an unfair or deceptive trade practice.

title: Hawaii H 62 — Hospitals and Care Homes Nurse to Patient Ratios
short_title: Hawaii H 62 — Hospitals and Care Homes Nurse to Patient Ratios
summary: Implements various nurse to patient ratios at hospitals and care homes, requires the Department of Health to audit healthcare facility compliance.

title: Hawaii H 465 — Food Sales Dynamic Pricing
short_title: Hawaii H 465 — Food Sales Dynamic Pricing
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI; Consumer protection
summary: Prohibits retailers from using dynamic pricing in the sale of food that is sold, or qualifies to be sold, as part of the federal Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program or Special Supplemental Foods Program for Women, Infants, and Children, establishes fines.

title: Hawaii H 484 — Efficient Transitional Homes Commission
short_title: Hawaii H 484 — Efficient Transitional Homes Commission
summary: Establishes the state Efficient Transitional Homes Commission to provide recommendations for the efficient, effective, and transparent management of transitional homes, requires annual reports to the Legislature.

title: Hawaii H 487 — Government Efficiency
short_title: Hawaii H 487 — Government Efficiency
summary: Appropriate funds to the Legislative Reference Bureau to procure artificial intelligence software and analytic services to streamline state law and regulations, requires a report to the Legislature.

title: Hawaii S 487 — Statewide Data and Artificial Intelligence Governance
short_title: Hawaii S 487 — Statewide Data and Artificial Intelligence Governance
summary: Establishes and appropriates funds for a data and artificial intelligence governance and decision intelligence center and necessary positions to improve data quality and data sharing statewide.

title: Hawaii H 726 — Data and Artificial Intelligence Governance
short_title: Hawaii H 726 — Data and Artificial Intelligence Governance
topics: Government use of AI; National security & defence
summary: Establishes and appropriates funds for a data and artificial intelligence governance and decision intelligence center and necessary positions to improve data quality and data sharing statewide.

title: Hawaii S 59 — Discriminatory Algorithmic Eligibility Determinations
short_title: Hawaii S 59 — Discriminatory Algorithmic Eligibility Determinations
topics: General AI governance; Employment & HR; Consumer protection
summary: Prohibits users of algorithmic decision making from utilizing algorithmic eligibility determinations in a discriminatory manner, requires users of algorithmic decision making to send corresponding notices to individual's whose personal information is used, requires users of algorithmic decision making to submit annual reports to the Department of the Attorney General, provides means of civil enforcement.

title: South Carolina S 225 — Artificial Intelligence Technologies
short_title: South Carolina S 225 — Artificial Intelligence Technologies
summary: (Senate Resolution) Expresses support for the development of artificial intelligence technologies in the state of state and oppose censorship or bias that would hamper the growth of these technological advancements.

title: Lithuania — Amendments to the Law on Information Society Services and the Law on Technology and Innovation (designating EU AI Act national competent authorities)
short_title: Lithuania AI Supervisory Authority Designation
issuing_body: Lithuanian Innovation Agency; Communications Regulatory Authority (RRT)
summary: Amends Lithuania's Law on Electronic Communications to designate supervisory authorities for the EU AI Act: Innovation Agency as notifying authority for conformity assessment bodies; Communications Regulatory Authority (RRT) as primary market surveillance authority. Lithuania also launched the EU's first national AI regulatory sandbox pilot program (€3 million allocated). Among the first EU member states to formally designate AI Act authorities.

title: Puerto Rico Senate Joint Resolution 1 — Ordering PRITS to conduct a study on AI governance policies, risk management frameworks, and best practices for Puerto Rico, and create a registry of AI developers
short_title: Puerto Rico S.J.R. 1 — AI Registry and Governance Study (PRITS)
issuing_body: PRITS
summary: Orders PRITS to conduct a study proposing AI governance policies for Puerto Rico consistent with state and federal law, develop a risk management policy based on the NIST AI Risk Management Framework or ISO/IEC 42001, design best practices frameworks for ethical AI use, and maintain a registry of companies developing AI in Puerto Rico. Semi-annual progress reports to the Legislative Assembly starting July 2026.

title: South Carolina S 72 — Distribution of Intimate Images
short_title: South Carolina S 72 — Distribution of Intimate Images
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Provides definitions relates to the distribution of intimate images, makes it unlawful for a person to intentionally disseminate an intimate image or a digitally forged intimate image of another person without effective consent of the depicted person, provides a penalty for the unlawful dissemination of intimate images.

title: South Carolina H 3043 — Identifiable Minor
short_title: South Carolina H 3043 — Identifiable Minor
summary: Relates to definitions applicable to certain offenses against minors, defines the term identifiable minor, relates to first degree sexual exploitation of a minor, relates to second degree sexual exploitation of a minor, and relates to third degree sexual exploitation of a minor, all, incorporates identifiable minors into the purview of the statute to address morphed child images, relates to criminal solicitation of a minor, relates to employment of a person under eighteen.

title: South Carolina H 3404 — Property Right in Use of Individuals Name
short_title: South Carolina H 3404 — Property Right in Use of Individuals Name
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Consumer protection; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Provides that every individual has a property right in the use of that individual's name, photograph, voice, or likeness in any medium in any manner and provides penalties.

title: South Carolina H 3406 — Covered Platform Operator Procedures
short_title: South Carolina H 3406 — Covered Platform Operator Procedures
summary: Provides definitions, provides that a covered platform operator may not upload or allow a user to upload certain pornographic images without certain verification, provides that a covered platform operator must establish certain procedures, provides that certain images may not be uploaded without consent, provides for civil penalties, provides for criminal penalties, establishes a legislative committee, provides that the attorney general shall create certain consent forms.

title: South Carolina H 3471 — Offenses Against Minor Applicable Definitions
short_title: South Carolina H 3471 — Offenses Against Minor Applicable Definitions
summary: Relates to definitions applicable to certain offenses against minors, defines the term identifiable minor, relates to first degree sexual exploitation of a minor, amends relates to second degree sexual exploitation of a minor, amends relates to third degree sexual exploitation of a minor, all, incorporates identifiable minors into the purview of the statue to address morphed child images.

title: South Carolina H 3517 — Deepfake Media Distribution
short_title: South Carolina H 3517 — Deepfake Media Distribution
summary: Prohibits the distribution of deceptive and fraudulent deepfake media of a candidate within ninety days of an election unless the media includes requisite disclosure language, authorizes a candidate whose likeness is depicted in media distributed in violation of this section to seek injunctive or other equitable relief as well as an action for damages against the distributor of the media.

title: AI Opportunities Action Plan
short_title: AI Opportunities Action Plan
topics: Government use of AI; Frontier / general-purpose AI
issuing_body: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
summary: The AI Opportunities Action Plan is an independent report by Matt Clifford commissioned by the government, containing 50 recommendations organised under three aims: laying foundations (compute, data, skills and regulation), driving AI adoption across the public and private sectors, and securing homegrown frontier AI capability. The government published a response accepting the recommendations and treats the plan as its roadmap for AI-led growth.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by Department for Science, Innovation and Technology. Oversight: DSIT leads delivery across government; recommendations adopted via the government response. Stated purpose: Use AI to drive economic growth, public-service improvement and sovereign UK AI capability.

title: Personal Data Protection Order, 2025 (S 1/2025)
short_title: Brunei PDPO 2025
issuing_body: Brunei Info-Communications Media Authority (AITI)
summary: Brunei's first data protection law, gazetted as S 1/2025 on 2025-01-08. Applies to private-sector organisations and NGOs only (public sector excluded). GDPR-style obligations, data-subject rights (access, correction, consent withdrawal, private right of action); enforced by AITI with penalties up to 10% of annual turnover or BND 1,000,000. Phased with ~1-year grace period, so full private-sector compliance ~January 2026.

title: New York S 463 — Promotion of Unlawful Material
short_title: New York S 463 — Promotion of Unlawful Material
summary: Prohibits the knowing and reckless promotion of unlawful or false material, provides remedies for the violation of such prohibition.

title: Puerto Rico S 68 — Artificial Intelligence Act
short_title: Puerto Rico S 68 — Artificial Intelligence Act
summary: Relates to the Artificial Intelligence Act of the Government.

title: Puerto Rico Senate Bill 101 — Amendment to the Act for Oversight of Political Campaigns and Electoral Code to require disclosure of AI-generated or AI-altered political advertising content and define artificial intelligence, generative AI, and deepfakes
short_title: Puerto Rico S 101 — AI Disclosure in Political Advertising
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Consumer protection; Elections
issuing_body: State Elections Commission
summary: Amends the Act for Oversight of Political Campaigns (Act 222-2011) and Electoral Code (Act 58-2020) to require that political communications generated or altered by AI include clear disclosure; defines artificial intelligence, generative AI, AI-generated content, and deepfakes; and criminalizes the malicious creation or dissemination of AI-generated realistic imitations of persons without consent in election contexts.

title: Puerto Rico Senate Joint Resolution 16 — Ordering PRITS to create and implement an AI-based application for monitoring public auction processes for transparency and fraud prevention
short_title: Puerto Rico S.J.R. 16 — AI Monitoring App for Public Auctions
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: PRITS
summary: Orders PRITS to develop and implement an AI-based application for real-time monitoring of public auction processes in Puerto Rico, capable of detecting suspicious patterns, generating automatic alerts on irregularities, and providing accessible reports to oversight entities. Development plan due to Legislature within 90 days; quarterly implementation reports during first year.

title: Expanded ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics – Generative AI
short_title: Expanded ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics – Generative AI (2025)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Data protection & privacy; Frontier / general-purpose AI
issuing_body: ASEAN Digital Ministers' Meeting
summary: Endorsed in January 2025, the expanded guide addresses risks specific to generative AI (hallucination, deepfakes and misinformation, intellectual property, privacy, security, bias, embedded values) and proposes governance dimensions covering accountability, data, development and deployment, incident reporting, testing and assurance, security, content provenance, safety research and public-interest use, with policy recommendations for member states.
scope: Voluntary; developers and deployers of generative AI across ASEAN.

title: Stratégie nationale de l'intelligence artificielle de l'Algérie
short_title: National AI strategy (2025)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of Algeria
summary: The strategy sets priorities on AI talent and research, start-ups, public-sector and industrial adoption, data and compute, and governance through the National AI Council.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Artificial Intelligence Strategy of the Republic of Azerbaijan for 2025–2028 (presidential decree, March 2025)
short_title: AI Strategy 2025–2028
topics: General AI governance; Education; Government use of AI
issuing_body: President of the Republic of Azerbaijan
summary: Approved by presidential decree in March 2025, the strategy sets goals for AI in public administration, the economy and education, data and computing infrastructure, talent, ethical and safe AI, and a coordinating institutional structure, with an action plan to 2028.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Bhutan National AI Strategy 2025 (NAIS 2025)
short_title: Bhutan National AI Strategy 2025
topics: Employment & HR; Health; Education; National security & defence
issuing_body: GovTech Agency, Royal Government of Bhutan
summary: A national strategy framed around the vision of AI rooted in Gross National Happiness. It identifies eight focus areas (agriculture and livestock, tourism, green energy, education, health, public service delivery, natural resources and biodiversity, and culture and language) and seven enablers such as infrastructure, governance and regulation, cybersecurity, skills, research, collaboration and funding. It aims to raise Bhutan's AI maturity by the end of the 13th Five Year Plan and includes monitoring, evaluation and risk-mitigation provisions.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by GovTech Agency, Royal Government of Bhutan. Oversight: GovTech Agency with annual action-plan reviews and a five-year strategy review. Stated purpose: Apply AI to national development in line with Gross National Happiness values.

title: Stratégie nationale de l'intelligence artificielle de la Côte d'Ivoire
short_title: National AI Strategy (2025)
topics: General AI governance; Health; Education; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of Côte d'Ivoire
summary: The strategy sets priorities on AI talent and research, adoption in public services, agriculture, health and education, data governance and infrastructure, and ethical use.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Egypt National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
short_title: Egypt National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
issuing_body: National Council for Artificial Intelligence, Ministry of Communications and Information Technology
summary: Egypt's first national AI strategy framed AI as a tool for the country's sustainable development goals and for positioning Egypt as an active contributor to AI in Africa and the Arab region. It covered AI for government, development, capacity building and international activities. It has been superseded by the 2025-2030 second edition.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by National Council for Artificial Intelligence, Ministry of Communications and Information Technology. Oversight: NCAI coordinates implementation across ministries. Stated purpose: Leverage AI for sustainable development and regional leadership.

title: National AI Strategy - Second Edition 2025-2030
short_title: National AI Strategy
issuing_body: National Council for Artificial Intelligence (NCAI), Ministry of Communications and Information Technology
summary: The second edition updates Egypt's 2021 strategy for 2025-2030 around six pillars: governance, data, infrastructure, technology, talent and ecosystem. It sets targets for AI specialists, startups and ICT's contribution to GDP, and includes plans for national foundational models and expanded regional and international cooperation.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by National Council for Artificial Intelligence (NCAI), Ministry of Communications and Information Technology. Oversight: NCAI (chaired by the ICT Minister) oversees implementation across ministries. Stated purpose: Move from AI adoption to large-scale, sovereign AI capability supporting Digital Egypt.

title: Ley para el Fomento de la Inteligencia Artificial y Tecnologías Emergentes (Decreto Legislativo, febrero de 2025)
short_title: Law for the Promotion of AI and Emerging Technologies
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Asamblea Legislativa de El Salvador
summary: Approved by the Legislative Assembly in February 2025, the law promotes AI development and investment, creates the National Agency for Artificial Intelligence (ANIA) as regulator, defines rights and principles (human oversight, transparency, non-discrimination, data protection), sets registration and sandbox mechanisms and limits liability of developers who act in good faith under the law, alongside data-processing rules for AI training.
scope: Developers, providers and users of AI systems in El Salvador and public bodies; ANIA issues implementing regulations.

title: Ghana National Artificial Intelligence Strategy (2025-2035)
short_title: Ghana National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
issuing_body: Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations
summary: A ten-year national roadmap launched by President Mahama that treats data as a national asset and sets out pillars covering education and skills, infrastructure and compute, data governance, ecosystem development, sector adoption, applied research and public-sector AI. It proposes a National AI Fund and performance indicators for ministries, and emphasises localisation of AI for Ghanaian languages.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations. Oversight: Ministry leads with NITA, Data Protection Commission and Cyber Security Authority; strategy recommends a Responsible AI Authority. Stated purpose: Make AI a driver of inclusive growth and position Ghana as a regional AI hub.

title: Hong Kong Generative Artificial Intelligence Technical and Application Guideline
short_title: Generative AI Technical and Application Guideline (2025)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Digital Policy Office, with the Hong Kong Generative AI Research and Development Centre
summary: Published in April 2025, the guideline covers the technical characteristics and risks of generative AI, governance principles (safety, transparency, accountability, data protection, fairness) and practical application guidance for developers, service providers and users across the AI lifecycle, and is intended as a reference for industry and government.
scope: Voluntary reference for developers, providers and users of generative AI in Hong Kong.

title: India AI Governance Guidelines (MeitY, 2025)
short_title: India AI Governance Guidelines
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
summary: The India AI Governance Guidelines set out a principle-based, pro-innovation approach to governing AI in India. They articulate guiding principles (such as trust, people-first design, fairness, accountability, safety and transparency), propose an institutional framework including an AI governance group and an AI Safety Institute role, favour applying existing laws over a new AI statute, and recommend voluntary commitments, techno-legal measures, risk-based oversight and incident reporting for AI systems.
scope: Non-binding guidance addressed to government bodies, industry and developers deploying AI in India. It does not create legal obligations; it signals regulatory expectations and possible future measures.

title: Legge 23 settembre 2025, n. 132 – Disposizioni e deleghe al Governo in materia di intelligenza artificiale
short_title: Law No. 132/2025 on artificial intelligence
topics: General AI governance; Employment & HR; Health; Government use of AI; Law enforcement & justice
issuing_body: Parliament of the Italian Republic
summary: Italy's framework AI law, published in the Official Gazette on 25 September 2025 and in force from 10 October 2025. It states principles (human-centric, transparent, safe AI; protection of fundamental rights), sets sector rules for healthcare (AI as support, not replacement, for clinical decisions), employment (information to workers, an AI-at-work observatory), intellectual professions (client disclosure), justice (judge decides; AI only for organisational support) and public administration, requires parental consent for children under 14, designates AgID and ACN as national authorities, delegates the government to align national law with the EU AI Act, and creates a criminal offence for unlawful dissemination of AI-generated or manipulated content with aggravating circumstances for other crimes committed with AI.
scope: Applies in Italy to public and private users, developers and providers of AI systems, with sector chapters for health, work, professions, justice and public administration; the EU AI Act continues to apply directly.

title: Act on Promotion of Research and Development, and Utilization of Artificial Intelligence-related Technology (Act No. 53 of 2025)
short_title: Act on Promotion of Research and Development, and Utilization of Artificial Intelligence-related Technology
issuing_body: National Diet of Japan; administered by the Cabinet Office
summary: Japan's first AI-specific statute establishes basic principles and a governmental framework for promoting AI research, development and use. It creates an AI Strategy Headquarters under the Cabinet, requires the government to adopt an AI Basic Plan, and provides for guidelines, information gathering and investigation of cases where AI infringes rights, together with guidance to businesses and the public. Businesses are asked to cooperate with government measures; the Act contains no fines or prohibitions.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by National Diet of Japan; administered by the Cabinet Office. Oversight: Artificial Intelligence Strategy Headquarters chaired by the Prime Minister with all Cabinet ministers as members. Stated purpose: Promote AI research and use nationally while addressing public concern about risks, without new penalties.

title: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan "On Artificial Intelligence" (signed November 2025)
short_title: Law on Artificial Intelligence (2025)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Parliament of the Republic of Kazakhstan
summary: The law defines AI systems and their classification by level of autonomy and risk, sets principles (legality, fairness, transparency, safety, human control), assigns duties to owners and operators of AI systems including risk management, labelling of AI-generated content and protection of personal data, prohibits certain manipulative and social-scoring uses, provides for a national AI platform and state support measures, and allocates state regulation to the authorised body.
scope: Owners, developers and operators of AI systems in Kazakhstan and public bodies using AI.

title: Kenya Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2025-2030
short_title: Kenya Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2025-2030
issuing_body: Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy (MICDE)
summary: Kenya's first national AI strategy sets a five-year agenda built on three pillars: AI digital infrastructure, data and AI governance, and AI research, innovation and commercialisation. It aligns with the Kenya National Digital Masterplan 2022-2032 and priorities sectors such as agriculture, health and education. A separate implementation roadmap was later published by the ministry.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy (MICDE). Oversight: MICDE leads implementation with partners; implementation roadmap published Dec 2025. Stated purpose: Position Kenya as a competitive, secure and future-ready AI economy.

title: Kuwait National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2025–2028
short_title: National AI Strategy 2025–2028
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of Kuwait (CAIT)
summary: The strategy sets objectives on AI in government services, national talent, data and cloud infrastructure, ethical and responsible AI, and partnerships, aligned with Kuwait Vision 2035.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Maryland S 904 — Building Information Guardrails Data Act of 2025
short_title: Maryland S 904 — Building Information Guardrails Data Act of 2025
summary: Establishes the Privacy Protection and Enforcement Unit within the Division of Consumer Protection in the Office of the Attorney General, establishes a data broker registry, requires certain data brokers to register each year with the Comptroller, imposes a tax on the gross income of certain data brokers for taxable years beginning after a specified date.

title: Maryland H 1089 — Building Information Guardrails Data Act of 2025
short_title: Maryland H 1089 — Building Information Guardrails Data Act of 2025
summary: Establishes the Privacy Protection and Enforcement Unit within the Division of Consumer Protection in the Office of the Attorney General, establishes a data broker registry, requires certain data brokers to register each year with the Comptroller, imposes a tax on the gross income of certain data brokers for taxable years beginning after a specified date, requires the revenue from the data broker tax be used by Maryland Public Television to provide digital literacy support to students.

title: Mississippi H 768 — ELVIS Act of 2025
short_title: Mississippi H 768 — ELVIS Act of 2025
summary: Enacts the Ensuring Likeness, Voice and Image Security Act of 2025, stipulates that every individual has a property right in the use of that individuals name, photograph, voice or likeness for the purpose of expanding artificial intelligence protections to individuals said property rights, stipulates that property rights provided in this act are exclusive to the individual, implements commercial exploitation guidelines, creates a civil action upon violation of this act.

title: New York Responsible AI Safety and Education (RAISE) Act (S.6953-B / A.6453-B, signed December 2025)
short_title: New York RAISE Act (frontier model safety)
topics: General AI governance; Frontier / general-purpose AI
issuing_body: New York State Legislature
summary: The RAISE Act requires large developers of frontier AI models (defined by training compute and revenue thresholds) to publish and follow a safety and security protocol, report critical safety incidents to the state within a set period, not deploy models that create unreasonable risk of critical harm, and submit to Attorney General enforcement with civil penalties; the chapter amendments create a state oversight office and align definitions with California's Transparency in Frontier AI Act.
scope: Large frontier-model developers whose models are available in New York; not deployers of ordinary AI systems.

title: New Zealand's Strategy for Artificial Intelligence: Investing with Confidence
short_title: New Zealand AI Strategy (2025)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
summary: Published in July 2025, the strategy aims to lift AI adoption by businesses, especially small and medium enterprises, and the public sector, by reducing barriers, providing clear guidance (Responsible AI Guidance for Businesses), building skills and pursuing a light-touch, proportionate regulatory approach that relies on existing law and international alignment (OECD principles). It rules out a standalone AI act for now.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: National Artificial Intelligence Policy 2025
short_title: National Artificial Intelligence Policy 2025
issuing_body: Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication (approved by the Federal Cabinet)
summary: Pakistan's first national AI policy, organised around six pillars: innovation ecosystem, awareness and readiness, secure AI, transformation of sectors, AI infrastructure, and international partnerships. It proposes a National AI Fund drawn from Ignite's R&D fund, centres of excellence, venture and innovation funds, regulatory sandboxes and KPIs, with an AI Council to oversee delivery. Targets include large-scale training of AI professionals and funded research projects.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication (approved by the Federal Cabinet). Oversight: MoITT with a proposed national AI Council and implementation directorate. Stated purpose: Build a domestic AI ecosystem, skills base and infrastructure while managing ethical and security risks.

title: Stratégie nationale de l'intelligence artificielle du Sénégal
short_title: National AI Strategy (2025)
topics: General AI governance; Health; Education; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of Senegal
summary: The strategy sets priorities on AI for public services, agriculture, health and education, talent and research, data and infrastructure, and ethical governance, within the New Technological Deal.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Стратегија развоја вештачке интелигенције у Републици Србији за период 2025–2030
short_title: AI Development Strategy 2025–2030
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of the Republic of Serbia
