summary: Adopted in 2025, the second national AI strategy sets goals to 2030 on research and talent, AI in the economy and public administration, data and compute infrastructure, trustworthy AI and alignment with the EU AI Act and the Council of Europe convention, and the preparation of an AI law.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Nacionalni program spodbujanja razvoja in uporabe umetne inteligence v Republiki Sloveniji do leta 2025
short_title: National AI Programme to 2025 (NpUI)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of the Republic of Slovenia
summary: Adopted in May 2021, the programme sets measures on research and innovation, skills, data and infrastructure, public-sector and business adoption, ethics and trustworthy AI, and international cooperation, including support for the UNESCO IRCAI centre.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Federal Council decision on the regulation of artificial intelligence: ratification of the Council of Europe Convention and sector-specific adjustments
short_title: Federal Council AI regulatory approach (2025)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Swiss Federal Council
summary: On 12 February 2025 the Federal Council decided how Switzerland will regulate AI: it will ratify the Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI and implement it mainly through targeted changes to existing law where needed (for example transparency, data protection and non-discrimination), avoid a horizontal AI act, and complement legislation with non-binding measures such as self-regulation and agreements with industry. Federal departments were tasked to prepare a consultation draft by the end of 2026.
scope: Sets direction for federal law-making; creates no obligations until implementing legislation is adopted.

title: Stratégie nationale de l'intelligence artificielle de la Tunisie
short_title: National AI Strategy (2025)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of Tunisia (Ministry of Communication Technologies)
summary: The strategy sets objectives on AI talent and research, adoption in public services and the economy, data and infrastructure, start-up support and ethical governance.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: ICO Detailed Guidance on Automated Decision-Making Including Profiling (UK GDPR)
short_title: UK ICO ADM Detailed Guidance
topics: General AI governance; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: Information Commissioner's Office (ICO)
summary: Detailed interpretive guidance from the UK Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) on the automated decision-making (ADM) provisions of the UK GDPR (Articles 22A-22D), last updated March 2026. Covers when ADM provisions apply (significant decision + solely automated + no meaningful human involvement), lawful bases for ADM (consent, contract, public task, legitimate interests — but not recognised legitimate interest), special category data restrictions, required safeguards (right to information about decisions, right to make representations, right to human intervention, right to contest), transparency obligations, and DPIA requirements. Explicitly addresses AI and machine learning systems in context of profiling and ADM. The guidance will inform a forthcoming statutory code of practice on AI and ADM. Currently being updated to reflect the Data (Use and Access) Act.

title: Law on Artificial Intelligence (Law No. 134/2025/QH15)
short_title: Law on Artificial Intelligence
issuing_body: National Assembly of Vietnam
summary: Vietnam's first dedicated AI statute, with eight chapters and 35 articles governing the research, development, provision, deployment and use of AI systems. It adopts a risk-based approach, requires human oversight in important decisions, and provides for national AI infrastructure, a national AI development fund, a regulatory sandbox and rules on AI-generated content. It took effect on 1 March 2026 with transition periods for existing systems.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by National Assembly of Vietnam. Oversight: Government/Ministry of Science and Technology as state management body. Stated purpose: Establish a comprehensive, risk-based legal framework for AI while promoting innovation.

title: Zimbabwe National Artificial Intelligence Policy
short_title: National AI Policy (2025)
topics: General AI governance; Health; Education; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of Zimbabwe
summary: The policy sets a framework for responsible AI adoption in government, agriculture, health, mining and education, skills and research, data governance and ethics.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Argentine Artificial Intelligence National Plan — Decree 1182/2024
short_title: Argentina AI National Plan Decree 1182/2024
issuing_body: Secretariat of Innovation, Science and Technology; AI Ethics Committee (created by decree)
summary: Decree 1182/2024 establishes Argentina's National AI Plan and creates an AI Ethics Committee within the national public administration. It requires impact assessments for AI systems used in government decisions, adopts a risk-based approach aligned with OECD principles, and mandates transparency for AI systems affecting citizens. The decree applies to national executive branch agencies and sets principles for future legislation.

title: Framework Act on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and Establishment of a Foundation for Trust (AI Basic Act, Act No. 20676)
short_title: AI Basic Act
issuing_body: National Assembly of the Republic of Korea; competent ministry Ministry of Science and ICT
summary: Korea's AI Basic Act is a comprehensive framework statute combining industrial promotion with trust and safety rules. It gives a legal basis for a national AI master plan every three years and the National AI Committee, supports R&D, data, standardisation and SMEs, and imposes duties on operators of high-impact AI (risk management, explanation, human oversight) and transparency duties to notify users of generative AI output. Foreign operators above a threshold must designate a domestic representative. It was promulgated in January 2025 and took effect on 22 January 2026 after a one-year grace period.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by National Assembly of the Republic of Korea; competent ministry Ministry of Science and ICT. Oversight: Ministry of Science and ICT as competent authority; presidential National AI Committee; AI Safety Institute. Stated purpose: Promote the AI industry while establishing trust obligations for high-impact and generative AI.

title: Law No. 2024/017 of 23 December 2024 on Personal Data Protection in Cameroon
short_title: Cameroon Personal Data Protection Law 2024
topics: General AI governance; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: Cameroon Personal Data Protection Authority (Commission de Protection des Données Personnelles)
summary: Comprehensive data protection statute enacted by Cameroon in December 2024, making Cameroon the 38th African country to adopt such legislation. Establishes a Personal Data Protection Authority; provides GDPR-aligned individual rights including erasure, portability, and objection. Includes explicit provisions on automated decision-making relevant to AI systems. Promulgated 23 December 2024 with an 18-month grace period; enforceable against controllers and processors from 23 June 2026.

title: Ley 21.719 sobre Protección de Datos Personales
short_title: Chile Data Protection Law (Ley 21.719)
issuing_body: Agencia de Protección de Datos Personales (not yet operational)
summary: Chile's comprehensive overhaul of personal data law replaces the 1999 Law 19.628 and aligns with GDPR standards. Article 8 bis grants data subjects the right to explanation and human review for automated decisions with significant effects. Creates an independent enforcement agency. Major obligations take effect December 2026.

jurisdiction: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
title: OAS Declaration and Plan of Action Towards Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy AI in the Americas (VII Meeting of Ministers of Science and Technology)
short_title: OAS AI Declaration for the Americas (2024)
issuing_body: Organization of American States (OAS)
summary: The OAS Declaration and Plan of Action adopted at the VII Meeting of Ministers of Science and Technology (December 2024) is a non-binding political declaration establishing a framework for inter-American AI governance cooperation. It launched a $1.1 million US-funded AI Policy Framework for the Americas project. The declaration commits OAS member states to principles of safe, secure, and trustworthy AI, with implementation supported through OAS institutional mechanisms.

title: Privacy and Other Legislation Amendment Act 2024 — Automated Decision-Making Provisions
short_title: Australia Privacy Act ADM Amendment
topics: General AI governance; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)
summary: Amends Australia's Privacy Act to require APP entities to disclose automated decision-making processes in privacy policies where AI could significantly affect individual rights or interests. Transparency obligation only — no prohibition or assessment requirement. Effective December 2026.

title: Marketing Submission Recommendations for a Predetermined Change Control Plan for Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Device Software Functions (FDA Final Guidance)
short_title: FDA PCCP Final Guidance for AI-Enabled Device Software
issuing_body: Food and Drug Administration (FDA); FDA Center for Devices and Radiological Health (CDRH)
summary: FDA's final guidance on Predetermined Change Control Plans (PCCPs) allows AI-enabled medical device makers to pre-specify the types of model updates and modifications that can be implemented after initial clearance without requiring a new 510(k) or PMA submission. The guidance expands the PCCP framework from ML-only to all AI-enabled device software functions and requires manufacturers to describe anticipated algorithm changes, performance objectives, and methodology for validating updates. This streamlines the regulatory pathway for continuously learning AI medical devices.

title: Methodology for the Risk and Impact Assessment of Artificial Intelligence Systems from the Point of View of Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law (HUDERIA)
short_title: HUDERIA risk and impact assessment methodology
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Council of Europe Committee on Artificial Intelligence (CAI)
summary: Adopted by the CAI in November 2024, HUDERIA is a structured methodology for assessing risks and impacts of AI systems on human rights, democracy and the rule of law across the lifecycle: context-based risk analysis, stakeholder engagement, risk and impact assessment, and mitigation planning with iterative review. It supports implementation of the Framework Convention and can be used by public and private organisations.
scope: Voluntary methodology for developers and deployers of AI systems, and for states implementing the Convention.

title: Strengthening Cyber Security and Building Trust in the Public Sector Act, 2024 (Ontario Bill 194)
short_title: Ontario Strengthening Cyber Security and Trust Act 2024 (Bill 194)
issuing_body: Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario
summary: Canada's first AI-specific regulatory requirements for public institutions. Applies to Ontario public sector entities (government, agencies, police, school boards). Requires AI governance policies, AI risk assessments, and public disclosure of AI use. Amends FIPPA with privacy impact assessments.

title: Proposed Law on Regulating Artificial Intelligence Technologies and Their Uses (Kingdom of Bahrain, Shura Council)
short_title: Bahrain Proposed AI Regulation Law
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media
issuing_body: AI Unit (Ministry designated by decree); Public Prosecution; Courts of Bahrain
summary: Submitted to the Bahrain Shura Council on 28 February 2024 by five members (Ref. 16 Q F6 D2), this 38-article proposed law would create the first binding AI regulatory framework in Bahrain, covering all persons residing in or operating from the Kingdom. It establishes: a licensing regime for commercial AI development and sale; an AI Unit within a designated Ministry for oversight, licensing, and enforcement; design requirements mandating human supervisability and non-discrimination; prohibitions on dangerous robots, deepfakes, and exclusive AI decision-making over life or freedom; civil liability for programmers and robot owners; and a tiered criminal penalty structure reaching imprisonment plus BD 20,000 (≈,000) for deepfake manipulation offenses. The explanatory memo explicitly cites inspiration from the EU AI Act and the Arab Guiding Law on AI, while emphasizing cultural and religious values. Entry into force would be six months after Gazette publication, with Executive Regulations due within three months. The proposal was cleared as legally admissible by the Shura Council Legal Advisors Authority.

title: NIST AI 100-4: Reducing Risks Posed by Synthetic Content — An Overview of Technical Approaches to Digital Content Transparency
short_title: NIST AI 100-4 — Reducing Risks from Synthetic Content
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media
issuing_body: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
summary: NIST AI 100-4 provides technical guidance on approaches to mitigate risks from AI-generated synthetic content including deepfakes, synthetic audio, and AI-generated text. Produced pursuant to EO 14110 Section 4(i), the publication surveys watermarking approaches, content provenance tracking, cryptographic methods, and deepfake detection technologies. It is intended as foundational technical guidance for organizations implementing digital content transparency and provenance systems.

jurisdiction: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
title: The Financial Stability Implications of Artificial Intelligence (FSB Report)
short_title: FSB — Financial Stability Implications of AI (2024)
summary: FSB report published November 14, 2024 as a G20 deliverable assessing AI adoption in global finance. Examines third-party concentration risks, market correlation risks from AI-driven herding behavior, cybersecurity risks, and model risk management challenges. Calls on national authorities to enhance AI monitoring frameworks and improve cross-border supervisory cooperation. Followed by the October 2025 FSB monitoring report.

title: Elections (Integrity of Online Advertising) (Amendment) Act 2024 (Singapore)
short_title: Singapore Elections (AI Integrity) Act 2024
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media
issuing_body: Elections Department Singapore (ELD); Returning Officer
summary: First Singapore legislation to explicitly mention artificial intelligence. Amends elections law to prohibit AI-generated or AI-manipulated online election advertising. Bans manipulated political content including deepfakes and AI-synthesized images, audio or video of candidates. Extends existing online election advertising regulations to cover AI-generated content.

title: Strategy for the development of artificial intelligence technologies until 2030 (Presidential Resolution, October 2024)
short_title: AI development strategy to 2030 (2024)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: President of the Republic of Uzbekistan
summary: The 2024 resolution approves a strategy to 2030 to raise the AI services market, deploy AI in public administration and priority sectors, build data centres and datasets, train specialists and adopt ethical principles and standards for AI.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Personal Data Protection (Amendment) Act 2024 (Act A1727)
short_title: Malaysia PDPA Amendment 2024
issuing_body: Personal Data Protection Commissioner (JPDP)
summary: Malaysia's 2024 amendment substantially updates the Personal Data Protection Act 2010 to align with GDPR standards. Mandates DPO appointment, 72-hour breach notification, expands sensitive personal data to include biometric data, and imposes direct obligations on data processors. AI systems processing personal data must comply with enhanced consent and DPO oversight requirements.

title: North Carolina Protecting Elections from Deceptive AI Act
short_title: North Carolina SB 880 (AI in Elections)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: North Carolina State Board of Elections
summary: Prohibits creating or distributing materially deceptive AI-generated media depicting a candidate within 60 days before an election without a clear disclosure label. Criminal misdemeanor for knowing violations. The disclosure must be conspicuous and state that the content contains AI-generated material.

title: White Paper on Strategic Direction for Artificial Intelligence and Data Governance Policy (Republic of Moldova, Ministry of Economic Development and Digitisation)
short_title: AI and Data Governance White Paper (Moldova)
topics: General AI governance; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: Ministry of Economic Development and Digitisation of the Republic of Moldova
summary: Moldova's Ministry of Economic Development and Digitisation published the country's first AI policy framework document on October 2, 2024—a White Paper on Strategic Direction for Artificial Intelligence and Data Governance Policy. The paper emphasizes ethical, inclusive, and sustainable AI development aligned with European standards, and complements Moldova's September 2024 signing of the Council of Europe AI Convention (CETS 225). As a non-binding framework, it signals Moldova's intent to align AI governance with EU norms ahead of its EU accession process.

title: Guía para Organismos Públicos y Privados sobre Transparencia y Protección de Datos Personales para una IA Responsable (AAIP, 2024)
short_title: AAIP Responsible AI Guide (2024)
topics: General AI governance; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: Agencia de Acceso a la Información Pública (AAIP)
summary: The AAIP Guide on Transparency and Personal Data Protection for Responsible AI, issued in October 2024 under Resolution 161/2023, provides best-practice guidance for public and private organisations deploying AI systems that process personal data. It covers the full AI lifecycle — data selection, model training, and deployment — and promotes privacy by design, data impact assessments, and ethical AI principles. While non-binding, the guide is an authoritative interpretive instrument issued by Argentina's national data protection authority.

title: Pennsylvania Act 125 of 2024 — Deepfake Sexual Images and AI-Generated CSAM (SB 1213)
short_title: Pennsylvania Act 125 of 2024 (Deepfake Sexual Images)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: courts; Pennsylvania Office of Attorney General
summary: Pennsylvania Act 125/2024 criminalizes creation and distribution of intimate/sexual deepfakes and classifies explicit AI-generated depictions of minors as CSAM. Makes it a crime to disseminate AI sexual depictions of current/former intimate partners with intent to harass. The PA OAG has already charged individuals under this law.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence: Training Data Transparency Act
short_title: California AB 2013 (Training Data Transparency)
issuing_body: California Attorney General
summary: Requires generative AI developers to publicly disclose information about the datasets used to train their models, including data types, sources, whether it included personal information, and whether synthetic data was used. Disclosure must be published on the developer's website.

title: Physicians Make Decisions Act
short_title: California SB 1120 (Health Insurance AI Utilization Review)
issuing_body: California Department of Managed Health Care; California Insurance Commissioner
summary: Prohibits health insurers and managed care plans from using AI or algorithms as the sole basis for denying, delaying, or modifying health care coverage decisions. Requires that any coverage determination made or assisted by AI must be reviewed and approved by a licensed California physician or appropriate health care provider. Applies to utilization review processes.

title: COMELEC Resolution No. 11064 — Guidelines on the Use of Artificial Intelligence and Social Media in Electoral Campaign
short_title: COMELEC Resolution 11064 (AI in Elections)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media
issuing_body: Commission on Elections (COMELEC)
summary: Binding regulatory resolution from the Commission on Elections applicable to all election participants in the Philippines. Prohibits AI-generated deepfakes in election campaigns and mandates digital watermarks and cryptographic metadata on all AI-generated campaign materials. Requires registration of all digital campaign channels and mandates disclosure when AI is used in campaign content. Considered one of the most comprehensive electoral AI regulations in Southeast Asia.

title: Advancing the Responsible Acquisition of Artificial Intelligence in Government (OMB Memorandum M-24-18)
short_title: OMB M-24-18 — Responsible AI Acquisition Memo
issuing_body: Office of Management and Budget (OMB)
summary: OMB Memorandum M-24-18 directed federal agencies on responsible AI acquisition principles under the Biden administration, establishing guidance on AI vendor due diligence, contractual safeguards for government AI purchases, and responsible AI principles that agencies must incorporate into procurement. The memo operationalized the AI acquisition aspects of EO 14110 for the federal contracting process. It was rescinded and superseded by OMB M-25-22 in April 2025.

jurisdiction: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
title: Global Digital Compact (Annex I of the Pact for the Future, A/RES/79/1)
short_title: UN Global Digital Compact
topics: General AI governance; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: Independent International Scientific Panel on AI; Global Dialogue on AI Governance
summary: The Global Digital Compact, adopted as Annex I of the Pact for the Future (A/RES/79/1) at the UN Summit of the Future on September 22, 2024, is a multilateral agreement committing UN member states to shared AI governance principles. Key AI provisions include establishing the Independent International Scientific Panel on AI and the Global Dialogue on AI Governance, calling for a global AI fund, and setting data governance and AI transparency commitments. While non-binding in the enforcement sense, it represents the broadest multilateral political consensus on AI governance to date.

title: National Guidelines on Artificial Intelligence Governance and Ethics (AIGE) (MOSTI)
short_title: AIGE Guidelines 2024
issuing_body: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MOSTI)
summary: Non-binding voluntary framework published by the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation with seven principles: fairness, safety, privacy, inclusiveness, transparency, accountability, and human benefit. Sector regulators are expected to develop implementation guidelines based on this national framework.

title: California AI Transparency Act
short_title: California SB 942 (AI Transparency Act)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: California Attorney General
summary: Requires large AI providers (1M+ monthly users) to implement watermarking tools for AI-generated images, video, and audio — both visible labels and imperceptible digital watermarks. Providers must offer free detection tools so users can verify whether content is AI-generated.

title: Political Advertisements: Artificial Intelligence Disclosures
short_title: California AB 2355 (Political Ad AI Disclosure)
issuing_body: California Fair Political Practices Commission
summary: Requires political advertisements that include AI-generated content to include a clear and conspicuous disclosure stating the content was created or substantially altered using AI. Applies to paid political advertisements in any medium. Enforced by the California Fair Political Practices Commission.

title: Artificial Intelligence: Intimate Images
short_title: California SB 926 (AI Nonconsensual Intimate Imagery)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: California courts (criminal and civil)
summary: Expands California's nonconsensual intimate imagery (NCII) law to cover AI-generated or digitally altered intimate images of real, identifiable persons. Creates both criminal liability (misdemeanor/felony depending on intent) and a private civil right of action for victims. Addresses sextortion using AI-generated imagery.

title: Social Media Platforms: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Content
short_title: California SB 981 (Deepfake Intimate Image Reporting — Platforms)
issuing_body: California Attorney General; California courts (civil)
summary: Requires large social media platforms to implement a mechanism allowing users to report sexually explicit AI-generated or digitally altered content depicting real people without their consent. Platforms must provide an easily accessible reporting tool and take action on valid reports. Complements SB 926 by imposing platform-level obligations.

jurisdiction: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
title: "Governing AI for Humanity" — Final Report of the UN Secretary-General's High-Level Advisory Body on Artificial Intelligence
short_title: UN HLAB — Governing AI for Humanity
summary: The final report of the UN Secretary-General's High-Level Advisory Body on Artificial Intelligence, released September 19, 2024 at the Summit of the Future. The 39-member expert body set out seven recommendations for global AI governance, including establishment of a new UN AI office, a global AI fund, an international AI data framework, and a capacity development network. The report informed the Global Digital Compact adopted at the same Summit.

title: Use of Digital Replicas of Deceased Performers Act
short_title: California AB 1836 (Deceased Performer AI)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: California courts (civil)
summary: Extends California right of publicity protections to deceased performers by requiring prior consent from the estate before creating or using an AI-generated digital replica of a deceased performer in an audiovisual work, sound recording, or live performance. Applies to performances and recordings made during the performer's life.

title: Contracts Involving AI Replicas of Performers Act
short_title: California AB 2602 (AI in Entertainment Contracts)
issuing_body: California courts (civil); California Labor Commissioner
summary: Voids provisions in entertainment contracts that grant employers the right to use an AI replica of a performer to replace work the performer would otherwise perform, unless the performer receives specific, individualized notice and representation by a qualified representative. Applies to contracts for audiovisual and sound recording work.

title: Defending Democracy from Deepfake Deception Act of 2024
short_title: California AB 2655 (Defending Democracy from Deepfake Deception Act)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Elections
issuing_body: California courts (civil)
summary: Requires large online platforms to label AI-generated content depicting political candidates or measures within 120 days of an election. Prohibits platforms from distributing materially deceptive AI-generated images or audio of candidates that did not actually make the depicted statements. Platforms must add disclosure labels and may be ordered to remove unlabeled deepfakes.

title: Elections: Deceptive AI Content
short_title: California AB 2839 (Election Deepfakes — Individual Liability)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Elections
issuing_body: California courts (civil)
summary: Prohibits distributing materially deceptive AI-generated images, audio, or video depicting candidates for office or election officials within 120 days of an election without a clear disclosure. Creates a private right of action for candidates, election officials, and the Attorney General. Enacted as urgency statute, effective immediately on signing.

title: Child Sexual Abuse Material: Artificial Intelligence
short_title: California AB 1831 (AI-Generated CSAM)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: California courts (criminal); California Attorney General
summary: Expands California's child sexual abuse material (CSAM) laws to expressly cover AI-generated, computer-generated, or otherwise digitally created depictions of minors engaged in sexual conduct. Makes it a felony to possess, distribute, or produce such material regardless of whether any real child is depicted.

jurisdiction: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
title: G20 Digital Economy Ministerial Declaration — Maceió, Brazil, 2024
short_title: G20 Maceió Digital Economy Ministerial Declaration 2024
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media
summary: G20 Digital Economy Ministers adopted the Maceió Declaration on September 13, 2024, with AI as a central pillar. Ministers agreed on using AI for inclusive and sustainable development, developing interoperable AI governance frameworks across G20 members, labelling of AI-generated content, and an AI Readiness Toolkit to support developing country capacity. The declaration reflects the Brazilian G20 presidency's emphasis on AI equity and inclusion.

title: China AI Safety Governance Framework (SAC NTC260, 2024)
short_title: China AI Safety Governance Framework (SAC NTC260)
topics: General AI governance; National security & defence
summary: China's National Technical Committee 260 on Cybersecurity (SAC NTC260) released the AI Safety Governance Framework in September 2024. The framework establishes principles for AI safety governance, classifies AI safety risks into inherent and systemic categories, and provides guidance on risk identification, assessment, and mitigation across the AI lifecycle. It complements China's binding CAC regulations on generative AI and algorithmic recommendations.

title: Voluntary AI Safety Standard (Australia)
short_title: Australian Voluntary AI Safety Standard
issuing_body: Department of Industry, Science and Resources
summary: The Voluntary AI Safety Standard gives Australian organisations ten guardrails for developing and deploying AI safely and responsibly: accountability and governance, risk management, data governance and protection, testing and monitoring, human control and intervention, user transparency, contestability, supply-chain transparency, record keeping, and stakeholder engagement. The guardrails were designed to align with the mandatory guardrails proposed for high-risk settings so that early adopters would be prepared if those became law.
scope: Voluntary; aimed at organisations deploying AI in Australia, especially deployers of AI systems in higher-risk settings. It creates no legal obligations.

title: Israel Signature of the Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI and Human Rights (CETS 225)
short_title: Israel — Signature of CoE AI Convention (CETS 225)
issuing_body: Government of Israel (national implementation)
summary: Israel signed the Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI, Human Rights, Democracy, and the Rule of Law (CETS 225) on September 5, 2024, becoming one of the first non-European countries to sign. As a signatory, Israel commits to implementing the Convention's principles — human rights safeguards, democratic oversight, and rule of law requirements for AI — upon ratification. The Convention entered into force in 2025 after receiving the required five ratifications. Israel was among the first Middle Eastern countries to sign an international AI governance treaty.

title: Uruguay Signature of the Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI and Human Rights (CETS 225)
short_title: Uruguay — Signature of CoE AI Convention (CETS 225)
issuing_body: Government of Uruguay (national implementation)
summary: Uruguay signed the Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI, Human Rights, Democracy, and the Rule of Law (CETS 225) on September 5, 2024, becoming the first Latin American country to sign an international AI governance treaty. Uruguay's signature reflects its strong data protection tradition (home to one of Latin America's most respected data protection frameworks and the Unidad Reguladora y de Control de Datos Personales, URCDP). As a signatory, Uruguay commits to implementing the Convention's human rights, democratic oversight, and rule of law requirements for AI upon ratification.

title: Qatar Central Bank Artificial Intelligence Guideline for Financial Institutions
short_title: Qatar Central Bank AI Guideline 2024
issuing_body: Qatar Central Bank (QCB)
summary: Binding AI guideline issued by the Qatar Central Bank on September 4, 2024, mandatory for all QCB-licensed financial institutions. Requires licensed entities to develop an AI strategy, conduct AI risk assessments, implement human oversight protocols, and establish AI governance committees at board level. High-risk AI systems (credit scoring, fraud detection, customer authentication) require explicit QCB pre-approval before deployment. Sets minimum standards for AI model documentation, validation, and performance monitoring in the financial sector.

title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption Framework: Maturity Model and Risk Classification
short_title: Saudi Arabia SDAIA AI Adoption Framework 2024
issuing_body: Saudi Data and AI Authority (SDAIA); National Center for AI (NCAI)
summary: Saudi Arabia's SDAIA AI Adoption Framework establishes a maturity model and risk-based classification system for AI adoption across government and the private sector, with a four-tier risk classification (low, limited, high, unacceptable) aligned with OECD and EU AI Act principles. First issued in 2024 and reinforced/re-released in November 2025 as a mandatory baseline that public-sector entities must follow for AI procurement, deployment and governance across five pillars (data governance, model accountability, transparency, human oversight, risk management), positioning SDAIA as the de facto AI regulator for the Saudi public sector. Binding for government entities; referenced as best practice for the private sector. Saudi Arabia declared 2026 the 'Year of AI' but has not yet enacted a standalone AI statute.

title: Regulation on Transfer of Personal Data Outside the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (SDAIA)
short_title: Saudi PDPL Cross-Border Transfer Regulation
issuing_body: Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA); National Data Management Office (NDMO)
summary: Binding regulation under the Saudi Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL) framework (implementing PDPL Article 29) governing cross-border transfers of personal data outside the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Requires adequacy assessments of recipient jurisdictions, standard contractual clauses, or binding corporate/common rules as lawful transfer mechanisms. The original regulation was published in the Official Gazette on 7 September 2023 alongside the PDPL Implementing Regulations; a materially revised version was published and took effect on 1 September 2024 (aligned with full PDPL enforcement), narrowing the recognised safeguards to standard contractual clauses, binding common rules, and certificates of accreditation. SDAIA subsequently issued Data Transfer Risk Assessment guidelines (early 2025). Directly relevant to AI systems that process Saudi personal data internationally.

title: GB 44495-2024 — Technical Requirements for Vehicle Cybersecurity (Mandatory National Standard)
short_title: GB 44495-2024 Vehicle Cybersecurity
issuing_body: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology; State Administration for Market Regulation
summary: Mandatory national standard covering 27 specific cybersecurity test requirements for connected and intelligent vehicles, applicable to new vehicle types from January 2026. Addresses vehicle data handling and cross-border transfer restrictions. Aligned with international standards UNECE R155 and ISO 21434 but includes China-specific requirements for data localization and security management.

title: Circular Externa No. 002 del 21 de agosto de 2024 — Lineamientos sobre el uso de IA en el tratamiento de datos personales (Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio)
short_title: SIC Circular No. 2/2024 (AI & Personal Data)
topics: General AI governance; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC)
summary: Colombia's Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) issued this binding regulatory circular establishing guidelines for data controllers and processors that use AI systems to process personal data. It requires that AI-based processing meet suitability, necessity, reasonableness, and proportionality standards under Colombia's data protection law (Law 1581/2012). The circular recommends Privacy Impact Assessments and privacy-enhancing techniques such as differential privacy, and situates AI governance within the existing data protection compliance framework.

title: FTC Final Rule on the Use of Consumer Reviews and Testimonials — Prohibition on Fake or False Consumer Reviews
short_title: FTC Fake Reviews Final Rule (2024)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media
issuing_body: Federal Trade Commission
summary: The FTC's Final Rule on Consumer Reviews and Testimonials (16 CFR Part 465), effective October 2024, is the first binding federal rule to explicitly prohibit AI-generated fake consumer reviews. It bans buying, creating, or distributing fake reviews including AI-generated ones, prohibits review suppression and insider reviews without disclosure, and imposes civil penalties of up to $51,744 per violation.

title: Illinois Public Act 103-0804 (HB 3773): Artificial intelligence in employment decisions – amendment to the Illinois Human Rights Act
short_title: Illinois HB 3773 (AI in employment, Human Rights Act amendment)
issuing_body: Illinois General Assembly
summary: Signed 9 August 2024 and effective 1 January 2026, the Act makes it a civil-rights violation for an employer to use artificial intelligence in recruitment, hiring, promotion, discipline, discharge or other terms of employment in a way that subjects employees to discrimination on the basis of protected classes, or to use zip codes as a proxy for protected classes. Employers must notify employees when AI is used for such decisions; the Department of Human Rights is to adopt rules on notice.
scope: Employers covered by the Illinois Human Rights Act using AI in employment decisions affecting Illinois employees and applicants.

title: Illinois Artificial Intelligence Video Interview Act — Extended to Employment Analytics
short_title: Illinois AIEA (AI Employment Analytics)
issuing_body: Illinois Department of Labor
summary: Extends Illinois AI employment obligations to include AI-assisted resume screening and candidate evaluation tools, beyond the earlier video interview AI law. Employers must notify candidates when AI analytics are used in the screening process and share race/ethnicity data of candidates reviewed by AI with the state annually.

title: Privacy Protection Law Amendment No. 13 (Israel, 2024)
short_title: Israel Privacy Amendment No. 13 (2024)
topics: Government use of AI; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: Israeli Privacy Protection Authority (PPA / Reshut Hagishut L'Pirtiyut)
summary: Sweeping reform of Israel's 1981 Privacy Protection Law, one of the first national laws to explicitly address AI training data and automated decision-making. Prohibits unauthorized scraping of personal data from the internet for AI model training. Mandates transparency and accountability for AI-based automated decisions affecting individuals. Imposes data minimization, purpose limitation, and security obligations on AI developers.

title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
short_title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
issuing_body: Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy (FMCIDE) with NITDA / NCAIR
summary: The draft strategy sets out Nigeria's vision for AI across five pillars: infrastructure, a thriving AI ecosystem, sectoral adoption, responsible and ethical AI, and governance. It was co-created through a 2024 multi-stakeholder workshop convened by the ministry and includes an implementation roadmap with pilot projects and KPIs. The published document on the NCAIR site is marked as a draft dated August 2024.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy (FMCIDE) with NITDA / NCAIR. Oversight: FMCIDE leads; NITDA and its National Centre for AI and Robotics implement. Stated purpose: Use AI for economic growth, social inclusion and technological leadership.

title: Draft South Africa National Artificial Intelligence (AI) Policy
short_title: Draft South Africa National Artificial Intelligence
issuing_body: Department of Communications and Digital Technologies (DCDT)
summary: Approved by Cabinet in March/April 2026 and gazetted for a 60-day comment period, the draft policy proposed guiding principles, institutional arrangements and implementation pathways for AI across the public and private sectors, building on the department's 2024 National AI Policy Framework. The Minister announced its withdrawal on 26 April 2026 after fictitious citations were found in its reference list, and the withdrawal was formally gazetted in June 2026.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by Department of Communications and Digital Technologies (DCDT). Oversight: DCDT; Cabinet-approved draft published for public comment. Stated purpose: Set national principles, institutions and pathways for safe and inclusive AI adoption.

title: The UAE Charter for the Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
short_title: The UAE Charter for the Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
issuing_body: UAE Cabinet / Artificial Intelligence, Digital Economy and Remote Work Applications Office
summary: A twelve-principle charter approved by the UAE Cabinet setting expectations for AI development and use, including safety, algorithmic bias, data privacy, transparency, human oversight, governance and accountability, and compliance with applicable laws and treaties. It is a guiding framework rather than binding legislation and supports the objectives of the UAE Strategy for AI.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by UAE Cabinet / Artificial Intelligence, Digital Economy and Remote Work Applications Office. Oversight: AI Office under the Minister of State for AI; applies across federal entities. Stated purpose: Guiding principles for safe, ethical and inclusive AI aligned with the 2031 strategy.

title: Disrupt Explicit Forged Images and Non-Consensual Edits Act of 2024
short_title: DEFIANCE Act (2024)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: US District Courts (civil); DOJ (criminal)
summary: Creates a federal civil cause of action for victims of non-consensual intimate digital forgeries (AI-generated NCII). Plaintiffs may sue any person who knowingly produces or possesses NCII with intent to distribute when they know or recklessly disregard that the depicted person did not consent. Allows injunctive relief, actual damages, and attorney fees. Also creates criminal liability under 18 U.S.C.

title: NIST Artificial Intelligence 600-1: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
short_title: NIST AI 600-1 (GenAI Profile)
topics: General AI governance; Data protection & privacy; National security & defence
issuing_body: NIST
summary: NIST AI 600-1 is a companion profile to the AI RMF 1.0, developed pursuant to the Biden EO 14110 mandate, that identifies 12 unique risk categories for generative AI systems — including hallucination, CBRN uplift, data poisoning, and information integrity — and maps over 200 suggested mitigations to the AI RMF's GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, and MANAGE functions. It is a voluntary document but serves as the primary federal technical benchmark for GenAI risk management by federal agencies and the private sector.

title: New Jersey Senate Bill 3432 — Artificial Intelligence Investments
short_title: New Jersey S 3432 — AI Investments and Innovation
summary: Authorizes state investments in AI research, development, and infrastructure in New Jersey. Establishes programs to attract AI companies, fund AI research, and prepare the workforce for AI-driven economy.

title: Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024 (Ethiopia)
short_title: Ethiopia Personal Data Protection Proclamation
issuing_body: Ethiopian Personal Data Protection Commission
summary: Ethiopia's foundational personal data protection law, modeled on the GDPR. AI-relevant provisions include: right to object to automated decision-making affecting individuals' legal interests, data protection impact assessments required for high-risk processing including AI profiling, explicit consent required for biometric data processing, and the right not to be subject to solely automated decisions with significant effects.

title: Delaware House Bill 333 — Delaware Artificial Intelligence Commission Act
short_title: Delaware AI Commission Act (HB 333)
issuing_body: Delaware AI Commission
summary: Delaware HB 333 establishes the Delaware Artificial Intelligence Commission within the Office of the State Auditor, charged with assessing AI risks and benefits across all three branches of state government, recommending AI governance and procurement standards, and reporting annually to the legislature. The Commission has no enforcement powers and imposes no obligations on private industry, and is scheduled to automatically terminate after 10 years.

title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 — Artificial Intelligence Act
short_title: EU AI Act
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Employment & HR; Health; Education; Government use of AI; Law enforcement & justice; Financial services; National security & defence; Frontier / general-purpose AI
issuing_body: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
summary: The EU AI Act is a binding regulation that sets rules for developing, placing on the market and using AI systems in the European Union. It bans a small set of practices considered unacceptable, imposes detailed requirements on "high-risk" AI systems used in areas such as employment, education, credit, essential services, law enforcement and safety-critical products, requires transparency for chatbots and synthetic content, and creates separate duties for providers of general-purpose AI models. Obligations apply in phases between 2025 and 2028.
scope: Applies to providers placing AI systems or general-purpose AI models on the EU market or putting them into service, to deployers established in the EU, and to providers and deployers in third countries where the system's output is used in the EU (Article 2). Excludes AI used exclusively for military, defence or national-security purposes, and activities of purely personal non-professional use. Free and open-source models get partial relief unless they are general-purpose models with systemic risk.

title: Federal Law No. 169-FZ on Amendments to Federal Law on Experimental Legal Regimes in the Field of Digital Innovations
short_title: Russia Federal Law 169-FZ (AI Sandbox Amendment)
issuing_body: Ministry of Digital Development, Communications and Mass Media; Bank of Russia (for financial sector)
summary: Extends and updates Russia's experimental legal regime (regulatory sandbox) framework for AI development under Federal Law No. 258-FZ. Introduces mandatory civil liability insurance for AI developers operating within regulatory sandboxes. Expands the ELR framework to cover generative AI systems, adding content moderation and user disclosure requirements during testing. Updates governance procedures for sandbox applications. Builds on the original 2020 framework that created the Moscow AI digital sandbox.

title: Hawaii Senate Bill 2687 / Act 191 — Prohibition on Materially Deceptive AI-Generated Deepfakes in Elections
short_title: Hawaii SB 2687 / Act 191 (AI Election Deepfakes)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: Hawaii Attorney General
summary: Hawaii Act 191 (SB 2687) prohibited materially deceptive AI-generated media in election campaigns without a prominent disclaimer and provided for civil and criminal enforcement, but enforcement was permanently enjoined by a federal court in early 2026 on First Amendment grounds. The law remains on the books but is unenforceable, making it a significant reference case in national debates about the constitutionality of AI deepfake election laws.

title: White Paper on Artificial Intelligence Regulation in Ukraine (bottom-up roadmap)
short_title: Ukraine AI Regulation White Paper
summary: Non-binding White Paper presented by Ukraine's Ministry of Digital Transformation on 26 Jun 2024, operationalizing the 2023 bottom-up AI Regulation Roadmap. Provides extra-legislative tools (self-assessment methodology, regulatory sandbox, AI-system labelling, voluntary code of conduct) to prepare business and the state for a future binding AI law aligned with the EU AI Act (drafting planned ~2026). This is Ukraine's actual current AI instrument, unlike the mislabelled 'draft law 11175' record (ua-ua-aidraft-2024), which should be re-sourced to this.

title: Quality Control Standards for Automated Valuation Models — 12 CFR Parts 34, 164, 225, 323, 722, 1026
short_title: Interagency AVM Quality Control Final Rule
issuing_body: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB); Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC); Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC); Federal Reserve Board; National Credit Union Administration (NCUA); Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA)
summary: Six federal financial regulators jointly finalized quality control standards requiring mortgage originators and secondary market issuers to adopt policies ensuring automated valuation models (AVMs) produce credible, accurate estimates free from discriminatory bias. Covered entities must implement nondiscrimination controls, data integrity checks, conflict-of-interest safeguards, and random sample testing. The rule implements Section 1473 of the Dodd-Frank Act and is the first binding federal mandate specifically governing AI/ML-based property valuation.

title: Massachusetts H. 4744 — An Act to Prevent Abuse and Exploitation
short_title: Massachusetts H. 4744 (Prevent Abuse and Exploitation Act)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: courts
summary: Massachusetts' first deepfake-specific law criminalizes nonconsensual distribution of intimate images including AI-generated deepfakes, amending the criminal harassment statute. Also establishes coercive control as domestic abuse element and creates teen diversion program for sexting.

title: Nevada Deceptive Artificial Intelligence in Elections Act
short_title: Nevada AB 384 (AI in Elections)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: Nevada Secretary of State; Nevada Attorney General
summary: Prohibits the knowing distribution of materially deceptive AI-generated media depicting a candidate within 60 days of an election without disclosure. Makes knowing violations a Category E felony. Requires disclosure label on AI-generated election content. Nevada's enhanced criminal penalties distinguish it from most state election deepfake laws.

title: Artificial Intelligence: Model Personal Data Protection Framework (Hong Kong Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data)
short_title: Hong Kong PCPD AI Framework 2024
topics: General AI governance; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data (PCPD)
summary: The PCPD's Model Personal Data Protection Framework for AI is Hong Kong's primary practical governance tool for organizations using AI systems that process personal data. Organized around four lifecycle phases — procurement, development, deployment, and monitoring — it provides checklists and guidance for applying the PDPO's six Data Protection Principles to AI contexts, addresses generative AI risks, and recommends AI interaction disclosure, human oversight for significant decisions, regular bias testing, and AI-specific incident response planning.

title: Louisiana Acts 2024, No. 142 (SB 6) — Unlawful Dissemination of AI-Generated Intimate Images (RS 14:73.14)
short_title: Louisiana SB 6 / Act 142 (AI Intimate Images)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: courts
summary: Louisiana's Act 142/2024 criminalizes dissemination or sale of AI-generated intimate images of another person without consent and with intent to coerce, harass, or intimidate. Creates RS 14:73.14. Platforms are not liable for user-generated content under this provision.

title: Tanzania National AI Guidelines 2024
short_title: Tanzania National AI Guidelines 2024
issuing_body: Ministry of Communication and Information Technology (MICIT)
summary: Tanzania's first national AI guidelines, issued by the Ministry of Communication and Information Technology as Draft Version One (Version 2.0, June 2024). Provides guidance for all stakeholders — public and private — on the ethical and secure development, deployment, and adoption of AI. Structured around eight AI principles (Valid and Reliable, Safe, Managed Bias, Resilient, Transparency, Accountability, Explainable and Interpretable, Privacy-Enhanced), a recommended AI Code of Ethics, ten AI Guidelines, and six implementation proposals covering: human agency and control, technical reliability and security, privacy and data management, transparency/explainability/traceability, diversity and non-discrimination, and risk management and accountability. Explicitly states that Tanzania has no specific AI legislation yet, but notes that AI misuse can lead to penalties under the Data Protection Act of 2022. A formal AI legal framework is described as being in development.

title: Vermont Act 161 of 2024 (H.878) — Nonconsensual Deepfake Pornography
short_title: Vermont H.878 / Act 161 (Deepfake Pornography)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: courts
summary: Vermont Act 161/2024 explicitly criminalizes nonconsensual deepfake pornography by amending Vermont's Revenge Porn Statute. AI-generated sexual imagery of identifiable persons without consent is treated equivalently to non-AI intimate image abuse.

title: Arizona SB 1359 — Synthetic Media; Political Advertising; Disclosure
short_title: Arizona SB 1359 (Synthetic Media Election Disclosure)
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: courts; Arizona Secretary of State
summary: Arizona's SB 1359 requires clear disclosure on AI-generated synthetic media used in political advertisements about candidates within 90 days of an election. Civil penalties of $10/day (first 15 days) and $25/day thereafter for non-disclosure. Parody and satire are exempt.

title: Arizona HB 2394 — Digitally Altered Media; Civil Action
short_title: Arizona HB 2394 (Deepfake Civil Remedies)
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: courts
summary: Arizona's HB 2394 creates a civil cause of action for victims depicted in AI-generated deepfakes without consent. Covers political candidates (within 180 days pre-election) and any citizen. Requires actual knowledge by publisher; civil remedies include injunctions and damages. No criminal penalties.

title: Loi n° 2024-449 du 21 mai 2024 visant à sécuriser et à réguler l'espace numérique
short_title: France SREN Law 2024
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: ARCOM; CNIL
summary: France's Digital Space Security and Regulation Law (SREN) introduces the first binding national French rules on AI-generated deepfakes and synthetic content. It criminalizes non-consensual distribution of AI-generated sexual deepfakes, requires content takedown mechanisms for illegal deepfakes, and extends ARCOM's regulatory powers over AI-generated online content.

jurisdiction: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
title: Seoul AI Safety Declarations 2024 (Ministerial Statement and Company Commitments)
short_title: Seoul AI Safety Declarations 2024
summary: Two outputs from the AI Seoul Summit: government ministerial statement on AI safety frameworks and international governance, and voluntary Frontier AI Safety Commitments signed by major AI companies (Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, xAI, and others) on safety evaluations, dangerous capability thresholds, information sharing, and incident reporting. Formally established the international AI Safety Institute network.

title: Minnesota Artificial Intelligence and Elections Disclosure Act
short_title: Minnesota HF 4114 (AI Elections Disclosure)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: Minnesota Secretary of State; Minnesota courts (civil)
summary: Prohibits the creation or distribution of materially deceptive AI-generated audio or visual media depicting a political candidate within 90 days of an election without a disclosure label. Requires prominent disclosure that content is AI-generated. Provides private right of action for candidates.

title: Colorado Senate Bill 24-205: Consumer Protections for Artificial Intelligence (Colorado AI Act)
short_title: Colorado AI Act
topics: General AI governance; Employment & HR; Health; Education; Government use of AI; Consumer protection; Financial services
issuing_body: Colorado General Assembly
summary: The Colorado AI Act requires developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems to use reasonable care to protect consumers from known or reasonably foreseeable risks of algorithmic discrimination. High-risk systems are those that make, or are a substantial factor in making, consequential decisions about education, employment, financial or lending services, essential government services, healthcare, housing, insurance or legal services. Deployers must run risk-management programmes and impact assessments, notify consumers, and explain adverse decisions; developers must document systems and disclose known risks.
scope: Applies to developers and deployers doing business in Colorado of high-risk AI systems affecting Colorado consumers, with exemptions (for example certain small deployers, systems approved by federal agencies, and some regulated financial institutions). Enforcement is exclusively by the Attorney General; there is no private right of action.

title: Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law (CETS No. 225)
short_title: Framework Convention on AI (CETS 225)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe
summary: The first international treaty on AI. Parties must adopt or maintain measures so that activities within the lifecycle of AI systems are consistent with human rights, democracy and the rule of law, covering public authorities and actors on their behalf and, by choice of approach, private actors. It sets principles (human dignity and autonomy, transparency and oversight, accountability, equality and non-discrimination, privacy, reliability, safe innovation), requires remedies, procedural safeguards and risk and impact assessment, allows moratoria or bans for incompatible uses, and creates a Conference of the Parties for follow-up. National-security activities and defence are excluded.
scope: Obligations fall on state parties for the public sector; parties choose how to address private-sector AI activities. Activities related to national security and research and development not yet in use are excluded.

title: Nondiscrimination in Health Programs and Activities — AI Patient Care Decision Support Provisions, 45 CFR Part 92
short_title: HHS Section 1557 Nondiscrimination Rule — AI Provisions
issuing_body: HHS Office for Civil Rights (OCR)
summary: The HHS Office for Civil Rights updated the Section 1557 nondiscrimination rule to explicitly address AI and algorithmic tools used in patient care decisions. Covered health entities must take reasonable steps to identify and mitigate discrimination risks in patient care decision support tools — including AI/ML clinical algorithms, prior authorization tools, and risk scoring systems — used to make or support decisions about patient care. The AI-specific provisions became effective May 2025; some other portions of the rule remain under litigation.

title: Iowa HF 2240 — Digitally Altered Intimate Images
short_title: Iowa HF 2240 (Deepfake Harassment)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: courts
summary: Iowa's HF 2240 criminalizes distribution of digitally altered (AI-generated) intimate images without consent as an aggravated misdemeanor. Extends the existing revenge porn statute to AI-generated content.

title: CS/HB 919 — Artificial Intelligence Use in Political Advertising
short_title: Florida HB 919 (AI in Elections)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: Florida Division of Elections; Florida Attorney General
summary: Requires political advertisements containing AI-generated content to include a clear and conspicuous disclosure stating the content was "created in whole or in part with the use of generative artificial intelligence." Applies to television, radio, digital, and print political advertising in Florida.

title: DHS Guidelines for AI Safety and Security in Critical Infrastructure (April 2024)
short_title: DHS AI Critical Infrastructure Safety Guidelines
summary: Issued pursuant to the Biden AI Executive Order (EO 14110), DHS published this Roles and Responsibilities Framework assigning accountability across the AI supply chain for critical infrastructure sectors. It defines responsibilities for cloud and compute providers, AI developers, critical infrastructure owners/operators, and civil society. The framework addresses AI-specific risks to the 16 critical infrastructure sectors and provides sector-specific guidance.

title: Alabama House Bill 172 — Prohibition on Materially Deceptive AI-Generated Media in Elections
short_title: Alabama HB 172 (AI Election Deepfakes)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: Alabama Attorney General; District Attorneys
summary: Alabama HB 172 makes it a criminal offense to knowingly distribute materially deceptive AI-generated media intended to influence an election within 90 days before that election, and requires a prominent disclaimer for any AI-generated content used in political advertising. First violations are Class A misdemeanors; repeat violations within five years are Class C felonies. Satire and parody are exempted.

title: Alabama House Bill 161 — Prohibition on Nonconsensual AI-Generated Intimate Images
short_title: Alabama HB 161 (AI NCII)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Data protection & privacy; Online safety & children
issuing_body: Alabama Attorney General; District Attorneys
summary: Alabama HB 161 prohibits the creation and distribution of nonconsensual AI-generated sexually explicit images of identifiable real persons, including both fully AI-generated images and AI-manipulated real photographs, providing criminal penalties (Class A misdemeanor) and a private civil cause of action for victims including actual, statutory, and punitive damages.

title: West Virginia House Bill 5690 — West Virginia Task Force on Artificial Intelligence Act
short_title: West Virginia HB 5690 (AI Task Force)
issuing_body: Governor's Office of Technology
summary: Creates the West Virginia Task Force on Artificial Intelligence within the Governor's Office of Technology. Members include state officials, industry representatives, and academic experts. Tasked with defining AI for state purposes, determining appropriate oversight responsibilities, identifying best practices for government AI use, and recommending legislative and regulatory frameworks. Report required by July 1, 2025. Advisory only — no industry obligations created.

title: AI Guidelines for Business
short_title: AI Guidelines for Business
issuing_body: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry and Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications
summary: The AI Guidelines for Business consolidate Japan's previous AI R&D, utilisation and governance guidelines into a single non-binding document addressed to AI developers, providers and business users. They set common guiding principles (such as human-centricity, safety, fairness, privacy, security, transparency and accountability) and describe agile governance practices, with an appendix of practical methods and checklists. The guidelines are updated periodically; version 1.0 was issued in April 2024 and version 1.2 in March 2026.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry and Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications. Oversight: METI and MIC jointly maintain; secretariat shared with IPA/AI Safety Institute; voluntary adoption by developers, providers and users. Stated purpose: Unify earlier AI ethics and governance guidelines into one voluntary, risk-based guide for business.

title: Iowa SF 2243 — Sexual Exploitation of Minors; Digitally Altered Images
short_title: Iowa SF 2243 (AI-Generated CSAM)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: courts
summary: Iowa's SF 2243 adds deepfake and digitally altered images to the definition of child pornography in Iowa law. AI-generated depictions of minors in sexual acts are treated equivalently to real CSAM. Passed unanimously (93-0 House, 46-0 Senate).

title: Virginia H 1083 — Office of Education Economics
short_title: Virginia H 1083 — Office of Education Economics
summary: Directs the Secretary of Education to convene a work group to review and develop a work plan related to the Virginia Longitudinal Data System and the Virginia Workforce Data Trust.

title: OMB Memorandum M-24-10: Advancing Governance, Innovation, and Risk Management for Agency Use of Artificial Intelligence
short_title: OMB M-24-10 (Federal AI Governance Memo)
summary: OMB M-24-10, issued March 28, 2024 under the Biden administration, was the primary binding governance framework for federal agency use of AI. It required each CFO Act agency to designate a Chief AI Officer (CAIO) within 60 days, establish an AI governance board, maintain an annual public inventory of AI use cases, and develop enterprise AI strategies. The memo established mandatory minimum risk-management practices for 'rights-impacting AI' and 'safety-impacting AI' — requiring AI impact assessments, ongoing monitoring, and human oversight before such systems could be used. Agencies that could not comply by December 1, 2024 were required to cease using non-compliant systems. M-24-10 was rescinded and replaced by OMB M-25-21 on April 3, 2025, by the Trump administration.

title: Virginia S 731 — Child Pornography Financing
short_title: Virginia S 731 — Child Pornography Financing
summary: Relates to production, publication, sale, financing of child pornography, relates to penalty, amends the definition of child pornography to include material that depicts a minor in a state of nudity or engaged in sexual conduct, as defined, where such depiction is obscene.

title: Wisconsin 2023 Act 123 — AI Disclosures in Political Communications
short_title: Wisconsin 2023 Act 123 (AI Political Disclosures)
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: Wisconsin Elections Commission
summary: Wisconsin requires disclosure when AI-generated audio or video (deepfakes) is used in political advertisements. Covers synthetic media in political communications; does not ban use, only mandates disclosure. Note: does not cover AI-generated photos.

title: India MeitY AI Advisory Note — Responsible Development and Deployment of AI (March 2024)
short_title: India MeitY AI Advisory (2024)
summary: India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) issued this advisory requiring all intermediaries and platforms to ensure AI models, LLMs, and generative AI tools do not produce unlawful content, do not enable bias or discrimination or threaten electoral integrity, and that under-tested AI is labelled with fallibility warnings. It also requires deepfake/synthetic media to be embedded with permanent unique metadata for traceability. Compliance required with immediate effect.

title: Ukraine Draft Law on Artificial Intelligence (No. 11175)
short_title: Ukraine Draft AI Law (2024)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media
issuing_body: National Authority for Cybersecurity (proposed); Ministry of Digital Transformation
summary: Ukraine has NOT enacted any AI law. The 'Draft Law No. 11175' could not be verified as a real bill, and the stored card URL (itd.rada.gov.ua/billInfo/Bills/Card/44497) actually resolves to an unrelated social-sphere bill (No. 11377 / Act 4607-IX). Ukraine's actual current AI instrument is the non-binding White Paper on AI Regulation (Ministry of Digital Transformation, 26 Jun 2024), part of a bottom-up roadmap; a binding EU-AI-Act-aligned law is only planned for submission around Q4 2026. Recommend re-sourcing this record to the White Paper (see new candidate ua-ua-aiwhitepaper-2024).

title: Indiana Deceptive AI Political Content Prohibition Act
short_title: Indiana SB 10 (Deepfakes Elections)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: Indiana Election Commission; Indiana Attorney General
summary: Prohibits the distribution of materially deceptive AI-generated audio or visual media depicting a candidate within 90 days before an election without clear disclosure. Requires a disclosure label stating the content is AI-generated. Indiana Election Commission may impose civil penalties.

title: IndiaAI Mission
short_title: IndiaAI Mission
issuing_body: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (Union Cabinet approval)
summary: A five-year national programme approved by the Union Cabinet with an outlay of about INR 10,372 crore. It funds shared public AI compute (10,000+ GPUs), an innovation centre for indigenous foundation models, a datasets platform, application development for public problems, skilling programmes, startup financing and work on safe and trusted AI. Implementation is handled by the IndiaAI division of Digital India Corporation.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (Union Cabinet approval). Oversight: IndiaAI Independent Business Division under Digital India Corporation, MeitY. Stated purpose: Build sovereign AI compute, data and model capacity and fund the domestic AI ecosystem.

title: New Mexico House Bill 182 — Prohibition on Materially Deceptive AI-Generated Content in Political Advertising
short_title: New Mexico HB 182 (AI Political Advertising)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: New Mexico Attorney General; District Attorneys
summary: New Mexico HB 182 prohibits the distribution of political advertising containing materially deceptive AI-generated depictions of candidates or public officials within 90 days of an election without a prominent disclosure, providing for criminal misdemeanor penalties and civil enforcement by the AG or affected candidates. The law explicitly exempts satire and parody and was effective May 15, 2024.

title: Guangdong Province Artificial Intelligence Industry Development Regulations
short_title: Guangdong AI Industry Development Regulations
issuing_body: Guangdong Provincial Department of Industry and Information Technology; Guangdong Cyberspace Administration
summary: Guangdong's AI Industry Development Regulations, building on Shanghai's 2022 model, establish a provincial framework for AI development and governance. Key provisions include: provincial AI innovation corridors (Shenzhen-Hong Kong, Guangzhou), safe harbour certification for compliant AI products, training data governance requirements, risk assessment for AI in critical applications, and provincial AI standard-setting in manufacturing and industrial AI.

title: PDPC Advisory Guidelines on Use of Personal Data in AI Recommendation and Decision Systems
short_title: PDPC AI advisory guidelines
issuing_body: Personal Data Protection Commission Singapore
summary: These advisory guidelines explain how the Personal Data Protection Act applies when organisations use personal data to develop, test and deploy AI systems that make recommendations, predictions or decisions. They clarify the consent obligation and relevant exceptions (business improvement and research), what to include in notifications to individuals, accountability practices such as documenting data provenance and model development, and expectations for service providers building bespoke AI systems.
scope: Organisations subject to the PDPA that use personal data in AI recommendation and decision systems, and service providers developing such systems for them. Advisory; not legally binding, but reflects how the PDPC interprets binding PDPA obligations.

title: Kuwait CITRA Data Privacy Protection Regulation No. 26/2024
short_title: Kuwait CITRA Data Privacy Regulation 2024
issuing_body: Kuwait Communications and Information Technology Regulatory Authority (CITRA)
summary: Binding data privacy regulation issued by Kuwait's Communications and Information Technology Regulatory Authority (CITRA) applying to CITRA-licensed telecom and IT service providers. Requires explicit consent for data processing, 72-hour breach notification, data localization for sensitive tiers, and cross-border adequacy assessments. Kuwait's primary data privacy instrument covering AI-processing entities in the licensed sector. Regulation No. 26/2024 (effective 19 February 2024) repealed and replaced the earlier Data Privacy Protection Regulation No. 42/2021; a companion instrument, No. 34/2024, replaced the data classification regulation No. 95/2021. A one-year grace period ran from Official Gazette publication (~March 2024).

title: Continental Artificial Intelligence Strategy
short_title: Continental Artificial Intelligence Strategy
issuing_body: African Union Commission (endorsed by the AU Executive Council)
summary: A continental framework that guides AU member states on harnessing AI for development while managing risks. It is organised around five focus areas: capturing AI benefits, building capabilities, minimising risks, stimulating investment, and fostering cooperation. It is non-binding and intended to inform national strategies and regional harmonisation.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by African Union Commission (endorsed by the AU Executive Council). Oversight: AU Commission coordinates; member states implement nationally. Stated purpose: Africa-centric, development-focused AI adoption aligned with Agenda 2063.

title: Национальная стратегия развития искусственного интеллекта на период до 2030 года (Presidential Decree No. 490 of 10 October 2019, as amended by Decree No. 124 of 15 February 2024)
short_title: National AI Strategy to 2030 (Decree 490, updated 2024)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: President of the Russian Federation
summary: The national strategy sets goals for AI research, compute, data, talent and adoption across the economy and public administration to 2030, with the 2024 amendment adding targets on domestic compute capacity, large generative models, share of organisations using AI, and trusted-AI requirements for the public sector. It is implemented through the federal "Artificial Intelligence" project.
scope: Government programme; obligations arise only through implementing acts.

title: Morocco Commission Nationale de Contrôle de la Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel — AI and Personal Data Guidelines
short_title: Morocco CNDP AI Data Protection Guidance
issuing_body: CNDP (Commission Nationale de contrôle de la Protection des Données à caractère Personnel)
summary: Morocco's CNDP issued guidelines in 2024 on the application of Law 09-08 to AI systems processing personal data. The guidelines address: lawful basis for AI training data collection, transparency obligations for automated processing, DPIA requirements for high-risk AI, right to human review of algorithmic decisions, and restrictions on biometric AI use. Morocco's CNDP is one of the most active data protection authorities in Africa and Francophone world.

title: National Cyber Security Agency Guidelines for the Secure Adoption and Usage of Artificial Intelligence (Qatar NCSA)
short_title: Qatar NCSA AI Security Guidelines 2024
issuing_body: Qatar National Cyber Security Agency (NCSA)
summary: A 36-page bilingual guidance document from Qatar's National Cyber Security Agency covering the secure development lifecycle for AI systems, model validation, data integrity, and supply chain risk management. Applies to organisations using AI in critical infrastructure and serves as a baseline for NCSA cybersecurity assessments. Non-binding but operationally influential for NCSA-assessed entities.

title: Abu Dhabi Law No. 3 of 2024 — On Establishing the Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Technology Council (AIATC)
short_title: Abu Dhabi AI & Advanced Tech Law 2024
issuing_body: Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Technology Council (AIATC)
summary: Abu Dhabi law establishing the Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Technology Council (AIATC) as the emirate's supreme authority for AI and advanced technology. The Council has independent legal personality and reports directly to the Ruler of Abu Dhabi. Its mandate covers strategy development, investment, regulatory proposals, attracting global companies, coordinating government and private sector AI activity, and directly investing in and establishing AI companies. All concerned government and private entities are legally obligated to implement Council regulations and cooperate with it. Supersedes/complements the Advanced Technology Research Council (ATRC) established by Abu Dhabi Law No. 14/2020.
