jurisdiction: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
title: Ethics and Governance of Artificial Intelligence for Health: Guidance on Large Multi-Modal Models (WHO)
short_title: WHO Guidance on Large Multi-Modal AI Models for Health
topics: General AI governance; Health; Data protection & privacy
summary: WHO guidance published January 18, 2024, building on the 2021 WHO Ethics and Governance of AI for Health framework. Contains over 40 recommendations for governments, technology companies, and healthcare providers on the use of large multimodal AI models in health settings. Key topics include bias mitigation, informed consent for AI-assisted care, liability allocation, hallucination risks, and equitable access. Widely referenced by national health regulators developing AI policies.

title: ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics
short_title: ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics (2024)
topics: General AI governance; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: ASEAN Digital Ministers' Meeting
summary: Endorsed at the 4th ASEAN Digital Ministers' Meeting in February 2024, the guide sets seven guiding principles (transparency and explainability, fairness and equity, security and safety, human-centricity, privacy and data governance, accountability and integrity, robustness and reliability) and a four-part governance framework (internal governance structures, human involvement in decision-making, operations management, stakeholder interaction), with national and regional recommendations including an ASEAN working group on AI governance.
scope: Voluntary; for organisations deploying traditional AI in commercial and non-military contexts across ASEAN member states.

title: Decisión Administrativa 899/2024 – Mesa Interministerial sobre Inteligencia Artificial (Administrative Decision 899/2024 – Interministerial Board on Artificial Intelligence)
short_title: Decisión Administrativa 899/2024
issuing_body: Jefatura de Gabinete de Ministros
summary: This administrative decision restructures the Interministerial Board on AI originally created in 2023, placing it under the presidency of the Secretariat of Innovation, Science and Technology and expanding its membership to ministries including Defence, Economy, Foreign Affairs, Health, Security, Human Capital, Justice and State Deregulation. The board is tasked with coordinating the government's approach to AI adoption across economic and social sectors and with developing national strategies. Argentina has not yet adopted a standalone national AI strategy or a binding AI law.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by Jefatura de Gabinete de Ministros. Oversight: Board chaired by the Secretaría de Innovación, Ciencia y Tecnología, co-coordinated with the Secretaría de Asuntos Estratégicos, with ministry members. Stated purpose: Coordinate national AI policy across ministries.

title: Plano Brasileiro de Inteligência Artificial 2024-2028 – PBIA (Brazilian Artificial Intelligence Plan 2024-2028)
short_title: Plano Brasileiro de Inteligência Artificial 2024-2028
issuing_body: Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação (MCTI) with the Conselho Nacional de Ciência e Tecnologia (CCT)
summary: The PBIA is a four-year national plan that commits around R$23 billion to AI infrastructure, skills, public-sector applications, business innovation and governance. Headline measures include acquiring a top-tier supercomputer powered by renewable energy, developing Portuguese-language models, and short-term actions in health, education, agriculture and public services. The proposal was presented at the 5th National Conference on Science, Technology and Innovation and formally approved by the CCT through Resolução CCT nº 4/2024, with a final version later published under MCTI coordination.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação (MCTI) with the Conselho Nacional de Ciência e Tecnologia (CCT). Oversight: MCTI coordinates implementation; plan proposal approved by the CCT. Stated purpose: Build sovereign AI capacity and public-interest AI applications.

title: Política Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial – Actualización 2024 y Plan de Acción (National Artificial Intelligence Policy – 2024 Update and Action Plan)
short_title: Política Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial
issuing_body: Ministerio de Ciencia, Tecnología, Conocimiento e Innovación (MinCiencia)
summary: Chile updated its 2021 National AI Policy in 2024, keeping the ten-year horizon to 2031 but reorienting it around ethics, governance and inclusion after a participatory process across the country's regions. The accompanying action plan lists 177 initiatives coordinated by 14 ministries under axes covering enabling factors, development and adoption, and governance and ethics, with periodic progress reporting. The update was presented on 2 May 2024 together with the announcement of a government bill to regulate AI systems.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by Ministerio de Ciencia, Tecnología, Conocimiento e Innovación (MinCiencia). Oversight: MinCiencia leads; interministerial coordination with semi-annual monitoring of the action plan. Stated purpose: Steer ethical, inclusive AI development and prepare the ground for regulation.

title: Estrategia Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial de Costa Rica 2024–2027
short_title: National AI Strategy 2024–2027
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of Costa Rica (MICITT)
summary: Launched in October 2024, the strategy sets pillars on governance and ethics, talent and skills, research and innovation, infrastructure and data, and adoption in the public sector and productive sectors, with an action plan to 2027 informed by UNESCO's Readiness Assessment Methodology.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Estrategia para el desarrollo y uso de la inteligencia artificial en Cuba
short_title: National AI strategy (2024)
topics: General AI governance; Health; Education; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of Cuba (Ministry of Communications)
summary: The strategy sets principles for the ethical development and use of AI in Cuba, priorities for public administration, health and education, and a governance structure led by the Ministry of Communications.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Eesti tehisintellekti tegevuskava 2024–2026 (Estonia's national AI action plan)
short_title: National AI strategy 2024–2026
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications
summary: The third Estonian AI action plan continues the "kratt" programme: adoption of AI in public services and the Bürokratt virtual-assistant ecosystem, support for private-sector use, skills and research, data availability, and preparation for the EU AI Act, including public-sector guidelines on generative AI.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: National Artificial Intelligence Policy of Ethiopia
short_title: National AI Policy (2024)
topics: General AI governance; Health; Education; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Council of Ministers of Ethiopia (Ethiopian Artificial Intelligence Institute)
summary: Approved by the Council of Ministers in 2024, the policy sets objectives for AI research and talent, adoption in agriculture, health, education, security and public services, data governance and infrastructure, and ethical, responsible use, with the Ethiopian AI Institute as implementing body.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: A Blueprint for Greece's AI Transformation – report of the AI Advisory Committee
short_title: Blueprint for Greece's AI transformation (2024)
topics: General AI governance; Health; Education; Government use of AI
issuing_body: AI Advisory Committee to the Prime Minister of Greece
summary: Delivered in November 2024, the Advisory Committee's report proposes a national AI strategy: public-sector AI deployment, AI in health, education and agriculture, sovereign Greek language models, compute, skills, regulatory sandboxes and governance aligned with the EU AI Act.
scope: Recommendations to the government; no obligations for organisations.

title: Artificial Intelligence: Model Personal Data Protection Framework
short_title: PCPD Model Personal Data Protection Framework for AI (2024)
issuing_body: Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data, Hong Kong
summary: Published 11 June 2024, the framework gives organisations that procure, implement and use AI systems involving personal data recommendations in four areas: AI strategy and governance (an AI governance committee, procurement due diligence), risk assessment and human oversight (a risk-based approach with levels of human involvement), customisation and implementation of AI models (data preparation, testing, security), and communication and engagement with stakeholders (transparency, explainability, opt-out, feedback). It builds on the 2021 Guidance on the Ethical Development and Use of AI.
scope: Voluntary for organisations in Hong Kong deploying AI with personal data; compliance with the Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance remains mandatory.

title: Aðgerðaáætlun um gervigreind 2024–2026 (Action plan on artificial intelligence)
short_title: AI action plan 2024–2026
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of Iceland
summary: The 2024–2026 action plan implements Iceland's AI policy with measures on AI in public services, the Icelandic language in AI systems, skills and research, ethics and security, and preparation for the EU AI Act.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

jurisdiction: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
country: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
title: UN General Assembly resolution A/RES/78/265: Seizing the opportunities of safe, secure and trustworthy artificial intelligence systems for sustainable development (21 March 2024)
short_title: UN General Assembly resolution 78/265 on safe, secure and trustworthy AI
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: United Nations General Assembly
summary: The first General Assembly resolution on AI, adopted by consensus with more than 120 co-sponsors, encourages states to promote safe, secure and trustworthy AI systems that respect human rights and advance the Sustainable Development Goals, to close digital divides, and to develop governance frameworks and interoperable safeguards; it calls on companies to act responsibly. It was followed by resolution A/RES/79/325 (August 2025) establishing an Independent International Scientific Panel on AI and a Global Dialogue on AI Governance under the Global Digital Compact.
scope: Recommendatory; addressed to member states, the UN system and stakeholders.

title: Strategia Italiana per l'Intelligenza Artificiale 2024-2026
short_title: Italian AI Strategy 2024–2026
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI; Frontier / general-purpose AI
issuing_body: Presidency of the Council of Ministers (Department for Digital Transformation) and AgID
summary: The 2024–2026 strategy, drafted by an expert committee for the Department for Digital Transformation and published in July 2024, organises action around research, public administration, enterprises and training, with a foundation-model and compute agenda, an AI foundation to coordinate delivery and a monitoring framework.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: National Artificial Intelligence Policy Framework (AI Task Force report)
short_title: National AI policy framework (2024)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of Jamaica (National AI Task Force)
summary: The task force report proposes a national AI policy with principles for responsible AI, a governance structure, skills and research programmes, public-sector use cases and sector priorities.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Концепция развития искусственного интеллекта на 2024–2029 годы
short_title: Concept for AI development 2024–2029
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan
summary: Approved by government decree in July 2024, the concept sets targets for AI infrastructure (supercomputing, data), talent, adoption in the public sector and economy, a national AI platform and regulatory development that led to the 2025 AI law.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Lebanon National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2024–2030
short_title: National AI Strategy 2024–2030
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of Lebanon (OMSAR)
summary: The strategy sets objectives for AI governance and ethics, talent and research, adoption in public services and the economy, and data infrastructure, drawing on UNESCO's readiness assessment.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Mongolia National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
short_title: National AI strategy (2024)
topics: General AI governance; Education; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of Mongolia
summary: The strategy sets goals for AI in public services, the economy, education and research, data and infrastructure, and ethical AI governance.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: National Programme for Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Digital Technologies; AI policy for government entities
short_title: National AI programme and government AI policy (2024)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of Oman (MTCIT)
summary: The programme sets AI adoption goals for government and priority sectors, talent and research initiatives and an AI policy with ethical principles and governance requirements for government entities.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Strengthening Cyber Security and Building Trust in the Public Sector Act, 2024 (Bill 194), Schedule 1: Enhancing Digital Security and Trust Act, 2024
short_title: Ontario Enhancing Digital Security and Trust Act, 2024 (Bill 194)
topics: Health; Education; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Legislative Assembly of Ontario
summary: The Act allows the Ontario government to make regulations governing the use of AI systems by public-sector entities (ministries, agencies, hospitals, school boards, municipalities as prescribed): requirements to disclose AI use, to develop and implement accountability frameworks, to take steps to manage risks, to have human oversight, and prohibitions on prescribed uses. It also addresses cyber security and children's digital information.
scope: Ontario public-sector entities as prescribed by regulation; not private organisations.

title: Working for Workers Four Act, 2024 (Bill 149): disclosure of artificial intelligence use in publicly advertised job postings
short_title: Ontario Working for Workers Four Act (AI disclosure in job postings)
issuing_body: Legislative Assembly of Ontario
summary: Amends the Employment Standards Act, 2000 to require employers with 25 or more employees to disclose in every publicly advertised job posting whether artificial intelligence is used to screen, assess or select applicants, alongside new rules on salary ranges and Canadian-experience requirements. The AI disclosure requirement is in force from 1 January 2026.
scope: Employers in Ontario with 25 or more employees publishing public job postings.

title: Política Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial del Paraguay
short_title: National AI Policy (2024)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of Paraguay (MITIC)
summary: Presented in 2024, the policy sets objectives on ethical and human-centred AI, capacity building, public-sector adoption, data and infrastructure, and research, aligned with the UNESCO recommendation.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Strategia Națională în domeniul Inteligenței Artificiale 2024–2027
short_title: National AI Strategy 2024–2027
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of Romania
summary: Approved by government decision in July 2024, the strategy sets objectives on infrastructure and data, research and innovation, skills, public-sector and business adoption, and governance and ethics aligned with the EU AI Act, with an action plan and monitoring indicators.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Generative AI Governance Guidelines (Saudi Data and AI Authority, 2024)
short_title: Saudi Generative AI Governance Guidelines
topics: General AI governance; Frontier / general-purpose AI
issuing_body: Saudi Data and AI Authority (SDAIA)
summary: Operational governance guidance for generative AI systems published by the Saudi Data and AI Authority (SDAIA). Full text unavailable at time of record creation.

title: Generative AI Public Guidelines (Saudi Data and AI Authority, 2024)
short_title: Saudi Generative AI Public Guidelines
issuing_body: Saudi Data and AI Authority (SDAIA)
summary: Public-facing guidance on responsible use of generative AI systems published by the Saudi Data and AI Authority (SDAIA). Full text unavailable at time of record creation.

title: Sierra Leone National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
short_title: National AI Strategy (2024)
topics: General AI governance; Health; Education; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of Sierra Leone
summary: The strategy sets priorities on AI in public services, health, agriculture and education, skills and research, data infrastructure and ethical governance.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: National Strategy on Artificial Intelligence for Sri Lanka
short_title: National AI Strategy (2024)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of Sri Lanka (Ministry of Digital Economy)
summary: The strategy sets priorities on AI skills and research, public-sector and industry adoption, data and compute infrastructure, and responsible-AI governance, with a national AI centre and implementation task force.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Färdplan för Sverige – AI-kommissionens slutbetänkande (SOU 2024:94)
short_title: AI Commission roadmap for Sweden (SOU 2024:94)
topics: General AI governance; Health; Government use of AI
issuing_body: AI Commission appointed by the Government of Sweden
summary: The government-appointed AI Commission's final report sets out a roadmap for Sweden with around 75 proposals: a national AI task force and data factory, compute and skills investment, AI in public administration and health care, access to data for research and innovation, and measures to make the most of the EU AI Act. It estimates costs and proposes a funding envelope over several years.
scope: Recommendations to the government; no obligations for organisations.

title: 人工智慧基本法 (Artificial Intelligence Basic Act) – draft approved by the Executive Yuan, July 2024
short_title: Artificial Intelligence Basic Act (draft)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI; Consumer protection
issuing_body: Executive Yuan of Taiwan (National Science and Technology Council)
summary: A framework act setting seven principles for AI development and use, requiring the government to promote AI research, talent and infrastructure, to establish a risk-classification framework and safety standards, to protect personal data, labour and consumers, to provide for liability, disclosure of AI-generated content and non-discrimination, and to designate competent authorities by sector, with the NSTC coordinating.
scope: Framework obligations on government agencies; obligations for private actors arise through sector regulation adopted under the act.

title: Ensuring Likeness, Voice, and Image Security (ELVIS) Act of 2024 (Tennessee Public Chapter 588)
short_title: Tennessee ELVIS Act
issuing_body: Tennessee General Assembly
summary: Signed 21 March 2024 and effective 1 July 2024, the ELVIS Act updates Tennessee's Personal Rights Protection Act to add voice to the protected attributes of name, photograph and likeness, prohibits publishing or making available an individual's voice or likeness without authorisation, and creates liability for distributing or making available an algorithm, software or tool whose primary purpose is producing an individual's voice or likeness without authorisation. It provides civil actions for individuals and licensees and criminal penalties.
scope: Anyone producing, publishing or distributing unauthorised AI-generated voice or likeness of individuals in Tennessee, and providers of tools primarily for that purpose.

title: Yapay Zekâ Kanunu Teklifi (Artificial Intelligence Law proposal submitted to the Grand National Assembly, June 2024)
short_title: Draft Artificial Intelligence Law (2024)
topics: General AI governance; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: Grand National Assembly of Türkiye (private member's bill)
summary: A short framework bill proposing principles for AI (safety, transparency, fairness, accountability, privacy), a risk-based approach with registration of high-risk systems, operator obligations and penalties, and supervision by designated authorities, broadly modelled on the EU AI Act.
scope: Would apply to developers, providers and users of AI systems in Türkiye if enacted.

title: Estrategia Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial del Uruguay 2024-2030 (National Artificial Intelligence Strategy of Uruguay 2024-2030)
short_title: Estrategia Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial del Uruguay 2024-2030
issuing_body: Agencia de Gobierno Electrónico y Sociedad de la Información y del Conocimiento (Agesic)
summary: Uruguay's 2024-2030 strategy was approved on 21 November 2024 by the public-sector Strategic Committee for AI and Data after a participatory process involving more than 300 people from state bodies, civil society and the private sector, with technical support from CAF and UNESCO. It sets guiding principles and three objectives: governance and safeguards for ethical and safe AI, national capabilities in infrastructure, data and talent, and use of AI for sustainable development and better public services. A roadmap with goals and semi-annual reporting accompanies the strategy.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by Agencia de Gobierno Electrónico y Sociedad de la Información y del Conocimiento (Agesic). Oversight: Agesic leads implementation under the Comité Estratégico del Sector Público para IA y Datos, with mid-term review and periodic progress reports. Stated purpose: Ethical, sovereign AI development supporting sustainable growth.

title: Utah Artificial Intelligence Policy Act (SB 149, 2024, as amended by SB 226 and SB 332 in 2025)
short_title: Utah Artificial Intelligence Policy Act (SB 149)
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Employment & HR; Health; Consumer protection
issuing_body: Utah State Legislature
summary: Effective 1 May 2024, the Act requires a person using generative AI to interact with a consumer in a consumer transaction to disclose clearly that the consumer is interacting with AI when asked (as amended in 2025, when the interaction is high-risk or on request), and requires providers of regulated occupations (for example health and legal services) to disclose generative-AI use proactively. It states that using AI is no defence to consumer-protection violations, created the Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy and an AI learning laboratory allowing regulatory mitigation agreements, and originally sunset in 2025, extended to 2027.
scope: Businesses using generative AI in consumer transactions in Utah and regulated occupations; enforced by the Division of Consumer Protection.

title: Zambia National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
short_title: National AI Strategy (2024)
topics: General AI governance; Health; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of Zambia (Ministry of Technology and Science)
summary: The strategy sets objectives on AI skills and research, adoption in public services, agriculture, health and mining, data infrastructure and responsible-AI governance.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Circular Letter of the Minister of Communication and Informatics No. 9 of 2023 on Artificial Intelligence Ethics
short_title: Indonesia AI Ethics Circular (SE 9/2023)
topics: General AI governance; Data protection & privacy
summary: Voluntary (non-binding) AI ethics guidance issued 2023-12-19 for public and private electronic-system operators. Sets ethical values (inclusivity, humanity, security, transparency, data protection) and directs internal AI ethics/data-governance policies, risk assessments, and disclosure of AI-generated content. Currently Indonesia's principal AI-specific instrument pending the draft Perpres.

title: FTC Policy Statement on Artificial Intelligence and Algorithmic Decision-Making
short_title: FTC AI Policy Statement (2023)
issuing_body: Federal Trade Commission (FTC)
summary: The FTC's 2023 Policy Statement on AI articulates the Commission's approach to AI enforcement under existing FTC Act authority. It asserts that unfair or deceptive AI practices, discriminatory algorithmic decisions, unfair data collection for AI training, and deceptive AI claims all fall within the FTC's existing Section 5 jurisdiction. The statement covers generative AI, algorithmic pricing, biometric data, and synthetic media.

title: Michigan Public Acts 263-266 — AI in Political Advertising Package
short_title: Michigan PA 263-266 (Deepfakes in Elections)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: Michigan law enforcement; Michigan courts
summary: Four-bill package criminalizing AI-generated deepfakes in elections. Requires disclosure of AI use in political ads. Criminalizes knowingly distributing materially deceptive AI media within 90 days of election with intent to harm a candidate or deceive voters. Establishes Class E felony penalties. One of the earliest state election deepfake laws.

jurisdiction: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
title: Guiding Document on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence Use in the Member States of the Cooperation Council for the Arab States of the Gulf
short_title: GCC AI Ethics Guideline
topics: General AI governance; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: GCC General Secretariat; Member state national authorities
summary: Published by the GCC General Secretariat in November 2023 and explicitly grounded in the UNESCO AI Ethics Recommendation (2021), this non-binding guiding document establishes a shared ethical framework for AI development and use across all six GCC member states (Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, UAE). It sets out four foundational values — respect for human dignity and autonomy; respect for Islamic Sharia, constitutions, and Gulf cohesion; environmental protection and sustainability; and promotion of peaceful use for citizens' welfare — alongside seven principles: (1) decisions are for humans; (2) safety and prevention of harm; (3) justice, equity, and non-discrimination; (4) privacy and data protection; (5) transparency and explainability; (6) responsibility, accountability, and awareness; (7) integrity and non-falsification. Each principle includes concrete recommendations covering human oversight activation, fallback plans, dataset auditing, traceability, explainability, legal accountability legislation, and awareness promotion. Member states are directed to use the document when developing new AI-related legislation, strategies, and policies.

title: Executive Order on the Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
short_title: EO 14110 (Biden AI EO)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; National security & defence
issuing_body: NIST; OSTP; OMB; DHS; DOJ; FTC
summary: Biden's landmark 2023 AI executive order directed federal agencies to develop safety standards, required developers of powerful AI systems to share safety test results with the government, and tasked NIST with creating AI risk benchmarks. It addressed everything from AI in hiring to biosecurity risks and was the most comprehensive US federal AI governance action prior to its revocation.

title: Online Safety Act 2023
short_title: UK Online Safety Act 2023
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: Ofcom
summary: UK Online Safety Act imposes platform duties to prevent illegal content, protect children, and ensure user safety. AI chatbots and generative AI systems are in scope as of Ofcom guidance from 2026. Requires risk assessments, proactive content moderation technology, and Ofcom registration for regulated services. UK has no dedicated AI Act.

title: Personal Data Protection Bill, 2023 (Pakistan)
short_title: Pakistan Personal Data Protection Bill
issuing_body: National Commission for Personal Data Protection (NCPDP)
summary: Pakistan has NOT enacted a comprehensive data protection law. The Personal Data Protection Bill 2023 (and a revised Federal-Cabinet-approved 2025 draft) remains a bill that has not passed Parliament as of mid-2026; the National Commission for Personal Data Protection does not yet exist. Interim framework is PECA 2016 (amended Jan 2025).

title: Beijing Measures for the Administration of Generative Artificial Intelligence Services (Trial)
short_title: Beijing GenAI Services Implementing Rules
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media
issuing_body: Beijing Municipal Cyberspace Administration; Beijing Municipal Public Security Bureau
summary: Beijing's Measures for Administering Generative AI Services implement the national GenAI Interim Measures at the municipal level, adding Beijing-specific requirements. Key additions: mandatory security assessment filing with Beijing Cyberspace Administration for GenAI services, content labeling requirements stricter than national standard, AI product registration for public-facing services, and prohibited content categories aligned with national CAC regulations but with additional local restrictions.

title: Voluntary Code of Conduct on the Responsible Development and Management of Advanced Generative AI Systems
short_title: Voluntary Code of Conduct on the Responsible Development and Management of Advanced Generative AI Systems
issuing_body: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
summary: This voluntary code asks Canadian developers and managers of advanced generative AI systems to commit to measures under six principles: accountability, safety, fairness and equity, transparency, human oversight and monitoring, and validity and robustness. Obligations are scaled according to whether a system is made available for general public use. It was introduced as a bridge while the Artificial Intelligence and Data Act was before Parliament, and lists around fifty signatory organisations.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada. Oversight: ISED administers; signatory companies self-implement the commitments. Stated purpose: Interim voluntary safeguards for generative AI developers pending binding legislation.

title: CFPB Circular 2023-03: Adverse Action Notification Requirements and the Equal Credit Opportunity Act in the Context of Artificial Intelligence
short_title: CFPB Circular on AI in Credit Decisions
issuing_body: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB); State attorneys general; Private plaintiffs under ECOA
summary: CFPB Circular 2023-03 clarifies that lenders using AI or complex machine learning models in credit decisions must comply with ECOA adverse action notice requirements regardless of model complexity. Lenders cannot use model opacity as an excuse to avoid providing specific reasons for credit denials. Circular addresses "black box" AI and requires explanations that are meaningful to applicants.

title: Jordan Personal Data Protection Law No. 24 of 2023
short_title: Jordan PDPL 2023
summary: Jordan's first comprehensive data protection law establishes the Personal Data Protection Council as an independent supervisory authority and creates a consent-based framework covering all organizations processing data of Jordanians and residents. Key provisions include core processing principles, sensitive data categories (health, genetic, biometric, political, religious, criminal, financial), full data subject rights including portability, DPO requirements for large-scale or sensitive processing, mandatory breach notification, and cross-border transfer restrictions. Published in the Official Gazette on 17 September 2023, the law entered into force six months later on 17 March 2024, with a one-year full-compliance deadline of 17 March 2025. Implementing regulations were still in development as of 2026; the operational regulator is the Personal Data Protection Directorate under MoDEE.

title: DIFC Data Protection Regulation 10: Processing Personal Data Through Autonomous and Semi-Autonomous Systems
short_title: DIFC Regulation 10 — Autonomous Systems
issuing_body: DIFC Commissioner of Data Protection
summary: The Dubai International Financial Centre's dedicated regulation for AI and automated decision-making. Controllers using autonomous or semi-autonomous systems must conduct data protection impact assessments, notify individuals when significant decisions are made automatically, provide human review rights, and register high-risk autonomous systems with the DIFC Commissioner. One of the earliest standalone AI/automated-systems regulations in the Middle East. NOTE: The 2020 in the ID refers to the parent Data Protection Law No. 5/2020; Regulation 10 on Autonomous Systems was itself enacted September 2023.

title: Interim Measures for the Management of Generative Artificial Intelligence Services
short_title: Interim Measures for the Management of Generative Artificial Intelligence Services
issuing_body: Cyberspace Administration of China with NDRC, Ministry of Education, MOST, MIIT, Ministry of Public Security and NRTA
summary: These measures govern generative AI services offered to the public in China, whether producing text, images, audio or video. Providers must use lawfully sourced training data, take steps against discrimination, protect personal information, label generated content, handle user complaints and ensure outputs comply with content rules. Services with public-opinion or social-mobilisation capacity must complete security assessments and algorithm filing. The measures took effect on 15 August 2023.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by Cyberspace Administration of China with NDRC, Ministry of Education, MOST, MIIT, Ministry of Public Security and NRTA. Oversight: Cyberspace Administration of China leads; sectoral ministries supervise within their remits. Stated purpose: Regulate public-facing generative AI to control content risks while supporting industry development.

title: Decreto Supremo N° 115-2025-PCM – Reglamento de la Ley N° 31814 (Supreme Decree No. 115-2025-PCM – Regulation of Law No. 31814)
short_title: Decreto Supremo N° 115-2025-PCM
issuing_body: Presidencia del Consejo de Ministros (PCM)
summary: This regulation, published on 9 September 2025, develops Law 31814 with six titles and 36 articles. It introduces a risk classification distinguishing prohibited uses, high-risk systems and acceptable-risk systems, sets transparency, data protection and governance obligations for public and private actors, and provides for sandboxes, capacity-building and reporting channels. Compliance is phased in over one to four years depending on the sector and type of organisation.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by Presidencia del Consejo de Ministros (PCM). Oversight: PCM's Secretaría de Gobierno y Transformación Digital supervises compliance. Stated purpose: Operationalise the AI promotion law with risk-based obligations.

title: Ley N° 31814 – Ley que promueve el uso de la inteligencia artificial en favor del desarrollo económico y social del país (Law No. 31814 – Law promoting the use of artificial intelligence for the country's economic and social development)
short_title: Ley N° 31814
issuing_body: Congreso de la República; implemented by the Presidencia del Consejo de Ministros (PCM)
summary: Law 31814, promulgated on 4 July 2023 and published on 5 July 2023, declares AI development of national interest and frames its use within Peru's digital transformation process. It sets principles such as risk-based safety, ethics, transparency and multi-stakeholder participation, and designates the PCM's digital government secretariat as the national AI authority. The law is promotional in character and left detailed obligations to a later regulation.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by Congreso de la República; implemented by the Presidencia del Consejo de Ministros (PCM). Oversight: PCM, through the Secretaría de Gobierno y Transformación Digital, is the national technical-regulatory authority. Stated purpose: Promote AI adoption within the national digital transformation while safeguarding rights.

title: Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 4 of 2023)
short_title: Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023
issuing_body: Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC)
summary: Nigeria's first Act-level data protection law supersedes the 2019 NDPR regulation and establishes the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC). Section 36 requires disclosure and human review rights for automated decisions with significant effects, directly applicable to AI systems. GDPR-aligned principles apply across all sectors. The NDPC issued the General Application and Implementation Directive (GAID) 2025 (issued 20 March 2025, effective 19 September 2025) as the Act's principal implementing instrument.

title: Rwanda National Artificial Intelligence Policy
short_title: Rwanda National AI Policy 2023
issuing_body: Ministry of ICT and Innovation; Rwanda Utilities Regulatory Authority (RURA)
summary: Rwanda's first national AI policy, approved by the Cabinet on April 20, 2023, making Rwanda the first African country to adopt a national AI policy. Establishes Rwanda's vision for AI-driven economic transformation and public service delivery across agriculture, health, education, and justice. Focuses on responsible AI development, data governance, AI talent development, and international AI cooperation. The policy commits Rwanda to human-centric AI aligned with African Union principles.

title: A pro-innovation approach to AI regulation (white paper and government response)
short_title: UK AI regulation framework
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
summary: The UK white paper sets out a principles-based, context-specific approach to regulating AI. Instead of a single AI law, it asks existing regulators to interpret and apply five cross-cutting principles within their remits: safety, security and robustness; appropriate transparency and explainability; fairness; accountability and governance; and contestability and redress. Central government provides coordination, monitoring and guidance.
scope: Applies to UK regulators and, through them, to organisations developing or using AI in regulated activities in the UK. It creates no direct legal obligations on businesses; obligations arise from the existing laws each regulator enforces.

title: Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA) — 2023 Amendments (Act No. 19234)
short_title: South Korea PIPA (2023 Amendments)
topics: General AI governance; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC)
summary: South Korea's landmark 2023 PIPA amendments introduce Asia-Pacific's strongest statutory right to explanation for automated AI decisions and the right to object to and demand human review of purely automated decisions that legally or significantly affect individuals. The amendments also modernize cross-border transfer mechanisms (SCCs, BCRs, adequacy decisions), introduce 72-hour breach notification aligned with GDPR, expand PIPC enforcement powers, and clarify extraterritorial scope covering foreign online service providers processing Korean residents' data.

jurisdiction: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
title: ISO/IEC 23894:2023 — Information Technology: Artificial Intelligence — Guidance on Risk Management
short_title: ISO/IEC 23894:2023 AI Risk Management
issuing_body: ISO member bodies (voluntary adoption)
summary: ISO/IEC 23894 provides technical guidance on integrating AI risk management into organisational risk management processes, aligned with ISO 31000. It identifies AI-specific risk sources (bias, opacity, data quality, adversarial inputs) and provides a structured process for risk identification, analysis, evaluation, and treatment.

title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0) and Generative AI Profile
short_title: NIST AI RMF
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI; Data protection & privacy; Frontier / general-purpose AI
issuing_body: National Institute of Standards and Technology (US Department of Commerce)
summary: The NIST AI Risk Management Framework is a voluntary framework for managing risks to individuals, organisations and society from AI. It organises practices into four functions: Govern, Map, Measure and Manage, and describes characteristics of trustworthy AI such as validity, safety, security, accountability, explainability, privacy and fairness. The July 2024 Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1) adds risks and suggested actions specific to generative AI. Many US procurement requirements and state laws reference the framework as a recognised approach.
scope: Voluntary and sector-agnostic; usable by any organisation designing, developing, deploying or evaluating AI systems. It creates no legal obligations, but Colorado SB 24-205 and federal procurement guidance treat conformity with the framework as evidence of reasonable care.

title: Disposición 2/2023 – Recomendaciones para una Inteligencia Artificial Fiable (Disposition 2/2023 – Recommendations for Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence)
short_title: Disposición 2/2023
issuing_body: Subsecretaría de Tecnologías de la Información, Jefatura de Gabinete de Ministros
summary: Disposición 2/2023 approves a set of recommendations for trustworthy AI addressed to projects designed, developed or adopted by the national public sector, together with a diagram of the stages of an AI project. Aligned with the UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI, it emphasises human-centred design, transparency, human oversight, non-discrimination, data protection and accountability across the project lifecycle. It is guidance rather than a binding regulatory regime.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by Subsecretaría de Tecnologías de la Información, Jefatura de Gabinete de Ministros. Oversight: Public-sector bodies apply the recommendations to their own AI projects. Stated purpose: Ethical guidance for AI projects in the national public administration.

title: Stratégie nationale d'intelligence artificielle et des mégadonnées 2023–2027
short_title: National AI and Big Data Strategy 2023–2027
topics: General AI governance; Health; Education; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of Benin (Ministry of Digital Affairs and Digitalisation)
summary: Adopted by the Council of Ministers in January 2023, the strategy sets objectives for AI and big-data skills, research, data infrastructure and governance, ethical AI and priority use cases in health, education, agriculture, tourism and living environment, with a 2027 horizon.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Projeto de Lei nº 2338/2023 – Dispõe sobre o uso da Inteligência Artificial (Bill No. 2338/2023 – On the use of Artificial Intelligence)
short_title: Projeto de Lei nº 2338/2023
issuing_body: Senado Federal (author: Senator Rodrigo Pacheco); now before the Câmara dos Deputados
summary: PL 2338/2023 is Brazil's flagship AI bill, introduced in the Senate in May 2023 and approved by the Senate plenary on 10 December 2024 after extensive amendment. It classifies AI systems by risk, bans certain uses, sets obligations for developers and deployers of high-risk systems, and provides for rights of affected persons and a national governance system. The Senate transmitted the text to the Chamber of Deputies on 17 March 2025, where a special committee is examining it.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by Senado Federal (author: Senator Rodrigo Pacheco); now before the Câmara dos Deputados. Oversight: Bill proposes a national AI governance system led by a competent authority (SIA); currently under review by a Chamber of Deputies special committee. Stated purpose: Create a comprehensive, risk-based legal framework for AI in Brazil.

title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and DPDP Rules, 2025
short_title: India DPDP Act
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Parliament of India; Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (Rules)
summary: The DPDP Act is India's cross-sector personal-data law. It applies to digital personal data processed in India and to processing outside India connected with offering goods or services to people in India. It requires a lawful basis (consent or specified legitimate uses), notice, purpose limitation, data accuracy, security safeguards, breach notification to the Data Protection Board and affected individuals, and grants rights of access, correction, erasure and grievance redress. Significant Data Fiduciaries face extra duties such as impact assessments and audits. The Act does not mention AI specifically, but it governs the personal data used to train and operate AI systems.
scope: Data Fiduciaries (controllers) and Data Processors handling digital personal data of individuals in India, including foreign entities offering goods or services to India. Excludes personal or domestic use and publicly available data made public by the individual or under law.

title: Surat Edaran Menteri Komunikasi dan Informatika Nomor 9 Tahun 2023 tentang Etika Kecerdasan Artifisial (Circular Letter No. 9 of 2023 on AI Ethics)
short_title: Surat Edaran Menteri Komunikasi dan Informatika Nomor 9 Tahun 2023 tentang Etika Kecerdasan Artifisial
issuing_body: Ministry of Communication and Informatics (now Ministry of Communication and Digital)
summary: A ministerial circular that lays out ethical values for developing and using AI, such as inclusivity, humanity, security, accessibility, transparency, accountability, personal data protection, sustainability and respect for intellectual property. It applies to AI-related businesses and to public and private electronic system operators in Indonesia. It is soft-law guidance intended as a basis for future regulation.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by Ministry of Communication and Informatics (now Ministry of Communication and Digital). Oversight: Ministry of Communication and Digital (Komdigi). Stated purpose: Set ethical expectations for AI developers and electronic system operators pending binding regulation.

jurisdiction: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
country: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
title: Hiroshima Process International Code of Conduct for Organizations Developing Advanced AI Systems (G7, 30 October 2023)
short_title: G7 Hiroshima AI Process code of conduct
topics: General AI governance; Frontier / general-purpose AI
issuing_body: G7 Leaders (Hiroshima AI Process)
summary: Eleven voluntary actions for organisations developing the most advanced AI systems, including foundation and generative models: risk identification and mitigation across the lifecycle, post-deployment vulnerability and incident monitoring, public transparency reports, responsible information sharing, security controls, content authentication such as watermarking, research on societal risks, priority to global challenges, technical standards, and data-input and personal-data safeguards. It sits alongside the Hiroshima Process guiding principles and, from 2025, an OECD-run voluntary reporting framework.
scope: Voluntary; aimed at developers of advanced AI systems worldwide.

jurisdiction: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
country: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
title: The Bletchley Declaration by countries attending the AI Safety Summit, 1–2 November 2023
short_title: Bletchley Declaration (AI Safety Summit 2023)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI; Frontier / general-purpose AI
issuing_body: 28 countries and the European Union attending the AI Safety Summit hosted by the United Kingdom
summary: Signed by countries including the United States, China, the EU, India, Japan and Brazil, the declaration recognises the opportunities of AI and the risks of frontier models, commits signatories to cooperate on identifying AI safety risks and building risk-based policies, and launched the summit series continued in Seoul (2024) and Paris (2025) and the network of AI safety institutes.
scope: Political declaration; no obligations for organisations.

title: Israel's Policy on Artificial Intelligence Regulation and Ethics
short_title: AI regulation and ethics policy (2023)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: Ministry of Innovation, Science and Technology and Ministry of Justice
summary: Adopted in December 2023 after public consultation, the policy sets Israel's approach: sector-specific regulation by existing regulators, a risk-based approach, preference for soft tools (standards, self-regulation, sandboxes) over binding rules at this stage, alignment with OECD principles, and common ethical principles (growth and sustainable development, human-centricity, equality, transparency, safety, accountability, privacy). It establishes an AI policy coordination centre and an expert advisory forum.
scope: Guidance to government ministries and regulators; no direct obligations on organisations.

title: Jordanian Artificial Intelligence Strategy and Implementation Roadmap 2023–2027
short_title: AI Strategy and Implementation Roadmap 2023–2027
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of Jordan (Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship)
summary: Adopted in 2023, the strategy sets priorities on AI governance and ethics, talent and research, adoption in government services and priority sectors, data infrastructure, and international cooperation, with an implementation roadmap and indicators to 2027.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: AI Ethics Principles
short_title: AI Ethics Principles
issuing_body: Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA)
summary: SDAIA's AI Ethics Principles set out ethical principles and associated controls for entities developing, deploying or affected by AI systems in Saudi Arabia, covering fairness, privacy and security, humanity, social and environmental benefit, reliability and safety, transparency, and accountability. The document assigns roles and responsibilities and marks certain controls as binding for public entities. The 2025 edition updates the September 2023 version 1.0.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA). Oversight: SDAIA issues and updates the principles and oversees adoption by public entities. Stated purpose: Ensure responsible, safe and rights-respecting AI development and use in the Kingdom.

title: Етичке смернице за развој, примену и употребу поуздане и одговорне вештачке интелигенције
short_title: Ethical guidelines for trustworthy AI (2023)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: Government of the Republic of Serbia
summary: Adopted in March 2023, the guidelines set principles and requirements for trustworthy and responsible AI in Serbia (human agency, safety, privacy, transparency, non-discrimination, societal well-being, accountability), with self-assessment questions for developers and users, drawing on the EU ethics guidelines and the UNESCO recommendation.
scope: Non-binding; addressed to public and private developers and users of AI in Serbia.

title: Real Decreto 729/2023, de 22 de agosto, por el que se aprueba el Estatuto de la Agencia Española de Supervisión de Inteligencia Artificial
short_title: Royal Decree 729/2023 (AESIA statute)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of Spain
summary: Creates and organises AESIA, the Spanish AI Supervision Agency, as a public body attached to the Ministry for Digital Transformation. AESIA supervises and inspects AI systems, promotes sandboxes and standards, and acts as national authority for the EU AI Act. The decree sets its governance, functions and funding.
scope: Institutional: establishes the agency and its powers over AI systems placed on or used in the Spanish market.

title: Real Decreto 817/2023, de 8 de noviembre, que establece un entorno controlado de pruebas para el ensayo del cumplimiento de la propuesta de Reglamento de IA
short_title: Royal Decree 817/2023 (AI regulatory sandbox)
issuing_body: Government of Spain
summary: Establishes Spain's controlled testing environment (sandbox) for providers of high-risk AI systems to test compliance with the then-proposed EU AI Act requirements: risk management, data governance, documentation, transparency, human oversight, accuracy and robustness. Participation is voluntary; participants receive guidance and produce documentation that feeds into national implementation.
scope: Voluntary for AI providers and, where relevant, deployers selected through calls; obligations arise only for participants.

title: Roadmap for the regulation of artificial intelligence in Ukraine
short_title: Roadmap for AI regulation (2023)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine
summary: Published in October 2023, the roadmap sets a two-stage, bottom-up approach: first voluntary instruments (white paper, general and sector recommendations, a self-assessment tool, a code of conduct and regulatory sandboxes) to help businesses prepare, then a law on AI harmonised with the EU AI Act, timed with Ukraine's EU accession path.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: SEC Proposed Rule: Conflicts of Interest Associated with the Use of Predictive Data Analytics by Broker-Dealers and Investment Advisers
short_title: SEC Proposed Rule on Conflicts of Interest in AI (2023)
issuing_body: Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
summary: The SEC's proposed rule would have required broker-dealers and investment advisers to evaluate and eliminate or neutralise conflicts of interest when using predictive data analytics (including AI and ML) in investor interactions. The rule targeted AI systems that optimise for firm interests at investors' expense, requiring conflict identification through testing, documented conflict elimination or neutralisation, disclosure to investors, and compliance program requirements. The SEC formally withdrew the rule in June 2025.

title: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2)
short_title: NIS2 Directive
issuing_body: National competent authorities; European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA); Computer Security Incident Response Teams (CSIRTs)
summary: The NIS2 Directive significantly expands the scope of the original NIS Directive (2016/1148), establishing cybersecurity risk-management and incident-reporting obligations for essential and important entities across 18 sectors including energy, transport, banking, health, digital infrastructure, and ICT service management. Entities must implement risk-proportionate technical and organisational cybersecurity measures covering supply chain security, vulnerability handling, cryptography, access control, and multi-factor authentication. Incident reporting follows a three-stage timeline: an early warning within 24 hours, a formal notification within 72 hours, and a final report within one month. Entities that are substantially dependent on network and information systems face management-body accountability requirements. National supervisory authorities may impose fines up to €10 million or 2% of global annual turnover for essential entities and €7 million or 1.4% for important entities. Member states must designate national competent authorities and establish CSIRTs. Repeals and replaces the original NIS Directive.

title: UAE Artificial Intelligence Ethics: Principles and Guidelines (December 2022)
short_title: UAE AI Ethics Principles and Guidelines
issuing_body: Office of the Minister of State for Artificial Intelligence, Digital Economy and Remote Work Applications
summary: Non-binding guidelines covering eight AI ethics principles for both public and private sector AI actors in the UAE: (1) Fairness — representative data, Discrimination Impact Assessments, diverse development teams; (2) Accountability — appeals procedures, external audit for critical decisions, human case evaluators; (3) Transparency — traceability of significant decisions, disclosure of AI interaction; (4) Explainability — right to explanation for significant decisions, counterfactual reasoning where full explainability is unavailable; (5) Robust, Safe and Secure — vulnerability assessments, fallback plans, human override capability; (6) Human Centered — no lethal force delegated to AI, opt-in for nudging systems, community norm compliance; (7) Sustainable and Environmentally Friendly — carbon awareness, energy consumption in model design; (8) Privacy Preserving — privacy by design, data minimization, consent logging. Applicable only to AI systems making or informing 'significant decisions'. Published under CC BY 4.0.

title: Tanzania Personal Data Protection Act 2022
short_title: Tanzania Personal Data Protection Act 2022
summary: Tanzania's first comprehensive personal data protection law establishing the Personal Data Protection Commission. Incorporates modern data protection concepts including nine principles, data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure, portability, objection), DPO requirements, DPIA obligations for high-risk processing, sensitive data categories, mandatory breach notification, and cross-border transfer rules. Enacted as Act No. 11 of 2022 (assented 27 November 2022) and brought into operation on 1 May 2023 by Government Notice No. 326 of 2023. Two implementing regulations followed in 2023 — the Personal Data Protection (Personal Data Collection and Processing) Regulations, 2023 and the Personal Data Protection (Complaints Settlement Procedures) Regulations, 2023 — with the PDPC becoming fully operational in 2024.

title: Provisions on the Administration of Deep Synthesis Internet Information Services
short_title: China Deep Synthesis Provisions
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Online safety & children
issuing_body: Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC); Ministry of Industry and Information Technology; Ministry of Public Security
summary: Regulates deep synthesis (deepfake/AI-generated) technology for video, voice, images, and text. Service providers must register users, implement ethics reviews, monitor content for illegal/disinformation use, and add visible labels to all synthetic content. Prohibits deepfakes implicating national security or reputational harm.

title: EU Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 — Digital Services Act (DSA)
short_title: EU Digital Services Act (DSA)
summary: The Digital Services Act establishes a tiered regulatory framework for online intermediary services in the EU, imposing the heaviest obligations — including annual algorithmic audits, systemic risk assessments, and researcher data access — on Very Large Online Platforms and Very Large Online Search Engines with ≥45 million EU users. All online platforms using recommender systems must disclose their main parameters and offer at least one non-profiling recommendation option. The European Commission has direct enforcement jurisdiction over VLOPs/VLOSEs with penalties up to 6% of global turnover.

title: Undang-Undang Nomor 27 Tahun 2022 tentang Pelindungan Data Pribadi (UU PDP)
short_title: Indonesia Personal Data Protection Law 2022
issuing_body: Personal Data Protection Agency (in formation)
summary: Indonesia's first comprehensive personal data protection law, modeled on GDPR. Prohibits automated decision-making that produces legal effects without human oversight mechanisms. Creates a Personal Data Protection Agency (still being constituted). Compliance transition ended October 2024.

title: Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights — Making Automated Systems Work for the American People (OSTP, 2022)
short_title: OSTP Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights (2022)
topics: General AI governance; Data protection & privacy
summary: The OSTP Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights, released on October 4, 2022, is a non-binding framework articulating five principles for the design, development, and deployment of automated systems in the United States: (1) safe and effective systems, (2) algorithmic discrimination protections, (3) data privacy, (4) notice and explanation, and (5) human alternatives, consideration, and fallback. Published by the Biden White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP), the Blueprint is intended to guide both government and private sector actors and to inform future legislation and rulemaking. It does not carry the force of law and creates no enforceable rights.

title: Shanghai Municipality Regulations on the Promotion and Development of the Artificial Intelligence Industry
short_title: Shanghai AI Industry Development Ordinance
issuing_body: Shanghai Municipal Commission of Economy and Information Technology (SMECIT); Shanghai Cyberspace Administration
summary: China's first city-level comprehensive AI ordinance, Shanghai's AI Industry Development Regulations promote AI innovation while establishing governance requirements. Key provisions: regulatory sandbox for AI products, mandatory disclosure for AI-enabled public services, training data governance requirements, risk classification for AI applications in public services, safe harbour for compliant AI products, and support for international AI cooperation.

title: Strategy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in the Republic of Tajikistan for the period up to 2040
short_title: AI Development Strategy to 2040
topics: General AI governance; Education; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of the Republic of Tajikistan
summary: Approved by government decree in 2021, the strategy sets long-term goals for AI research, education, infrastructure and use in the economy and public administration to 2040.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Shenzhen Special Economic Zone Artificial Intelligence Industry Promotion Regulation
short_title: Shenzhen AI Industry Promotion Regulation
issuing_body: Shenzhen Municipal Government
summary: China's first sub-national comprehensive AI regulation, enacted by Shenzhen's Special Economic Zone legislature. Covers the full lifecycle of AI development, promotion, governance, and accountability. Requires AI providers in specified domains to conduct algorithmic impact assessments, disclose AI use to affected parties, and allow human review of automated decisions. Includes innovation incentives alongside governance obligations.

title: EU Regulation (EU) 2022/868 — Data Governance Act (DGA)
short_title: EU Data Governance Act (DGA)
summary: The Data Governance Act establishes EU-wide frameworks for re-using protected public sector data, operating trusted data intermediation services, and collecting voluntary data donations for general-interest purposes including AI research. Its data altruism mechanism enables individuals to lawfully contribute personal data (including health records and genomic data) to AI training datasets for public benefit, while the intermediation services framework prohibits data brokers from using pooled data to train their own AI models. The DGA provides the governance infrastructure underlying Common European Data Spaces in health, mobility, agriculture, and other sectors. It entered into force on 23 June 2022 and became applicable on 24 September 2023.

title: Personal Data Protection Act, No. 9 of 2022 (Sri Lanka)
short_title: Sri Lanka Personal Data Protection Act 2022
issuing_body: Data Protection Authority (DPA) of Sri Lanka
summary: Sri Lanka became the first South Asian country to enact comprehensive privacy legislation. Data subjects may object to automated processing creating irreversible and continuous impacts on rights and freedoms. The Data Protection Authority was established August 2023; core compliance obligations delayed by 2025 amendments.

title: Oman Personal Data Protection Law 2022 (Royal Decree No. 6/2022)
short_title: Oman PDPL 2022
summary: Oman's first comprehensive data protection law establishes a consent-based framework covering all organizations processing personal data in Oman or about Oman residents, administered by the Information Technology Authority. Key provisions include six core processing principles, sensitive data categories (health, genetic, biometric, racial, religious), data subject rights (access, correction, deletion, restriction, objection, consent withdrawal), DPO requirements for large-scale processing, mandatory breach notification, and cross-border transfer restrictions. Executive Regulations were issued via Ministerial Decision No. 34/2024, with the transition/compliance period ending and full enforcement from early February 2026. Supervisory authority is the Ministry of Transport, Communications and Information Technology (MTCIT), which absorbed the former Information Technology Authority (ITA).

title: Plan national de convergence pour le développement de l'intelligence artificielle
short_title: National Convergence Plan for AI (2022)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Federal Government of Belgium with the Regions and Communities
summary: Adopted in 2022, the convergence plan coordinates the federal and regional AI initiatives around nine objectives, including trustworthy AI, skills, data, research, public-sector adoption and international positioning, with AI4Belgium as the delivery coalition.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Data Act (Part 3 of Bill C-27, Digital Charter Implementation Act, 2022)
short_title: Artificial Intelligence and Data Act
issuing_body: Parliament of Canada (sponsored by the Minister of Innovation, Science and Industry)
summary: The Artificial Intelligence and Data Act (AIDA) was proposed as Part 3 of Bill C-27 and would have required organisations designing, developing or deploying high-impact AI systems to assess and mitigate risks of harm and bias, keep records and publish information, with enforcement by an AI and Data Commissioner and penalties for serious offences. The bill passed second reading in the House of Commons in April 2023 and was studied in committee through 2024 but never advanced to report stage. It lapsed when the 44th Parliament ended in early 2025 without the bill being passed.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by Parliament of Canada (sponsored by the Minister of Innovation, Science and Industry). Oversight: Proposed AI and Data Commissioner within Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada. Stated purpose: Regulate high-impact AI systems to prevent harm and biased output in the private sector.

title: Νόμος 4961/2022: Αναδυόμενες τεχνολογίες πληροφορικής και επικοινωνιών, ενίσχυση της ψηφιακής διακυβέρνησης και άλλες διατάξεις
short_title: Law 4961/2022 (emerging technologies, AI chapter)
topics: Employment & HR; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Hellenic Parliament
summary: Law 4961/2022, published in July 2022, contains a chapter on artificial intelligence: public-sector bodies must carry out an algorithmic impact assessment and publish information before deploying AI systems that affect people, keep a register of AI systems, and ensure the Hellenic Data Protection Authority's oversight; medium and large private companies must inform workers about AI systems used in employment decisions and maintain an ethical-use policy. It also regulates IoT, 3D printing, blockchain and unmanned aircraft.
scope: Public-sector bodies deploying AI in Greece and medium/large private employers using AI in employment; complements the EU AI Act.

jurisdiction: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
title: BCBS Newsletter No. 27 — Developments in Credit Risk Management Across the Financial Sector: Current Practices and the Role of AI and Machine Learning
short_title: BCBS Newsletter No. 27 — AI/ML in Credit Risk
summary: BCBS Newsletter No. 27, published January 2022, outlines supervisory expectations for the use of AI and machine learning in banking, with a focus on credit risk management. Key topics include model explainability requirements, governance frameworks for AI/ML, model risk management adaptations, and financial stability implications of widespread AI adoption in banking. The primary BCBS policy signal on AI/ML in banking risk management.

title: Jordanian Charter of Artificial Intelligence Ethics
short_title: Charter of AI Ethics (2022)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship
summary: The charter sets ethical principles for the development and use of AI in Jordan, including human dignity, fairness, transparency, accountability, safety, privacy and sustainability, addressed to public and private organisations.
scope: Voluntary; public and private AI actors in Jordan.

title: Thailand National AI Strategy and Action Plan (2022-2027)
short_title: Thailand National AI Strategy and Action Plan
issuing_body: Cabinet of Thailand (prepared by MHESI and MDES; NECTEC/NSTDA secretariat)
summary: A cabinet-approved strategy and action plan with five strategies: readiness in ethics, law and regulation; national AI infrastructure; human capability and education; AI technology and innovation development; and promotion of AI use in public and private sectors. It sets targets for AI talent, research prototypes and economic impact through 2027 and is implemented in phases coordinated across ministries.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by Cabinet of Thailand (prepared by MHESI and MDES; NECTEC/NSTDA secretariat). Oversight: National AI Committee with NECTEC/NSTDA as secretariat. Stated purpose: Build an effective AI ecosystem to strengthen the economy and quality of life by 2027.

title: Provisions on the Administration of Algorithmic Recommendations in Internet Information Services
short_title: China Algorithm Recommendations Regulation
issuing_body: Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC); Ministry of Industry and Information Technology; State Administration for Market Regulation
summary: First globally binding regulation of algorithmic recommendation systems. Requires platforms with 1M+ users to register recommendation algorithms, offer non-personalized options, enable user preference modification, conduct risk assessments, and report to regulators. Prohibits discriminatory pricing and addictive design patterns targeting minors.

title: Zimbabwe Cyber and Data Protection Act [Chapter 12:07] (Act No. 5 of 2021)
short_title: Zimbabwe Cyber and Data Protection Act 2021
summary: Zimbabwe's combined cybersecurity and data protection framework in a single statute. Establishes POTRAZ as the data protection supervisory authority and the Cybersecurity Centre for operational cybersecurity functions. Provides eight data protection principles, data subject rights, sensitive data protections, breach notification obligations, critical infrastructure protection requirements, and cybercrime offenses.

title: New York City Automated Employment Decision Tools Law
short_title: NYC Local Law 144 (AEDT)
issuing_body: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
summary: First city-level law in the US regulating AI hiring tools. Requires NYC employers and employment agencies using automated employment decision tools to conduct annual independent bias audits, publish audit results publicly, and notify job candidates that AI is being used in the hiring process.

title: Law N° 058/2021 of 13/10/2021 Relating to the Protection of Personal Data and Privacy in Rwanda
short_title: Rwanda Data Protection and Privacy Law 2021
issuing_body: National Cyber Security Authority (NCSA) — Data Protection and Privacy Office
summary: Rwanda's first comprehensive data protection law establishes the National Cyber Security Authority (NCSA), through its Data Protection and Privacy Office, as oversight body. Sets foundational principles for lawful data processing applicable to AI systems operating in Rwanda, including data subject rights and controller registration.

title: An Act to modernize legislative provisions as regards the protection of personal information (SQ 2021, c 25)
short_title: Quebec Law 25 (Privacy Modernization Act)
issuing_body: Commission d'accès à l'information (CAI)
summary: Quebec's landmark privacy modernization law is the most AI-relevant enacted privacy law in Canada. Section 12.1 requires organizations to inform individuals when decisions are made exclusively through automated processing, disclose the logic used, and allow human review. Privacy Impact Assessments are mandatory for high-risk systems before deployment.

title: Personal Data Protection Law (Royal Decree M/19 of 1442H)
short_title: Saudi Arabia PDPL (Royal Decree M/19)
issuing_body: Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA)
summary: Saudi Arabia's first comprehensive personal data protection law, administered by SDAIA (the Saudi Data and AI Authority). Amendments in 2023 (Royal Decree M/148) and implementing regulations in September 2023 triggered full enforcement. The law includes provisions on automated profiling and sensitive data directly applicable to AI systems.

title: Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China — AI-Relevant Provisions
short_title: China PIPL (AI provisions)
topics: General AI governance; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC); Provincial data protection authorities
summary: China's comprehensive personal data law directly applicable to AI: requires lawful basis for processing personal data in AI training, mandates consent for sensitive data, grants individuals rights to access, correct, and delete data, and prohibits differential treatment based on personal information analysis. AI recommendation algorithms must provide opt-out mechanisms.

title: Guidelines on the Operation of AI in the Financial Sector (FSC — 2021 version)
short_title: FSC/FSS AI Guidelines (Financial)
issuing_body: Financial Services Commission; Financial Supervisory Service
summary: Non-binding regulatory guidance from the Financial Services Commission covering reliable, fair, transparent, and safe use of AI in the Korean financial sector. Note: the database contains the July 2021 Operational Guidelines; the FSC issued updated Development and Utilization Guidelines in July 2022.

title: UAE AI Guide on Deepfakes (National Program for Artificial Intelligence, July 2021)
short_title: UAE AI Guide on Deepfakes
summary: Public awareness guide on deepfakes published by the UAE National Program for Artificial Intelligence. Explains what deepfakes are, how GANs work, categories of forged content (shallow fakes vs. deepfakes), visual and audible manipulation techniques, positive use cases (medical, entertainment, customer service), self-protection tips (limiting personal data shared online), and detection signs. References UAE laws prohibiting cyberbullying and identity impersonation. Introduces the Digital Wellbeing Council established under Sheikh Saif bin Zayed Al Nahyan.

title: Act on the Protection of Personal Information (APPI) — 2022 Amendments (Act No. 57 of 2003, as amended by Act No. 77 of 2021, in force June 2022)
short_title: Japan APPI (2022 Amendments)
topics: General AI governance; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: Personal Information Protection Commission (PPC)
summary: Japan's 2022 APPI amendments represent the most expansive revision of Japan's primary personal data protection law, introducing mandatory breach notification, a strengthened opt-out regime for third-party data transfers requiring PPC registration, new data subject rights including cessation of third-party provision, tightened cross-border transfer rules with explicit consent requirements, and a new pseudonymously processed information category enabling AI development use cases. Corporate penalties increased tenfold to JPY 100 million. (A further APPI amendment bill from the triennial review was approved by the Cabinet on 7 April 2026 and submitted to the Diet — adding an AI/statistical-processing consent exemption, protections for children under 16, and administrative monetary penalties — but is not yet in force as of mid-2026.)

title: Australia's AI Action Plan 2021 — National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
short_title: Australia National AI Strategy 2021
summary: Australia's AI Action Plan 2021 is a high-level national strategy organised around three pillars — getting AI foundations right (data, infrastructure, trust), growing Australia's AI capability (research, business adoption, international engagement), and using AI for the greater good (health, environment, regional communities). It reinforces Australia's voluntary AI Ethics Principles (2019) and commits the federal government to applying them in all AI procurement and development, while encouraging (but not requiring) private sector adoption. The Action Plan has been substantially superseded by the Voluntary AI Safety Standard (September 2024) and the forthcoming mandatory high-risk AI regime.

title: Financial Services (Robotic and AI Enabled Advisory Services) Rules 2021
short_title: Mauritius Financial Services AI Advisory Rules
topics: General AI governance; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: Financial Services Commission (FSC) Mauritius
summary: Mauritius rules governing robo-advisory and AI-enabled financial advisory services.
