Requires licensed financial advisors deploying AI-powered advisory systems to disclose the automated nature of advice, ensure the system is fit for purpose, maintain human escalation options for clients, and conduct ongoing performance monitoring. One of the first sector-specific AI financial services regulations in Africa.

title: Ecuador Ley Orgánica de Protección de Datos Personales (LOPDP) 2021
short_title: Ecuador LOPDP 2021
summary: Ecuador's first comprehensive data protection law with GDPR-inspired structure. Establishes the SNPDP as supervisory authority. Provides seven principles, ARCO+ rights (including portability and non-discrimination), automated decision-making notification and human review rights, DPO requirements, DPIA obligations, sensitive data categories, 72-hour breach notification, and significant administrative fines.

title: Abu Dhabi Global Market Data Protection Regulations 2021
short_title: ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021
summary: The ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 establish a comprehensive GDPR-aligned data protection framework for entities operating in Abu Dhabi's international financial free zone. Enacted by the ADGM Board of Directors on 14 February 2021, with staggered compliance deadlines: new entities by August 2021, existing entities by February 2022. Key provisions include lawful basis requirements, full data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure, portability, objection), rights to contest automated decisions and obtain human intervention, mandatory DPIAs for high-risk processing, 72-hour breach notification, cross-border transfer mechanisms, and DPO requirements. Administrative penalties capped at USD 28 million; data subjects may also claim compensation for material and non-material damage through the ADGM Courts. The 2021 Regulations remain the base framework but have since been formally amended by the Data Protection Regulations (Amendment No. 1) 2024 (22 February 2024) and the Data Protection Regulations (Amendment No. 1) 2025 (9 September 2025), and supplemented by the Data Protection Regulations (Substantial Public Interest Conditions) Rules 2025.

title: National Security Presidential Memorandum 33 (NSPM-33) — National Security Strategy for United States Government-Supported Research and Development
short_title: NSPM-33 (R&D Security Policy)
summary: NSPM-33, issued January 14, 2021 (final days of Trump administration), establishes national security policy for federally-funded R&D. It addresses the risk of foreign governments — particularly China — accessing US research through talent recruitment programs, undisclosed affiliations, and research theft. Key requirements: disclosure of foreign funding/affiliations for all federally-funded researchers, standardized disclosure forms across agencies, export controls alignment, and agency-specific research security programs. The memo was implemented through NSPM-33 Implementation Guidance (January 2022) issued by the Biden OSTP.

title: FDA Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning (AI/ML)-Based Software as a Medical Device Action Plan
short_title: FDA AI/ML Action Plan for Software as Medical Device
issuing_body: Food and Drug Administration (FDA); FDA Center for Devices and Radiological Health (CDRH)
summary: The FDA's AI/ML Action Plan for Software as Medical Device (SaMD) establishes the agency's regulatory approach to AI-enabled medical devices. It outlines five action areas: tailored regulatory framework for AI/ML-based SaMD, good machine learning practice standards, patient-centred approaches, algorithm transparency, and real-world performance monitoring. The Action Plan underpins FDA's pre-submission program for AI medical devices and is being updated through the Predetermined Change Control Plan (PCCP) pathway.

jurisdiction: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
country: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
title: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence (adopted by the General Conference, 23 November 2021)
short_title: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI
topics: General AI governance; Health; Education; Government use of AI; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: UNESCO General Conference (193 member states)
summary: The first global normative instrument on AI ethics. It sets values (human rights and dignity, environment and ecosystem flourishing, diversity and inclusiveness, peaceful and just societies) and principles (proportionality and do no harm, safety and security, fairness, sustainability, privacy, human oversight, transparency and explainability, responsibility, awareness and literacy, multi-stakeholder governance), and eleven policy action areas from ethical impact assessment and data policy to gender, education, health and the environment. UNESCO supports implementation with a Readiness Assessment Methodology (RAM) and an Ethical Impact Assessment tool used by dozens of countries.
scope: Addressed to member states; recommends measures for public and private AI actors; non-binding.

title: AI – Here for Good: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy for Ireland (2021, refreshed 2024)
short_title: AI – Here for Good (National AI Strategy)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of Ireland (Department of Enterprise, Trade and Employment)
summary: Ireland's national AI strategy, first published in July 2021 and refreshed in November 2024 to reflect the EU AI Act and generative AI, is organised around building public trust, leveraging AI for economic and societal benefit, and enablers such as data, infrastructure, skills and governance. The refresh sets out Ireland's AI Act implementation model, public-sector AI guidelines and an AI advisory council.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: National Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2021-2025 (AI-Rmap)
short_title: National Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2021-2025
issuing_body: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MOSTI)
summary: Malaysia's five-year AI roadmap developed by MOSTI through a quadruple-helix consultation. It sets strategic thrusts on governance, R&D, infrastructure, talent and adoption, and identifies national use cases in five priority sectors: agriculture and forestry, healthcare, smart cities and transport, education and public services. It is guided by responsible AI principles including fairness, transparency, accountability and privacy.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MOSTI). Oversight: MOSTI with Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation. Stated purpose: Build a national AI innovation ecosystem to raise productivity and competitiveness.

title: New York City Local Law 144 of 2021 on Automated Employment Decision Tools (AEDT) and DCWP implementing rules
short_title: NYC Local Law 144 (automated employment decision tools)
topics: General AI governance; Employment & HR; Elections
issuing_body: New York City Council; rules by the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
summary: Employers and employment agencies may not use an automated employment decision tool to screen candidates or employees for hiring or promotion in New York City unless the tool has had an independent bias audit within the past year, a summary of the audit results is published, and candidates receive at least ten business days' notice of the tool's use, the job qualifications assessed, and how to request an alternative process or accommodation. The bias audit calculates selection and scoring impact ratios by sex, race/ethnicity and intersectional categories. Enforcement began 5 July 2023.
scope: Employers and employment agencies using AEDTs for candidates or employees residing in New York City.

title: Quebec Law 25 (S.Q. 2021, c. 25): provisions on decisions based exclusively on automated processing and biometric systems
short_title: Quebec Law 25 (automated decisions and biometrics)
topics: General AI governance; Deepfakes & synthetic media; Government use of AI; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: National Assembly of Quebec
summary: Section 12.1 of the private-sector privacy act (as amended by Law 25, in force 22 September 2023) requires any enterprise that uses personal information to render a decision based exclusively on automated processing to inform the person no later than when the decision is made, and, on request, to tell them what personal information was used, the reasons and principal factors and parameters, and their right to have the information corrected, and to give them an opportunity to submit observations to a person who can review the decision. Biometric identification databases must be declared to the Commission d'accès à l'information 60 days before use, and privacy impact assessments are mandatory for projects involving personal information. Penalties reach CAD 25 million or 4% of worldwide turnover.
scope: Enterprises and public bodies in Quebec using personal information in exclusively automated decisions or biometric systems.

title: Ulusal Yapay Zekâ Stratejisi 2021–2025 (National Artificial Intelligence Strategy)
short_title: National AI Strategy 2021–2025
topics: General AI governance; Employment & HR; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Presidency of the Republic of Türkiye (Digital Transformation Office) and Ministry of Industry and Technology
summary: Published by Presidential Circular in August 2021, the strategy sets six priorities: training AI experts and increasing employment, supporting research and innovation, access to quality data and technical infrastructure, regulations to accelerate socio-economic adaptation, strengthening international cooperation, and accelerating structural and workforce transformation. Its action plan was updated for 2024–2025.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data (UAE PDPL)
short_title: UAE PDPL
issuing_body: UAE Federal Government
summary: The UAE Personal Data Protection Law is the federal data-protection law applying outside the DIFC and ADGM free zones. It sets principles for lawful processing, consent and its exceptions, data-subject rights (including the right to object to automated decision-making without human intervention), controller and processor duties, security and breach notification to the UAE Data Office, cross-border transfer rules, and data protection impact assessments for high-risk processing including new technologies.
scope: Controllers and processors in the UAE (outside the financial free zones) and those outside the UAE processing personal data of individuals in the UAE. Government data, security bodies and health and banking data covered by other laws are excluded or partly excluded.

title: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020
short_title: National AI Initiative Act (2020)
issuing_body: NIST; NSF; OSTP; NITRD Program
summary: The foundational US federal AI law, enacted as Division E of the FY2021 NDAA. Establishes the National AI Initiative to coordinate federal AI R&D, creates the National AI Initiative Office within OSTP, requires a National AI Research Resource, and mandates an AI technical standards program at NIST. Sets the institutional framework for subsequent federal AI governance.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Government Act of 2020
short_title: AI in Government Act of 2020
issuing_body: GSA; OMB
summary: The AI in Government Act of 2020 (enacted as part of the Consolidated Appropriations Act) directed GSA to create an AI Center of Excellence to facilitate AI adoption across federal agencies, and directed OMB to produce guidance ensuring federal AI use is effective, ethical, and accountable. It established the interagency AI coordination working group.

title: Executive Order 13960 — Promoting the Use of Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence in the Federal Government
short_title: EO 13960 (Trump Trustworthy AI EO)
summary: EO 13960, signed by President Trump on December 3, 2020, established nine principles to guide all federal agencies in the design, development, acquisition, and use of artificial intelligence. The principles — lawful, purposeful and performance-driven, accurate and reliable, safe and secure, understandable, responsible and traceable, regularly monitored, transparent, and accountable — were intended to promote trustworthy AI across the federal government and foster public trust. Agencies were required to submit plans documenting how their existing AI use cases align with these principles. Implemented in conjunction with the AI in Government Act of 2020 and the NIST AI standards effort.

title: Saudi Arabia National Strategy for Data and Artificial Intelligence (NSDAI) 2020
short_title: Saudi Arabia National Data & AI Strategy
issuing_body: Saudi Data and AI Authority (SDAIA)
summary: Saudi Arabia's National Strategy for Data and Artificial Intelligence, issued by the Saudi Data and AI Authority (SDAIA). A comprehensive national strategy aligned with Vision 2030, covering data governance, AI development, talent, and ecosystem building. SDAIA was established in 2019 as the apex body for data and AI in Saudi Arabia. [Record created from secondary sources — full text unavailable at time of entry; should be verified when source is accessible.]

title: Paraguay Law No. 6534 — Personal Data Protection
short_title: Paraguay Data Protection Law 2020
summary: Paraguay's primary data protection law establishing SENATIC as the supervisory authority. Provides data protection principles, lawful processing bases, sensitive data special categories (health, genetic, biometric, political, criminal), ARCO data subject rights, mandatory database registration, cross-border transfer restrictions, and administrative and criminal penalties.

title: Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection (revDSG / nFADP) — AI Applicability
short_title: Switzerland FADP (Revised Federal Act on Data Protection)
issuing_body: Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC)
summary: Switzerland's revised Federal Act on Data Protection (revDSG/nFADP), in force since September 2023, substantially aligns Swiss data protection with the GDPR. It is relevant to AI through: mandatory data protection impact assessments for high-risk processing, a right not to be subject to solely automated decisions with legal effects, opt-out from automated profiling, transparency obligations for automated processing, and special category protections for biometric and genetic data.

title: Egypt Personal Data Protection Law, Law No. 151 of 2020
short_title: Egypt Personal Data Protection Law 2020
issuing_body: Personal Data Protection Center (PDPC); Ministry of Communications and Information Technology
summary: Egypt's first comprehensive data protection law covers automated processing with provisions (Article 34) applicable to AI-driven decisions. The long-pending Executive Regulations were issued in late 2025 by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 816 of 2025, with a one-year grace period so full enforcement (PDPC licensing/permits, 72-hour breach notice) is expected around late 2026.

title: Privacy Act 2020 (New Zealand)
short_title: New Zealand Privacy Act 2020
issuing_body: Office of the Privacy Commissioner (OPC)
summary: New Zealand's principal privacy statute establishing 13 Information Privacy Principles applicable to collection, use, disclosure, and storage of personal data. No express automated decision or AI-specific provisions, but IPP 8 (data accuracy) and IPP 11 (disclosure limits) apply to AI systems. The Privacy Commissioner issued non-binding AI guidance in September 2023. Amended by the Privacy Amendment Act 2025 (royal assent 23 September 2025), which adds Information Privacy Principle 3A (notification of indirect collection), in force 1 May 2026; the Biometric Processing Privacy Code 2025 took effect 3 November 2025 (grace period to 3 August 2026).

title: Uruguay Decree No. 64/020 — Automated Individual Decision-Making
short_title: Uruguay Automated Decision Decree 2020
summary: Uruguay's regulation on automated individual decision-making, requiring meaningful human intervention for decisions significantly affecting individuals based solely on automated processing. Provides rights to human review, explanation of algorithmic logic, and DPIAs for high-risk automated processing. One of Latin America's most advanced AI-specific data protection rules.

title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy of the Republic of Cyprus
short_title: National AI Strategy (2020, action plan 2024)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Council of Ministers of Cyprus
summary: Approved in January 2020 and updated by an action plan in 2024, the strategy covers research, skills, data and infrastructure, public-sector and business adoption, and ethical, trustworthy AI aligned with the EU framework.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Rome Call for AI Ethics (Pontifical Academy for Life, 28 February 2020)
short_title: Rome Call for AI Ethics
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: Pontifical Academy for Life (RenAIssance Foundation)
summary: A declaration of six principles for the ethical development of AI (transparency, inclusion, responsibility, impartiality, reliability, security and privacy), first signed in February 2020 by the Pontifical Academy for Life, Microsoft, IBM, FAO and the Italian government, and since joined by other religious leaders, universities and companies. It calls for "algor-ethics" and human-centred design and is used as a reference in faith-based and corporate AI ethics commitments.
scope: Voluntary declaration for signatory organisations; no legal obligations.

title: Magyarország Mesterséges Intelligencia Stratégiája 2020–2030
short_title: AI Strategy 2020–2030
topics: General AI governance; Education; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of Hungary (Ministry for Innovation and Technology)
summary: Adopted in September 2020, the strategy sets goals to 2030 on data economy, AI research and education, public-sector and industrial adoption, and transformative programmes such as an AI-driven public administration and language technology, coordinated with the AI Coalition of companies, universities and public bodies.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Strategi Nasional Kecerdasan Artifisial Indonesia 2020-2045 (National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence)
short_title: Strategi Nasional Kecerdasan Artifisial Indonesia 2020-2045
issuing_body: Agency for the Assessment and Application of Technology (BPPT), now part of BRIN
summary: Indonesia's long-range national AI strategy, prepared by a BPPT-led multi-stakeholder working group. It covers ethics and policy, talent, infrastructure and data, research and industry innovation, and names five priority areas: health, bureaucratic reform, education and research, food security, and mobility and smart cities. It includes quick wins and a phased implementation roadmap through 2045.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by Agency for the Assessment and Application of Technology (BPPT), now part of BRIN. Oversight: BPPT-led working group (now BRIN) with ministries, universities and industry. Stated purpose: Direct AI development toward Indonesia's 2045 development goals across priority sectors.

title: Informatīvais ziņojums "Par mākslīgā intelekta risinājumu attīstību"
short_title: Informational report on AI development (2020)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Cabinet of Ministers of Latvia
summary: The 2020 informational report approved by the Cabinet sets Latvia's direction on AI: public-sector use cases, data availability, skills, research and ethical principles, later carried into the Digital Transformation Guidelines 2021–2027.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Algorithm Charter for Aotearoa New Zealand (2020)
short_title: Algorithm Charter for Aotearoa New Zealand
topics: Government use of AI; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: Stats NZ (Government Chief Data Steward) on behalf of signatory agencies
summary: Launched in July 2020, the charter commits signatory government agencies to transparency (plain-English explanations of how algorithms are used), partnership with Māori (Te Tiriti), people-focused use, data fit for purpose, privacy, ethics and human rights safeguards, human oversight and channels for challenge, applied through a risk matrix for high-impact algorithms. Around 30 agencies have signed; a 2021 review recommended stronger implementation.
scope: Voluntary for New Zealand government agencies that sign; applies to operational algorithms that affect people.

title: Nasjonal strategi for kunstig intelligens (National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence)
short_title: National Strategy for AI (2020)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Norwegian Ministry of Local Government and Modernisation
summary: Published in January 2020, the strategy sets ethical principles for AI in Norway based on the EU High-Level Expert Group guidelines, and measures on data access and sharing, language resources, research, skills, public-sector and business adoption, security and the Data Protection Authority's sandbox.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Polityka dla rozwoju sztucznej inteligencji w Polsce od roku 2020
short_title: Policy for the development of AI in Poland (2020)
topics: General AI governance; Education; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Council of Ministers of Poland
summary: Adopted by resolution of the Council of Ministers in December 2020, the policy sets goals for AI in society, business, science, education, international cooperation and the public sector, with short-, medium- and long-term actions and an ethics and trustworthy-AI dimension.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Federal Law No. 123-FZ of 24 April 2020 on an experiment to establish special regulation to create the conditions for the development and implementation of AI technologies in Moscow
short_title: Federal Law 123-FZ (Moscow AI experimental regime)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Federal Assembly of the Russian Federation
summary: Establishes a five-year experimental legal regime in Moscow (from 1 July 2020) allowing participants to develop and deploy AI technologies under special rules, including processing of anonymised personal data for AI purposes, coordinated by the Moscow government with a register of participants. It was accompanied by amendments to the personal-data law.
scope: Registered participants of the experiment in the city of Moscow.

title: Leitlinien "Künstliche Intelligenz" für den Bund
short_title: Guidelines on AI for the Federal Administration (2020)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Swiss Federal Council
summary: Adopted in November 2020, seven guidelines steer the use of AI by the federal administration: putting people at the centre, conditions for development and use, transparency and explainability, accountability, security, active participation in AI governance, and involvement of stakeholders.
scope: Applies to the federal administration of Switzerland when it develops, procures or uses AI systems; cantons and private organisations are not bound.

title: Tennessee S 2020 — Health and Accident Insurance
short_title: Tennessee S 2020 — Health and Accident Insurance
summary: Prohibits health insurance entities from downcoding reimbursement claims from healthcare professionals except in limited circumstances, makes certain other changes related to health insurance claim adjudication.

title: The Data Protection Act, No. 24 of 2019 (Cap 411C)
short_title: Kenya Data Protection Act 2019
issuing_body: Office of the Data Protection Commissioner (ODPC)
summary: Kenya's comprehensive data protection law establishes the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner (ODPC) with provisions on automated processing applicable to AI systems. The Act prohibits subjecting data subjects to automated processing decisions with legal effects without adequate safeguards and disclosure.

title: Directive on Automated Decision-Making
short_title: Canada Directive on Automated Decision-Making
issuing_body: Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat
summary: Canada's Treasury Board directive requires federal government institutions to assess and document the impact of automated decision systems before deploying them. Uses a tiered impact level system (I-IV) where higher-impact systems require peer review, algorithmic impact assessments, human review options, and explanations to affected parties. Level IV systems (highest impact) require ministerial approval. One of the first binding automated-decision governance rules for a national government.

title: Panama Law No. 81 on the Protection of Personal Data
short_title: Panama Data Protection Law 2019
summary: Panama's first comprehensive personal data protection law establishing APDATOS within AIG as the supervisory authority. Provides seven data protection principles, consent-based processing, sensitive data categories, ARCO data subject rights, mandatory database registration, cross-border transfer restrictions, security obligations, breach notification, and administrative fines up to USD 50,000.

title: Uganda Data Protection and Privacy Act 2019
short_title: Uganda Data Protection and Privacy Act 2019
summary: Uganda's primary data protection law implementing the constitutional right to privacy under Article 27. Establishes the Personal Data Protection Office under NITA-U, enshrines six data protection principles, provides data subject rights including access, correction, deletion, and objection, protects sensitive data categories including biometric and health data, and mandates breach notification.

title: Model AI Governance Framework (Second Edition) and Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI
short_title: Singapore Model AI Governance Framework
topics: General AI governance; Frontier / general-purpose AI
issuing_body: Infocomm Media Development Authority and Personal Data Protection Commission; AI Verify Foundation (generative AI edition)
summary: Singapore's Model AI Governance Framework is a voluntary, sector-agnostic guide for organisations deploying AI. The second edition (January 2020) covers four areas: internal governance structures and measures, determining the level of human involvement in AI-augmented decision-making, operations management (data, model development, monitoring), and stakeholder interaction and communication. The May 2024 Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI extends it with nine dimensions including accountability, data, trusted development and deployment, incident reporting, testing and assurance, security, content provenance, safety and alignment research, and AI for the public good.
scope: Voluntary; applicable to any organisation developing or deploying AI in Singapore or wishing to align with Singapore's expectations. It is referenced by the PDPC and IMDA and underpins the AI Verify testing framework.

title: National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence
short_title: National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence (2019)
topics: General AI governance; Health; Government use of AI; Frontier / general-purpose AI
issuing_body: Government of Denmark (Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Industry, Business and Financial Affairs)
summary: Published in March 2019, the strategy sets a responsible foundation for AI (ethical principles, data ethics council, legal clarity), more and better data, strong competences and new knowledge, and increased investment, with priority sectors of health, energy and utilities, agriculture and transport, and a set of public-sector pilot projects.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

jurisdiction: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
country: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
title: OECD Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (OECD/LEGAL/0449), adopted 22 May 2019 and revised 3 May 2024
short_title: OECD AI Principles (Recommendation on AI)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: OECD Council
summary: The first intergovernmental standard on AI. It sets five values-based principles (inclusive growth and well-being; human rights and democratic values including fairness and privacy; transparency and explainability; robustness, security and safety; accountability) and five recommendations to governments (invest in research, foster an inclusive AI ecosystem, enable an agile policy environment, build human capacity and prepare for labour-market transition, cooperate internationally). The 2024 revision updated the definition of an AI system (adopted by the EU AI Act and other laws) and added references to general-purpose and generative AI, misinformation and environmental sustainability. Adherents include all OECD members and several non-members; the G20 AI Principles (2019) draw on it.
scope: Addressed to governments (adherents) and, through them, to AI actors; non-binding.

title: Lithuanian Artificial Intelligence Strategy: A vision of the future
short_title: Lithuanian Artificial Intelligence Strategy (2019)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Ministry of the Economy and Innovation
summary: Published in 2019, the strategy sets a vision for AI in Lithuania across research, industry, public sector, skills and ethics, and proposes a coordination structure and funding measures.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Artificial Intelligence: a strategic vision for Luxembourg
short_title: AI: a strategic vision for Luxembourg (2019)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of Luxembourg (Ministry of Digitalisation)
summary: Published in May 2019, the vision positions Luxembourg as a living lab for applied AI with priorities on skills, data and infrastructure, public-sector use, research and trustworthy, human-centric AI.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy for Qatar 2019
short_title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy for Qatar 2019
topics: Employment & HR; Education; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (formerly Ministry of Transport and Communications)
summary: Developed by the Qatar Center for Artificial Intelligence and adopted by the government as the national strategy, the document sets out six pillars: education, data access, employment, business, research, and ethics. It provides recommendations for building an AI research and innovation ecosystem and for the responsible adoption of AI across society. A national AI committee was subsequently formed to develop an implementation plan.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (formerly Ministry of Transport and Communications). Oversight: National Artificial Intelligence Committee under MCIT oversees implementation planning. Stated purpose: Prepare Qatar for an 'AI+X' future in line with Qatar National Vision 2030.

title: UAE National AI Guide 2019 — Companion Guide to the UAE AI Strategy 2031
short_title: UAE National AI Guide 2019
issuing_body: Office of the Minister of State for Artificial Intelligence
summary: An educational companion guide to the UAE National AI Strategy 2031, published by the Office of the Minister of State for Artificial Intelligence as part of the National Program for Artificial Intelligence. Covers AI history, types (narrow/general/super AI), machine learning techniques (supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement learning), deep learning, and data science. Documents UAE AI deployments across healthcare, aviation, transport, finance, retail, media, energy, and government services. Introduces the UAE's governance framework (UAE AI and Blockchain Council, Data Committee, Cybersecurity and Risk Management Committee), references Smart Dubai's Ethical AI Toolkit (four domains: Ethics, Security, Humanity, Inclusiveness), addresses bias and employment impacts, and provides an AI adoption framework for organisations. Includes UAE AI education initiatives from K-12 to postgraduate level.

title: Serbia Law on Personal Data Protection — Provisions Applicable to AI (Law No. 87/2018, updated 2023)
short_title: Serbia Personal Data Protection Law (AI Applicability)
issuing_body: Commissioner for Information of Public Importance and Personal Data Protection (Serbia)
summary: Serbia's Law on Personal Data Protection (Law No. 87/2018), modelled closely on GDPR, provides the operative AI governance framework for Serbia pending specific AI legislation. It covers: data protection impact assessments for high-risk processing, right not to be subject to solely automated decisions, explicit consent for biometric data, and data subject access and rectification rights applicable to AI-processed data.

title: UAE Federal Decree-Law No. (25) of 2018 on Projects of Future Nature (Regulatory Sandbox for AI and Future Technologies)
short_title: UAE Federal Decree-Law 25 (Data Use)
issuing_body: UAE Cabinet
summary: A three-article UAE federal decree law authorising the Cabinet to grant interim licenses for innovative AI and future-technology projects where no existing legislation applies. The Cabinet may set conditions and procedures for such projects and may temporarily exempt them from federal legislation to the extent required for implementation. The stated purpose is to enable piloting of projects while preparing future legislation to regulate them — a formal regulatory sandbox mechanism at the federal level.

title: Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados Pessoais (LGPD), Lei nº 13.709/2018
short_title: Brazil LGPD (Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados)
issuing_body: Autoridade Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD)
summary: Brazil's comprehensive data protection law (LGPD) establishes GDPR-aligned rights and obligations applicable to all data processing including AI systems. Article 20 grants data subjects the right to review decisions made solely by automated means and to request disclosure of the criteria and procedures used. ANPD has been actively enforcing since 2021.

title: Bahrain Personal Data Protection Law 2018 (Law No. 30 of 2018)
short_title: Bahrain PDPL 2018
summary: Bahrain's PDPL was one of the first comprehensive data protection statutes in the GCC, establishing the Personal Data Protection Authority and a consent-based framework covering all organizations processing personal data in Bahrain or about Bahrain residents. Key provisions include sensitive data categories (health, genetic, biometric, racial, financial), data subject rights (access, correction, deletion, objection), cross-border transfer restrictions, mandatory breach notification, DPO requirements for large-scale or sensitive processing, and a licensing regime for high-risk processing activities. The PDPA issued a package of implementing ministerial resolutions on 17 March 2022 (DPO duties, technical/organizational measures, breach notification, sensitive-data processing, data-subject rights, and international transfers).

title: California Consumer Privacy Act / California Privacy Rights Act — Automated Decision-Making Technology Regulations
short_title: California CCPA/CPRA (AI provisions)
issuing_body: California Privacy Protection Agency; California Attorney General
summary: CCPA/CPRA grants Californians rights to opt out of automated decision-making technology (ADMT), request human review of significant AI decisions, and access data used in profiling. CPRA's 2023 ADMT regulations required by CPPA are among the most expansive in the US for limiting algorithmic profiling.

title: Algeria Law No. 18-07 on the Protection of Personal Data
short_title: Algeria Personal Data Protection Law 2018
summary: Algeria's comprehensive personal data protection law establishing the ANPDP as an independent supervisory authority. Provides lawful processing bases, extensive sensitive data categories (health, genetic, biometric, political, religious, criminal), data subject rights, mandatory registration and authorization requirements, cross-border transfer restrictions, and criminal penalties. Amended and completed by Law No. 25-11 of 24 July 2025 (JORADP No. 48), which strengthened the regime with a mandatory DPO, processing register/audit log, a 5-day breach notification window, and stronger administrative penalties, and reaffirmed the ANPDP.

title: National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence (#AIforAll)
short_title: National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence
issuing_body: NITI Aayog
summary: A discussion paper that set out India's first national approach to artificial intelligence. It prioritises five sectors (healthcare, agriculture, education, smart cities and infrastructure, and smart mobility) and proposes research institutions, data ecosystems and skilling measures to support adoption. It also flags privacy, fairness and explainability as issues needing attention and recommends institutional structures for responsible AI.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by NITI Aayog. Oversight: NITI Aayog (policy think tank of the Government of India). Stated purpose: Position India as an AI leader while using AI for inclusive social and economic growth.

title: Stratégie nationale pour l'intelligence artificielle (National AI Strategy, phases 1–3, 2018–2025)
short_title: National AI strategy
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of France (Ministry of the Economy, SGPI)
summary: Launched in March 2018 following the Villani report, the national AI strategy funds research institutes (3IA then AI clusters), talent, compute and business adoption. The second phase (2021) focused on training and diffusion into the economy; the third phase (2024–2025) emphasises sovereign generative-AI models, compute and public-sector use, and framed France's hosting of the AI Action Summit in February 2025.
scope: Government investment and coordination programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Strategie Künstliche Intelligenz der Bundesregierung (AI Strategy of the Federal Government, 2018, updated 2020)
short_title: AI Strategy of the Federal Government
topics: General AI governance; Health; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Federal Government of Germany (BMBF, BMWK, BMAS)
summary: The federal AI strategy, adopted in November 2018 and updated in December 2020, sets out how Germany intends to make AI research, transfer and use competitive while anchoring AI in fundamental rights and the common good. The 2020 update raised planned federal funding to around EUR 5 billion to 2025 and added priorities on pandemic response, sustainability, health, mobility and AI in the public sector. It commits to a European approach to AI regulation and to trustworthy-AI standards.
scope: Applies to federal government action: research funding, transfer programmes, skills, infrastructure and public-sector use. It creates no obligations for private organisations.

title: Mauritius Artificial Intelligence Strategy
short_title: Mauritius AI Strategy (2018)
topics: General AI governance; Health; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Government of Mauritius (Ministry of Technology, Communication and Innovation)
summary: Published in November 2018, the strategy identifies AI applications in manufacturing, health, fintech, agriculture, ocean economy and public services, proposes a Mauritius AI Council, skills programmes and data policies, and addresses ethics and regulation.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: UAE National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence 2031
short_title: UAE AI Strategy 2031
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: UAE Government, Office of the Minister of State for Artificial Intelligence
summary: The UAE National Strategy for AI 2031 aims to position the UAE as a global leader in AI by 2031. It sets objectives across priority sectors, AI talent and research, data and infrastructure, government adoption and governance, including a commitment to AI ethics and to developing appropriate regulation. It is a strategy document that guides government programmes and does not itself impose obligations on private organisations.
scope: UAE federal government entities and national programmes; indirectly the private sector and research institutions participating in national AI initiatives.

title: Pan-Canadian Artificial Intelligence Strategy
short_title: Pan-Canadian Artificial Intelligence Strategy
issuing_body: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
summary: The Pan-Canadian AI Strategy is Canada's national AI strategy, first funded in Budget 2017 with $125 million and delivered largely through CIFAR and three national AI institutes. A second phase from 2021 added funding for commercialisation, standards and computing capacity, with further support in the 2024 Fall Economic Statement. It focuses on attracting and retaining researchers, translating research into industry adoption and promoting responsible AI.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada. Oversight: ISED oversees; CIFAR delivers research and talent pillars with Amii, Mila and the Vector Institute. Stated purpose: Build Canadian AI research capacity, talent and commercialisation.

title: Finland's Age of Artificial Intelligence: Turning Finland into a leading country in the application of AI (objective and recommendations for measures)
short_title: Finland's Age of Artificial Intelligence (2017)
topics: General AI governance; Government use of AI
issuing_body: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment of Finland
summary: The 2017 report of the steering group appointed by the Minister of Economic Affairs proposed eight key actions to make Finland a leader in applying AI: enhancing business competitiveness, using data in all sectors, faster adoption, top-level expertise and talent, bold decisions and investments, the best public services, new cooperation models and a human-centred approach. It launched the national AI programme continued in the 2019 final report and the AI 4.0 programme.
scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Law No. 13 of 2016 on the Protection of Personal Data Privacy
short_title: Qatar Personal Data Privacy Protection Law
issuing_body: National Cyber Security Agency (NCSA); Ministry of Interior
summary: Qatar's personal data protection law establishing rights and obligations for personal data processing. Applied to AI systems through NCSA guidance. Requires consent for processing personal data, provides access and rectification rights, and classifies sensitive data (health, biometric, financial) with heightened protections. Penalties include both fines and imprisonment for serious violations.

title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 — General Data Protection Regulation (Automated Decision-Making Provisions)
short_title: GDPR (Article 22)
topics: General AI governance; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: National Data Protection Authorities; European Data Protection Board
summary: Article 22 GDPR grants individuals the right not to be subject to solely automated decisions (including profiling) that produce legal or similarly significant effects. Requires human intervention, explanation, and contestation rights when exceptions apply. First major binding regulation of AI decision-making globally.

title: Kişisel Verilerin Korunması Kanunu (Law on Protection of Personal Data No. 6698), as amended by Law No. 7499/2024
short_title: Turkey KVKK (Law No. 6698, as amended 2024)
issuing_body: Personal Data Protection Authority (Kişisel Verileri Koruma Kurumu — KVKK)
summary: Turkey's GDPR-like personal data protection law (KVKK), significantly amended in 2024 to align cross-border data transfer rules with GDPR adequacy mechanisms. Data subjects have the right to object to solely automated processing affecting their rights. No standalone Turkish AI law enacted; multiple AI bills (June 2024, and further bills November and December 2025) remain in committee.

title: Dominican Republic Law No. 172-13 on the Protection of Personal Data
short_title: Dominican Republic Data Protection Law 2013
summary: Dominican Republic's primary data protection law covering personal data in public and private databases. INDOTEL serves as supervisory authority. Provides data subject ARCO rights, habeas data judicial remedy, lawful processing requirements, mandatory database registration, sensitive data protections, and criminal penalties up to 2 years imprisonment. Particular focus on credit bureau and financial data.

title: Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013 (POPIA)
short_title: South Africa POPIA
issuing_body: Information Regulator of South Africa
summary: South Africa's POPIA establishes 8 conditions for lawful personal data processing and has been fully enforced since July 2021. Section 71 explicitly addresses automated decision-making, granting data subjects rights to request human review of decisions based solely on automated processing. The Information Regulator has issued enforcement notices and fines. The POPIA Amendment Regulations 2025 (GG 52523) expanded data-subject request channels; in April 2025 the Information Regulator announced work on ethical AI / automated decision-making guidance, though no binding AI-specific POPIA amendment exists as of mid-2026. A verified official copy of the Act is also hosted by the National Treasury (treasury.gov.za/POPIA/).

title: Côte d'Ivoire Law No. 2013-450 on the Protection of Personal Data
short_title: Ivory Coast Personal Data Protection Law 2013
summary: Côte d'Ivoire's comprehensive personal data protection law designating ARTCI as the supervisory body for data protection in addition to its telecommunications regulatory role. Provides data protection principles, lawful processing bases, special category data protections, mandatory ARTCI declaration, data subject rights, cross-border transfer restrictions, and criminal penalties.

title: Ley Estatutaria 1581 de 2012 — Proteccion de Datos Personales
short_title: Colombia Personal Data Protection Law
issuing_body: Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC)
summary: Colombia's foundational data protection law establishing rights and obligations for personal data processing. Applied to AI systems by the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) through regulatory guidance on algorithmic systems and automated profiling. Requires consent for personal data processing, provides access and rectification rights, and protects sensitive categories including biometric data. The SIC has issued specific guidance on AI systems under this law.

title: Data Privacy Act of 2012 (Republic Act No. 10173)
short_title: Philippines Data Privacy Act 2012
issuing_body: National Privacy Commission (NPC)
summary: The Philippines' comprehensive data protection law prohibits solely automated decisions with legal effects without legal authorization or data subject consent (Section 21). The NPC issued Advisory No. 2024-04 explicitly applying DPA principles to the full AI lifecycle. No AI-specific enacted law exists in the Philippines; the DPA is the primary binding framework.

title: Ghana Data Protection Act 2012 (Act 843)
short_title: Ghana Data Protection Act 2012
summary: Ghana's primary data protection law and one of sub-Saharan Africa's earliest comprehensive data protection frameworks. Establishes the Data Protection Commission, mandates registration of data controllers and processors, enshrines eight data protection principles, provides data subject rights including access and correction, and protects sensitive data categories including health, financial, and biometric data. A Data Protection Bill, 2025 that would repeal and replace Act 843 (renaming the Commission an Authority, 72-hour breach notice, higher penalties, and automated-decision provisions) was in draft/public consultation and not yet introduced in Parliament as of 2026; Act 843 remains in force. Note: recorded enacted_date reflects the 10 May 2012 date of assent (gazette notification 18 May 2012); the 16 October 2012 commencement date is per secondary sources and unverified against the official gazette.

jurisdiction: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
title: APEC Cross-Border Privacy Rules (CBPR) System
short_title: APEC Cross-Border Privacy Rules System
summary: APEC's voluntary certification framework enabling free personal data flows between participating economies (US, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Canada, Mexico, Philippines, Chinese Taipei, Australia). Organizations certified against APEC Privacy Framework principles by accredited Accountability Agents can transfer data across participating economies. In 2022 the Global CBPR Forum was established to expand the system beyond APEC. Increasingly relevant for AI training data flows in Asia-Pacific.

title: Costa Rica Law No. 8968 — Protection of Personal Data
short_title: Costa Rica Data Protection Law 2011
summary: Costa Rica's primary data protection law and Central America's most developed data protection framework. Establishes PRODHAB as a powerful independent agency. Provides ARCO rights, lawful processing bases, sensitive data categories, habeas data judicial remedy, mandatory database registration, cross-border transfer restrictions, and significant administrative fines up to CRC 172 million.

title: Tennessee S 2010 — Health and Accident Insurance
short_title: Tennessee S 2010 — Health and Accident Insurance
summary: Creates the Regulate Artificial Intelligence (AI) In Health Care Act.

title: Illinois Biometric Information Privacy Act
short_title: Illinois BIPA
topics: General AI governance; Data protection & privacy
issuing_body: Illinois courts (private right of action)
summary: Requires private entities collecting biometric identifiers (fingerprints, retinal scans, facial geometry, voiceprints) to obtain written consent, establish retention policies, and prohibits selling biometric data. Provides private right of action with statutory damages per violation. Highly relevant to AI facial recognition and voice AI systems.

title: Uruguay Law No. 18.331 — Protection of Personal Data and Habeas Data Action
short_title: Uruguay Data Protection Law 2008
summary: Uruguay's primary data protection law and the first outside Europe to receive EU adequacy recognition (2012). Establishes the URCDP as supervisory authority, provides seven data protection principles, ARCO rights (access, rectification, cancellation, opposition), habeas data judicial action, mandatory database registration, sensitive data categories, and cross-border transfer restrictions.

title: Senegal Law No. 2008-12 on the Protection of Personal Data
short_title: Senegal Personal Data Protection Law 2008
summary: One of West Africa's earliest and most comprehensive personal data protection laws. Establishes the CDP as an independent supervisory authority and serves as an ECOWAS reference framework. Provides five data protection principles, mandatory CDP declaration or authorization, sensitive data categories, data subject rights (information, access, rectification, opposition), cross-border transfer restrictions, and criminal penalties.

jurisdiction: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
country: International organisations (OECD, UNESCO, UN, G7, ISO)
title: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 Information technology – Artificial intelligence – Management system
short_title: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 AI management system
issuing_body: ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 42
summary: The first certifiable management-system standard for AI. It specifies requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining and improving an AI management system within an organisation: context and leadership, AI policy, risk and impact assessment, objectives, resources and competence, operational controls across the AI lifecycle, performance evaluation and improvement, with Annex A controls on data, transparency, human oversight, third parties and responsible use. Certification is voluntary but increasingly requested in procurement; regulators reference it as evidence of governance.
scope: Voluntary; any organisation developing, providing or using AI systems. This site does not reproduce the standard's text.

title: Tennessee S 1999 — Energy
short_title: Tennessee S 1999 — Energy
summary: Enacts the Data Center, Artificial Intelligence, and Clean Transition Tariff Accountability Act.

title: Tennessee S 1998 — Consumer Protection
short_title: Tennessee S 1998 — Consumer Protection
summary: Requires certain food retail establishments to use a nondigital presentation of price, prohibits a food retail establishment from using personalized algorithmic pricing, makes other changes related to food retail establishments.

title: Tennessee S 1990 — Trade Regulation
short_title: Tennessee S 1990 — Trade Regulation
summary: Enacts the Stop Rent Rigging Act.

title: Texas S 1960 — Digital Replication Rights
short_title: Texas S 1960 — Digital Replication Rights
topics: Deepfakes & synthetic media; Consumer protection; Law enforcement & justice
summary: Relates to digital replication rights in the voice and visual likeness of individuals, provides private causes of action, authorizes a fee.

title: Tennessee H 1951 — Criminal Offenses
short_title: Tennessee H 1951 — Criminal Offenses
summary: Creates a new offense of coercive suicide, specifies that a person or entity commits the offense of coercive suicide if such person or entity owns an artificial intelligence system and the artificial intelligence system advises or encourages a person to commit or attempt to commit suicide.

title: Tennessee H 1946 — Consumer Protection
short_title: Tennessee H 1946 — Consumer Protection
summary: Enacts the Curbing Harmful AI Technology (CHAT) Act.

title: Alabama S 129 — Artificial Intelligence
short_title: Alabama S 129 — Artificial Intelligence
summary: Relates to artificial intelligence, relates to disclosure of artificial intelligence-generated content required, enforcement provided.

title: Alabama S 141 — Education Trust Fund
short_title: Alabama S 141 — Education Trust Fund
summary: Relates to Regular Session Education Trust Fund.

title: Alabama H 280 — Rural Health
short_title: Alabama H 280 — Rural Health
topics: General AI governance; Health; Consumer protection
summary: Relates to Rural health care, states health command established to designate an artificial intelligence assisted health platform in rural communities.

title: Alabama H 291 — Crimes and Offenses
short_title: Alabama H 291 — Crimes and Offenses
summary: Relates to crimes and offenses, relates to crime of distribution of materially deceptive media established, permanent injunctive relief authorized.

title: Alabama H 324 — Consumer Protection

title: The National Guidelines on AI Governance & Ethics (AIGE)
short_title: The National Guidelines on AI Governance & Ethics
issuing_body: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MOSTI)
summary: Voluntary national guidelines that set out seven principles for responsible AI: fairness; reliability, safety and control; privacy and security; inclusiveness; transparency; accountability; and human-centricity. They give tailored guidance to end users, policymakers and AI developers and are meant to build public trust and reduce ethical risks while supporting adoption.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MOSTI). Oversight: MOSTI (guidelines are voluntary). Stated purpose: Promote trustworthy, human-centred AI through shared principles for users, policymakers and developers.

title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Governance Bill (proposed)
short_title: Artificial Intelligence
issuing_body: Ministry of Digital / National AI Office (NAIO)
summary: A proposed horizontal AI law announced for stakeholder engagement and public consultation by the Ministry of Digital through the National AI Office. It takes a risk-based approach across the AI lifecycle, assigns responsibilities according to actors' roles, and is intended to complement existing laws rather than regulate AI outputs directly. It encourages incident reporting, safeguards and sandboxes, and the government aims to table it in Parliament.
scope: Scope is as set out in the official text linked below. Issued by Ministry of Digital / National AI Office (NAIO). Oversight: National AI Office under the Ministry of Digital. Stated purpose: Create Malaysia's first horizontal, risk-based statutory framework for AI.

scope: Government programme; no obligations on private organisations.

title: Maryland SB 936 — Artificial Intelligence — Consumer Protections (failed)
short_title: Maryland SB 936 (High-Risk AI Consumer Protection)
summary: Maryland SB 936 (2025), with House companion HB 1331, would have required developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems to use reasonable care to protect consumers from algorithmic discrimination. Developers would have been required to document intended uses, limitations, and risks; deployers would have been required to implement risk management policies, conduct pre-deployment impact assessments, and notify consumers when high-risk AI is used in consequential decisions affecting them. The Attorney General would have enforced the act. Both bills died in committee during the 2025 regular session without reaching a floor vote. Note: sometimes cited in secondary sources under the bill numbers SB 1050/HB 1457, which do not correspond to AI legislation in the 2025 Maryland session.

issuing_body: Information Commissioner's Office

scope: Any controller or processor using personal data in AI systems in the UK, at any lifecycle stage. It does not apply to AI that processes no personal data.
